docs.title: 2026-09-24-0554-YUMC
docs.html:
model: gpt-6-astra, lane: deepdive, 2026-09-24 05:49, 15m29s, 5,119,550 tokens (220,977 fresh, 4,873,216 cached, 25,357 out), stamped from the session log rather than self-reported

YUMC — Yum China

What it does: Yum China operates and franchises restaurants in China, principally KFC and Pizza Hut. It earns restaurant sales and fees from franchisees.

This run's ranking and cash allocation.

1. Order

BUY 2 shares of YUMC on NYSE, limit @ USD 41.00, regular session only, day order for 24 September 2026. Use Trading 212 Invest/Stocks ISA, which lists this ordinary common stock; it is not an ADR.

Allocate £63.25 of the pot's £90.15 cash to this ticket after reserving £26.90 for EXPN.L. At the local USD-per-GBP rate 1.3241, the limit deploys £61.93, plus £0.093 FX. This leaves £1.23 after both tickets, or £1.09 allowing Experian's £0.135 tax contingency. At the snapshot price of $40.85, this ticket instead deploys £61.70. Cash and FX are from positions and prices.

Commission £0, custody £0, entry FX 0.15%, transaction tax £0 expected, ADR charge £0. Dividend conversion is free at Trading 212, so expected first-year brokerage/custody costs are 0.15% of the ticket. Separately, assuming UK treaty eligibility and a valid W-8BEN, US dividend withholding is 15% of distributions: about 0.32% of capital at the local 2.13% trailing yield, or roughly 0.47% including entry fees. Even the unreduced 30% withholding case would total about 0.79%; future yield is not promised (broker explanation of US withholding). A future sale is excluded. Both §4.1a and §4.1 pass under the Trading 212 schedule; dividend tax is not a broker fee.

The order is 12.39% of £500 contributed capital, below the £250 cap. No whole-share or fee exception is used. A third share would exceed available cash even without Experian. No Rule 4 halving: brand-level price/traffic and margin observations arrive within two quarters. The modest current EPS disagreement is disclosed below and does not materially change this ticket's valuation. Use a maximum £62.10 including entry fees if execution FX moves; do not chase above the dollar limit. Leo executes; this file places no order.

2. Thesis

Restaurant expansion can compound the existing cash-generating network, rather than depending on a general Chinese consumption rebound. The acquisition of Pizza Hut's mainland rights has now closed, creating a specific operating change whose financing cost and return can be tested (completion filing). My inference is that the market underweights the combination of cash-funded reinvestment and brand ownership; whether discounting and delivery competition consume those benefits is the test, not an assumed moat.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At Q3 results, locally estimated 4 November, read by 6 November 2026, re-read if either brand has negative same-store sales with positive same-store transactions, or restaurant margin falls 100bp year on year. Q2 KFC/Pizza Hut restaurant margins were 17.1%/12.9%; use the corresponding prior-year quarter when testing Q3, not these seasonally different Q2 figures (release).

For Pizza Hut, remove only the royalty saving actually disclosed for the measured period before comparing margins. The issuer expects a 2.8 percentage-point steady-state brand benefit, but Q3 is a partial period; do not substitute that expectation for a realised bridge (transcript, page 7). No bridge means unresolved and triggers a re-read.

Outside Yum, check Meituan Core Local Commerce margin and subsidy commentary at its next quarterly filing, no later than 1 December 2026. Q2 margin was 7.9%; below 5% accompanied by renewed subsidy spending warns of platform pressure. This is a competition proxy, not Yum market share (Meituan, page 13).

Break: By 1 March 2027, propose sale under §5.1 if the same brand has two consecutive post-entry quarters of negative same-store sales, positive transactions and at least 100bp comparable margin contraction in each; a single 300bp contraction independently breaks the case. Apply the actual royalty bridge. Non-positive FY2026 operating cash less capital spending is a separate break. These are this proposal's thresholds, not company guidance. Missing disclosure remains unresolved, never a pass.

4. Review date

6 November 2026, regardless of price. External competition review by 1 December; two-quarter assessment by 1 March 2027.

5. Numbers as of today

Snapshot: 24 September 05:49:42 UTC; YUMC's regular mark is 23 September 20:00:02 UTC, not today's trading or an extended-hours print.

Local check: disagreements disclosed. Q2 issuer operating profit is $348m, versus local $360m; use $348m and 11.1% for current operating performance. Revenue $3.138bn and EPS $0.70 agree. Local quarter EPS totals $2.73, agreeing with researchEps but not the $2.68 headline. Use the $2.73 company-adjusted current denominator; it retains investment marks. Reported and vendor distributions remain separate references. The oneOff flag compares the research multiple to a vendor floor; it does not certify an adjusted historical percentile. There is no denominatorDrift flag.

The annual discrepancy also matters: FY2025 issuer operating profit is $1.290bn, versus local $1.326bn; issuer margin is 10.9%, versus the vendor-derived 11.24%. FY2024 issuer margin was 10.3%. Use those issuer margins to assess the business, and treat the local capital ratio as a screening proxy (FY2025 release). The difference does not reverse the improving-margin direction.

Adjustments: Existing normalizedEps.YUMC already records Q3/Q4 2025 and H1 2026, plus two annual values; the FY2024 $0.08 gain is the only cited annual one-off deduction. Rechecked H1 $1.57 and Q2 $0.70, already stored, so no duplicate appended. No newly quantified income-to-remove was established. Neither two annual values nor this TTM certify five years of adjusted history.

Why this is not 7532.T again: the case rests on store economics and operating cash, and explicitly tests falling customer spend against traffic. It assumes neither a tourist rebound nor currency gains; the USD listing still carries underlying RMB exposure.

6. The case against

Theses: none.

Dominant risk (competitive): delivery-platform competition and discounting can buy transactions while destroying the profit per restaurant.

Earliest observable: Q3 brand same-store sales, transactions and comparable restaurant margins, estimated 4 November; Meituan's next quarterly margin and incentive disclosure, checked by 1 December. P3 can fail while openings and repurchases still lift group EPS.

The acquisition cost $1.2bn and adds financing risk; ownership does not itself prove an adequate return. Lower average tickets already make traffic an incomplete measure of demand. H1 cash generation is not a promise that capital returns and acquisition financing can both continue indefinitely.

Combined exposure: no YUMC holding appears in holdings, so current direct human-book weight is 0%. The order adds China consumer exposure to a book already 6.83% China and 14.01% Consumer Cyclical, per signals; those percentages have different denominators from the pot and must not be added to its 12.39%.

TW's direct issuer EPS gives 26.45x versus 23.81x reported. EXPN's vendor and reported figures agree closely, but its annual Benchmark base remains separate. denominatorDrift: NKE, WLY and ADUS are flagged; their cash percentiles are shown above. GOOG is flagged in the non-watchlist table. These discrepancies can arise from one-offs, acquisition accounting or working capital; this screen does not invent a single cause. None is proposed on reported cheapness alone. For cash-only names, operating cash is not free cash flow: financing flows, advance receipts and asset investment require business-specific checks.

Shortlist findings that affected the choice

  • YUMC: the issuer FY2025 operating profit is $1.290bn, not local $1.326bn; issuer margin 10.9%, not local 11.24%. Q2 has the same direction of difference. Use issuer operating economics for P3 and label local ROIC a proxy. The case still has a growing operating business; it is not an unqualified margin-screen pass. FY2025 release.
  • EXPN: current growth is not evidence that bypass cannot happen. The actual observed distribution risk is potential FICO reseller reach, not actual replacement of bureau reports. One share, a monthly external check and half-sizing reflect that distinction. The proposal reconciles issuer annual EPS and local quote units.
  • RSGN: H1 sales fell 13.1%, orders 11.4%, while backlog rose 17.1%; free cash flow CHF11.5m improved. EXPN.L — Experian

What it does: Experian supplies credit data, identity and fraud checks, and decision tools to lenders and other businesses. It also runs consumer credit and financial-product services.

This run's ranking and cash allocation.

1. Order

BUY 1 share of EXPN.L on the London Stock Exchange, limit @ 2,690 GBp (£26.90), through Trading 212 Invest/Stocks ISA, regular session, day order for 24 September 2026. The broker lists EXPN.

The maximum otherwise available allocation is £90.15, below the £250 contributed-capital cap. Apply Rule 4 and §7.2a once, not twice: the uncertain distribution economics and incomplete adjusted history warrant a £45.075 half-allocation. One whole share deploys £26.90, leaving £18.175 of that allocation undeployed. Reassign that unused cash to the separately researched YUMC ticket; it does not permit a second Experian share.

Commission £0, purchase FX £0 on this GBP line, custody £0, ADR charge £0: 0% entry broker fees. Transaction tax expected £0, inferred from Experian's Jersey incorporation and Jersey share register (issuer FAQ) against HMRC's UK-register rule. Retain £0.135, or 0.5%, as a tax contingency if the broker treats the ticket differently. It is a reserve, not an assertion that tax is payable.

Dividend conversion is free at Trading 212. Expected first-year brokerage/custody costs are 0%, or 0.5% including the transaction-tax contingency; both fee gates pass under the broker schedule. A future disposal and personal income tax outside an ISA are excluded.

Concentration is 5.38% of £500 contributions, with no exception. Combined with two YUMC at their limit and FX charge, expected cash is £1.23, or £1.09 after the tax reserve. Neither a cheaper fill nor an unfilled YUMC ticket authorises more Experian. Leo executes; no order is placed here.

2. Thesis

Experian's existing data and decision businesses are growing organically, and the local annual series shows improving operating returns rather than earnings growth solely from repurchases. A reported multiple of 22.00x versus a 36.40x historical median is a 39.6% de-rating: my interpretation is that the market discounts loss of paid distribution and decision economics as alternatives spread, not merely a weak credit quarter. I judge that discount too broad for a small position because Q1 growth spans B2B and multiple regions; that is evidence against a collapse already underway, not proof that T2 cannot arrive, so future paid volumes and fee losses must decide the case (Q1 update).

3. Falsifier

Warning: Active at entry as an exposure warning: FICO says direct-licence partners cover 73.1% of mortgage reseller volume, above this proposal's 70% warning threshold. That is potential reach, not use or lost Experian revenue. At 23 October 2026, and monthly thereafter, re-read FICO's programme and partner announcements for commercial launch, production volume or direct evidence of a lender replacing a paid Experian service (FICO announcement).

At Experian's 18 November H1 results, warn if a disclosed comparable paid-data/decision volume or net unit price falls more than 5% year on year because of substitution, even if aggregate revenue grows. If these measures remain absent, the dominant risk is still unobservable and the position stays small; revenue guidance is not a substitute test.

Break: At any subsequent disclosure, and reviewed no later than 31 May 2027, propose sale under §5.1 if identified lost annualised revenue from direct licensing, report replacement or platform bypass reaches 5% of FY2026 revenue ($422m) without an offsetting recurring stream; or if comparable paid volumes/net unit prices decline more than 10% in two consecutive observations from that cause. Independently, non-positive FY2027 operating cash after intangibles, equipment and lease principal breaks the cash-generation case. These are analyst thresholds. Lack of disclosure is unresolved, not a break or a pass.

4. Review date

23 October 2026 for external distribution evidence, 18 November 2026 for H1 results, and 31 May 2027 as the full-year backstop. External publications are event-driven; these review dates do not promise publication.

5. Numbers as of today

Local check: Annual revenue and operating profit agree with the issuer. Local FY2026 annual EPS is missing; the quote's 122p implies $1.6154, slightly below the issuer's $1.634 annual diluted EPS. Keep the local 22x reported screen and use separately labelled annual issuer multiples for the economic check. Neither the Benchmark annual P/E nor a current FX translation inherits the local historical percentile. No denominatorDrift flag: both local distributions clear the decile.

Adjustments: normalizedEps.EXPN.L already stores the two FY2025/26 Benchmark diluted annual values ($1.555/$1.787), with zero contiguous interim periods and no research TTM. Existing FY2026 $101m financing, $9m disposal and $2m contingent-consideration gains are gross evidence only, not deductions. The issuer figures were rechecked; no duplicate or newly certified after-tax adjustment was appended. Two annual adjusted observations do not establish five years of comparable history.

Why this is not 7532.T again: the case is tied to operating margin, returns on capital and cash after software/database investment, not an AI launch story. The GBP trading line reports in USD and earns across currencies; a GBP quote does not remove currency risk.

6. The case against

Theses: T2, agents and alternate underwriting may bypass paid decision workflows; T3, identity and audit data may support demand but no separate agent revenue is certified; T1, cheaper models can aid competitors as well as Experian.

Dominant risk (competitive): lenders and intermediaries bypass Experian's paid distribution or decision services, reducing fees before headline revenue reveals the damage.

Earliest observable: FICO's launch/usage announcements, checked monthly, then any Experian unit-price, volume or revenue-loss disclosure at H1. These are not guaranteed series, so the main risk has no reliably dated complete measure: Rule 4 halves the allocation.

Direct FICO scoring is not replacement of the underlying bureau data. Equally, continuing data demand does not protect a distributor's mark-up. Margin growth can initially hide loss of units through pricing and product mix. The near-40% historical de-rating could be rational if those economics deteriorate; P3 must test that possibility, not dismiss it.

Combined exposure: no EXPN.L holding appears in holdings, so direct human-book weight is 0%. Its North American business adds economic overlap to a book already 67.32% US and 59.93% Technology plus Communication Services (signals); a London listing is not geographic diversification by itself.

What it does: Yum China operates and franchises restaurants in mainland China, mainly KFC and Pizza Hut. Most of its revenue is food sold in its own restaurants, both in-store and through delivery. The rest comes from franchise fees and from supplying franchisees.

This run's ranking, cash and the other proposal are in the run report.

1. Order

BUY 2 shares of YUMC on the NYSE, DAY limit USD 41.00, for the 23 September regular session. If it is unfilled, the order lapses. Take a fresh quote before placing another. Currency USD, funded from GBP.

Broker: Trading 212, which lists YUMC (instrument page). Commission is £0 and the FX fee is 0.15% (Trading 212 FX fee). There is no stamp duty on a US-listed share, and no ADR fee, because this is common stock. Broker fees come to 0.15% of the ticket, inside §4.1a's 0.5%. First-year costs are also 0.15%, inside §4.1's 2%. A third share would take the debit to £93.02, more than the pot's cash.

Full size, not half. I considered both halving rules and neither applies:

  • §7.2a. This morning's run halved because only the reported basis was in the decile. Since then the price has fallen further. The vendor-recurring and the repo's own adjusted percentiles are now both 9.6%, and the company-adjusted TTM EPS equals reported EPS ($2.73). So the bases no longer disagree about whether the stock is cheap.
  • Rule 4. The dominant risk is observable at Q3, which is locally estimated for 4 November. That is inside two quarters.

This position is 12.4% of contributed capital, well inside §4.2.

2. Thesis

Yum China is a restaurant operator whose existing network pays for its own expansion: in H1 2026 it produced $705m of operating cash after capital spending, and its filed FY2025 operating margin rose to 10.94% from 10.28% while revenue grew 4.4%. The shares have fallen 17% in a month (from $49.52 to $40.81, local closes) with no filing, guidance change or results to explain it. That fall reflects the market's worry about lower average tickets and higher delivery costs across the whole system. What the market may be under-weighting is that this is a cash-generating operator returning capital at a mid-teens multiple, not a growth story that needs a Chinese consumer recovery to work. Whether discounting is eroding the economics of each restaurant is not assumed away here; it is what P3 tests.

3. Falsifier

The thresholds below are my decision rules, not management guidance.

Warning: At Q3 results (locally estimated 4 November 2026, read by 6 November), a warning fires if either:

  • Brand demand: KFC or Pizza Hut reports negative same-store sales while its same-store transactions are still positive. That would mean traffic is being bought with price.
  • Brand margin: either brand's restaurant margin falls 100bp or more year on year. The Q2 baselines are KFC 17.1% and Pizza Hut 12.9%. For Pizza Hut, first remove the royalty saving the company actually discloses for the post-purchase period. Management expects a 2.8-point steady-state benefit, so an unadjusted flat margin could hide deterioration. If the company gives no bridge, the test is unresolved and still triggers a re-read.

Outside the company, check Meituan's next quarterly filing by 1 December 2026. A warning fires if its Core Local Commerce operating margin is below 5% (Q2 baseline 7.9%) and the filing attributes the fall to renewed subsidies or incentives. This measures delivery-platform price competition, not Yum's share.

Break: By 1 March 2027, propose a sale under §5.1 in any of three cases:

  • Two quarters: the same brand reports two consecutive post-entry quarters with negative same-store sales, positive transactions and a restaurant-margin fall of at least 100bp in each.
  • One quarter: a single quarter with a 300bp margin fall.
  • Cash: FY2026 operating cash less capital spending is zero or negative.

All three can trip while openings and buybacks still lift group EPS.

4. Review date

6 November 2026, regardless of price. Then 1 December 2026 for the Meituan check, and 1 March 2027 for the two-quarter conclusion.

Local check: partly disagree. Revenue, net income ($929m) and EPS reconcile with the issuer. Local operating income is $1.326bn against the filed $1.290bn for FY2025, because Yahoo's field is on a different basis. I use the issuer's figure for margins and P3, and keep the local capital ratios only as a labelled screening proxy.

Adjustments: Nothing new was writable. The existing entries already cover this name: the FY2024 $0.08 per share investment gain, and the company-adjusted EPS for Q3 2025, Q4 2025 and H1 2026. I found no new one-off in this run. Company-adjusted EPS equals GAAP EPS and still includes investment marks, so it is not "one-off-free" earnings.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: 7532.T was a tourism story bought after the rebound, without the fundamentals. Here nothing is paid for a recovery. The case rests on filed operating profit, cash after capex and a stated ROIC. The falsifier tests per-restaurant economics directly rather than headline growth. The currency risk is stated, not assumed away: earnings are in RMB, the listing is in USD, and Leo's money is in GBP.

6. The case against

Theses: none. Yum sells food, not seats, models or compliance. No entry in theses.md bears on it.

Dominant risk (competitive): Price and delivery competition, much of it funded by the platforms, erode each restaurant's economics. Lower tickets and higher delivery costs could do this while openings, royalty savings and buybacks keep group EPS rising.

Earliest observable: At Q3 results (locally estimated 4 November): each brand's same-store sales against its transactions, and its restaurant margin after the disclosed royalty saving. Outside the company, Meituan's quarterly filing by 1 December. Both are within two quarters, so Rule 4 does not halve the order.

Secondary arguments, stated to persuade:

  • Growth is slow. Revenue grew 4.4% in FY2025. Leo's filter wants growth as well as value, and a mid-single-digit grower at 15x is fair rather than cheap unless margins keep rising.
  • The recent fall is unexplained, and that is not comforting. A 17% slide in a month with no filing can mean the market already sees Q3 ticket pressure that the Q2 figures do not show yet. Buying before 4 November means buying before that evidence exists.
  • The Pizza Hut royalty purchase changes the comparison. It was bought with $1.2bn of consideration and financed partly with a CNH 8.4bn bridge facility (closing filing). Margin gains from it are paid for, not organic.
  • Concentration in China. The human book already has 6.9% in China and 8.1% in Hong Kong (signals.json byGeography). This adds China consumer exposure. It is a new company for the combined position, not diversification away from China. YUMC itself is 0% of the human book, so there is no direct overlap.
  • Currency and policy. RMB earnings, a US listing and Sino-US policy risk sit on top of the business risk.

EXPN.L — Experian

What it does: Experian collects credit, identity and business data on consumers and companies. It sells credit reports, scores, analytics and decisioning software to lenders, insurers, retailers and others, mainly in North America, the UK and Brazil. It also runs a consumer business that sells credit monitoring and earns referral fees when consumers take out financial products.

This run's ranking, cash and the other proposal are in the run report.

1. Order

BUY 1 ordinary share of EXPN.L on the London Stock Exchange, DAY limit 2,690 GBp (£26.90), for the 24 September regular session. London was closed when this was written. Currency GBP. Place this order after the YUMC order, and only if at least £27.04 of cash remains.

Broker: Trading 212, which lists EXPN (instrument page). Broker fees are 0%, inside §4.1a. On tax: Experian is incorporated in Jersey and says UK stamp duty and SDRT do not normally apply to its shares (Experian shareholder tax page; HMRC). The £0.13 is set aside in case the contract note says otherwise. First-year costs are at most 0.5%, inside §4.1's 2%.

Half size, under Rule 4. The dominant risk is that fewer paid reports are needed, or that fees are taken by someone else. No complete, scheduled public series measures that. Partner announcements arrive when they arrive, and Experian does not publish paid-unit volumes. So the earliest observable is undated, and the order is half.

§7.2a points the same way: none of the historical years carries a certified adjustment. I apply one halving for both reasons, not two, because they describe the same uncertainty. This position is 5.4% of contributed capital.

2. Thesis

Experian earns a recurring toll each time a lender pulls data or runs a decision. That toll grew 12.3% in FY2026 on a statutory operating margin held at 23.8% to 24.2% for three years. It left $1.465bn of cash after intangibles, capex and lease payments, and still grew 9% organically in B2B in Q1 FY27. The market has cut its multiple from a five-year median of 36.4x to 22.0x, a de-rating of about 40%. At an unchanged multiple, that would be the same as permanently losing about 40% of the earnings. The price is therefore discounting a large, lasting loss of the toll to direct score licensing and agent-driven underwriting (T2).

My claim is only that the discount is larger than the evidence so far supports, because paid B2B activity is still growing. Whether the toll is shrinking beneath that growth is exactly what P3 tests. I do not assume the data franchise is safe.

3. Falsifier

The thresholds below are my decision rules, not guidance. A figure that is not disclosed counts as unresolved, never as a pass.

Warning — already active at entry. FICO says its signed direct-licence partners cover 73.1% of mortgage reseller volume, above my 70% line (FICO, 13 August). That measures potential reach, not usage. It is one reason the order is half-sized. Three further checks keep the warning live:

  • By 23 October 2026, re-read FICO's direct-licence programme and Plaid's underwriting announcements. Warn again if any partner agreement has entered production, if disclosed coverage has grown, or if a named lender says it has replaced paid Experian reports.
  • At the 18 November H1 result, warn if any consistently defined paid-volume or net-price series falls more than 5% year on year, even while revenue grows.
  • At any time, warn if FHFA, Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac announce a move from three required bureau reports to fewer (FHFA credit scores).

Break: propose a sale under §5.1, at any review and at the latest by 31 May 2027 after FY27 results, if either:

  • Lost revenue: Experian discloses lost annualised revenue from report replacement, direct licensing or platform bypass of at least 5% of FY26 revenue ($422m), without a disclosed offsetting new recurring stream.
  • Volume or price: a comparable paid-volume or net-price series falls more than 10% year on year in two consecutive observations, attributed to such substitution.

Separately, FY27 operating cash less intangibles, capex and lease principal at zero or below breaks the cash part of P2. It does not certify that the substitution risk has passed.

4. Review date

23 October 2026, regardless of price. Then the 18 November 2026 H1 result, a date the issuer has confirmed in its Q1 FY27 update. The formal annual checkpoint is 31 May 2027.

5. Numbers as of today

Local check: agree on revenue, operating and attributable profit. The local FY26 row has no EPS field. The quote's 122 GBp trailing EPS is close to the issuer's $1.634 at today's FX (123.4 GBp). The small gap comes from translation. I quote both and do not restate either.

Adjustments: Nothing new to append. The store already holds FY26's $101m financing fair-value gain, $9m disposal profit and $2m contingent-consideration gain, all as arithmetic:false because none is stated after tax and attributable to shareholders. It also holds diluted Benchmark EPS for FY25 ($1.555) and FY26 ($1.787). No research TTM exists: Experian publishes adjusted EPS only half-yearly and annually. So the 19.9x is a current reference and does not inherit the reported percentile.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: No AI or identity revenue is counted, and nothing is paid for a narrative. The case rests on filed margins, cash after reinvestment, ROIC and current organic growth. The warning that already applies is disclosed and sizes the position down rather than being argued away.

6. The case against

Theses:

  • T2 bears directly. Agents and direct score licensing can move decision work, and its fees, away from the bureau's paid reports.
  • T3 is a possible tailwind through identity and permissions, but no material revenue from it is evidenced, so none is counted.
  • T1 cuts both ways. Cheaper models lower Experian's own costs, and also the cost of competing analytics.

Dominant risk (competitive): Lenders, resellers and platforms capture the scoring and decision economics, so fewer paid reports are needed or the reseller margin disappears.

Earliest observable: FICO's and Plaid's partner and production announcements (event-driven, re-read by 23 October), then Experian's H1 disclosure on 18 November. Paid-unit data is undated and may never be published, so Rule 4 halves the order.

Secondary arguments:

  • The warning is already on. Signed coverage of 73.1% is past my line on day one. Buying under an active warning needs the reduced size and the dated re-read; neither makes the risk smaller.
  • Revenue can hide the loss. Price rises, acquisitions and consumer services can keep group growth positive while the core toll shrinks. That is T2's early shape in Leo's own words, and group growth is therefore not used as a pass anywhere in P3.
  • The earnings quality depends on the basis. Benchmark EPS excludes acquisition amortisation and fair-value items, and the $101m financing gain sits inside statutory profit. The 19.9x and 21.8x figures are close, but neither has an adjusted history behind it.
  • The combined exposure is mostly the US. EXPN.L is 0% of the human book, but most of its profit is US credit activity. A London quote does not diversify away from the book's 67% US weight.

YUMC — Yum China

What it does: Yum China operates and franchises restaurants in mainland China, principally KFC and Pizza Hut. It earns money from restaurant sales, franchise fees and supplying franchisees.

This run's ranking and allocation.

1. Order

BUY 1 share of YUMC on NYSE, DAY limit USD41.58 for the 23 September 2026 regular session. Currency USD. Assumed broker: Trading 212 Invest/ISA, whose YUMC share listing was verified.

Allocate £46 maximum total debit, half the ordinary £92 cash-funded target under §7.2a. At local USD/GBP 1.3313, principal is £31.2326, FX fee £0.0468, expected debit £31.2795. Unused allocation is £14.7205. Pot cash after this order alone is £60.7205; after the companion one-share EXPN order it is £33.9705. These are estimates at snapshot FX; do not place if the broker's debit exceeds £46. An unfilled DAY order expires, with no automatic chase or carry-forward.

Expected first-year holding costs: £0 flat commission, £0 custody, 0.15% entry FX, no ADR depositary fee because this is common stock, and no UK stamp duty on this US share. The broker schedule and HMRC support those assumptions. Modelled ticket cost is 0.15%, below both the 0.5% broker gate and 2% first-year gate; bid/ask spread is unquoted and the limit caps the purchase price. A later exit is not assumed in the first-year holding estimate.

Principal equals 6.25% of £500 contributed, within the £250 per-name cap. No whole-share exception is needed. A second share would cost £62.56 including FX and breach this reduced £46 allocation, even though the pot has spare cash. No flat commission argues for rounding up.

2. Thesis

Yum China's existing restaurant network is producing more operating cash after restaurant investment, providing an observable source of funding for expansion rather than requiring a broad Chinese consumer rebound. The current opportunity is to own that operating business while smaller formats and franchising expand its reach, with FY2025 filed operating margin improving to 10.93% from 10.28% and H1 2026 cash after capital spending at $705m (FY2025, H1). My hypothesis is that the price underweights this existing cash engine; whether discounting and delivery costs erode the return is the test in P3, not an assumption that scale prevents competition.

3. Falsifier

The following thresholds are my investment rules, not management guidance.

Warning: At Q3 results, locally estimated 4 November 2026, re-read by 6 November if either KFC or Pizza Hut has negative same-store sales while same-store transactions remain positive, or if either brand's comparable restaurant margin falls 100 basis points year on year. For Pizza Hut, remove only the actually disclosed benefit of the newly acquired royalty rights from the post-purchase period: management expects a 2.8 percentage-point steady-state margin benefit after VAT, so flat reported margin can conceal deteriorating restaurant economics (Q2 transcript, page 7). An absent bridge is unresolved and triggers a re-read; do not substitute the expected benefit as if realised.

Independently, check Meituan Core Local Commerce operating margin and incentive commentary at its next quarterly filing, by 1 December 2026. The Q2 baseline is 7.9%; below 5% with renewed subsidy/incentive spending warns of competitive pressure. This is an external platform-pressure proxy, not an estimate of Yum's market share (Meituan Q2 filing, page 13).

Break: By 1 March 2027, propose sale under §5.1 if the same brand reports two consecutive post-entry quarters with negative same-store sales, positive transactions and at least 100bp comparable restaurant-margin contraction in each; a 300bp contraction in one quarter independently breaks the case. Apply the actual royalty bridge above. These tests can fail while new openings and repurchases support headline EPS. Separately, non-positive full-year operating cash less capital spending breaks the cash-engine case; cash failing to cover ordinary and minority dividends warns. Disclose acquisition payments and borrowing separately rather than treating debt-funded distributions as operating cash.

4. Review date

6 November 2026, regardless of price, with the external quarterly checkpoint by 1 December and two-quarter conclusion by 1 March 2027.

5. Numbers as of today

Local check: partly disagree. Revenue and EPS reconcile, and filed FY2025 net income is $929m, matching local. Local operating profit is $1.326bn versus filed $1.290bn in FY2025, and $360m versus filed $348m in Q2. I use the issuer figures for margins and P3. The local capital ratio is retained only as a labelled screening proxy. The current issuer-adjusted EPS equals reported EPS but retains investment marks; it does not certify “one-off-free” earnings.

Adjustments: Reused the existing FY2024 $0.08 per-share investment gain and issuer annual/quarterly EPS records; no duplicate appended. One historical year carries a cited specific gain adjustment; two annual years carry issuer-adjusted EPS. Neither is enough to certify adjusted history, and the live research denominator has no research percentile. The historical-basis disagreement is material, hence half-size.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: I have not valued a consumer recovery or royalty savings that have not printed. Filed operating profit, cash after investment, the capital employed and transaction-versus-ticket economics determine whether this is working; USD trading does not remove RMB operating or GBP translation risk.

6. The case against

Theses: none.

Dominant risk (competitive): Discount-led demand and delivery-platform competition erode per-restaurant economics even while openings, royalty savings and repurchases keep group EPS growing.

Earliest observable: Brand same-store sales versus transactions and royalty-comparable restaurant margins at Q3, read by 6 November; independent platform margin/incentive evidence from Meituan quarterly, next by 1 December. This is observable within two quarters, so Rule 4 does not add another reduction.

Pizza Hut margins already lag KFC's. Acquiring rights costs cash and changes the comparison: the 7 August closing filing records $1.2bn consideration and a CNH8.4bn bridge facility. Savings are purchased, not organic margin expansion, and financing can reduce the benefit. A high distribution payout, RMB exposure and China's consumer environment are secondary risks.

Combined exposure: YUMC has 0% direct weight in the human book's complete signals.book.names list. This adds China consumer exposure alongside existing China holdings; it is a new company, not geographic diversification away from China. No private portfolio amount or invented combined weight is used.

EXPN.L — Experian

What it does: Experian collects credit, identity and other consumer/business data and sells reports, analytics and decision tools to lenders and other organisations. It also provides consumer credit services and earns referral revenue when consumers take financial products.

This run's ranking and allocation.

1. Order

BUY 1 ordinary share of EXPN.L on the London Stock Exchange, DAY limit 2,675 GBp (£26.75), for the 23 September 2026 regular session. Broker: Trading 212 Invest/ISA, using its verified EXPN share instrument, funded in GBP.

Allocate £46 maximum total debit, half the ordinary £92 cash-funded target. Rule 4 applies because neither paid-report displacement nor lost intermediary economics has a complete, scheduled public measurement; §7.2a also applies to uncertified adjusted history. These describe overlapping uncertainty, so I apply one half-size reduction, not repeated mechanical halvings. Principal is £26.75, unused allocation £19.25. Cash after this order alone is £65.25; after the companion YUMC order, £33.97 at snapshot FX.

Expected first-year holding costs: £0 flat commission, £0 custody and £0 FX for a GBP-funded GBP share, per Trading 212. Expected transfer tax is £0: Experian's share-specific statement says no UK/Irish stamp duty or SDRT normally applies, consistent with HMRC's distinction for foreign shares. Retain £0.1338 as a conservative 0.5% tax contingency until the ticket confirms treatment; even if charged, first-year ticket costs remain 0.5%, while broker fees are 0%, satisfying both gates. This is an ordinary share, so no ADR custody fee. Spread is unquoted; the limit controls the purchase price.

Principal is 5.35% of £500 contributed, below the £250 cap. No whole-share exception. A second share costs £53.50 and exceeds the reduced allocation even before any tax. No flat fee rewards a larger order. The DAY order expires if unfilled; no automatic later order.

2. Thesis

Experian's case is the present business of repeatedly supplying decision data to paying institutions, with FY26 statutory margins broadly stable across three years and positive cash remaining after investment, rather than an assumed new AI revenue stream. The market's approximately 40.10% de-rating from the local reported-multiple median is consistent with fear that software agents, alternate underwriting and direct scoring distribution reduce its toll; I judge applying that loss across the whole franchise too harsh against current B2B organic growth and the breadth of financial-services/vertical demand, while treating that judgement as the hypothesis P3 must test (Q1 FY27, local workings below). The case for a small position now is that current cash-producing activity can finance the transition, but there is no premise that proprietary data defeats substitution or that an Agent Trust launch has already earned anything.

3. Falsifier

These are analyst decision thresholds. “Not disclosed” means unresolved, never passed.

Warning: Active at entry: FICO says signed direct-license partners cover 73.1% of mortgage reseller volume, above my 70% partner-coverage warning line. This measures potential distribution reach, not usage; the same 13 August announcement still promises a later commercial-availability update. The warning is acknowledged now and is one reason to size small.

At a scheduled 23 October 2026 re-read of FICO/partner announcements, warn again if any such agreement has entered production, if disclosed partner coverage expands, or if a named lender says it has replaced paid Experian reports with cash-flow underwriting. Check the FICO direct-license programme and Plaid's underwriting updates monthly thereafter. These publications are event-driven, not a promised monthly data release.

At the 18 November 2026 H1 result, require any disclosed paid data/decision volumes, net unit pricing and lost distribution fees to be read separately from total revenue. A greater than 5% year-on-year decline in a consistently defined paid-volume or net-price series warns even if acquisitions and other price increases sustain revenue. Also re-read on a change from three required bureau reports to fewer under FHFA/Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac rules; credit-score choice alone is not that change.

Break: At any review, with a formal conclusion by 31 May 2027 after FY27 results, propose sale under §5.1 if either:

  • Experian discloses lost annualised net revenue from report replacement, direct licensing or decision-platform bypass of at least 5% of FY26 statutory group revenue, $422.25m, without an offsetting disclosed new recurring net-revenue stream; or
  • a comparable disclosed paid-volume or net-unit-price series falls more than 10% year on year in two consecutive observations attributable to such substitution.

These are direct economic loss tests and can trip while group revenue still grows. If the required unit or lost-fee disclosures never become public, this dominant-risk test remains unmeasurable; it is not replaced with a reassuring group-growth figure. Keep the warning and reduced sizing, and reconsider ownership at the dated review.

Separately, non-positive filed full-year operating cash less intangible purchases, PP&E and lease principal breaks the financing part of P2. That cash safeguard does not certify that substitution risk has passed.

4. Review date

23 October 2026, regardless of price, for external commercial-deployment evidence. 18 November 2026 is the issuer-confirmed H1 result date in its Q1 announcement; read it by 20 November. Formal annual checkpoint: 31 May 2027, an analyst deadline rather than an announced results date.

The current quote's 122 GBp is close to, but not identical with, the issuer's 122.7372 GBp equivalent at today's FX; I use the issuer's native-USD diluted EPS for that certified annual comparison. Rule 5 valuation interpretation: 21.93x versus 36.6029x is a 40.10% multiple discount. Holding the old multiple constant, a roughly equivalent earnings haircut would explain the price; that is a scenario, not an estimate of what investors collectively forecast. My small-position judgement is that present paid activity and reinvestment cash support more durable earning capacity than that across-the-board scenario; P3 determines whether the evidence contradicts it. The prior median is not a price target, and 19.93x Benchmark EPS never inherits the reported percentile.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: the Agent Trust/control-layer narrative receives no forecast revenue. Current capital returns, reinvestment cash, an external competing distribution mechanism and explicit currency/basis differences carry the argument. High margins invite competitors; stable past margins do not prove future protection.

6. The case against

Theses: T2, agents can move decision work away from paid workflows and weaken intermediation; T3, identity and permissions may create demand, but no separately evidenced material earnings contribution is assumed; T1, cheaper models can lower Experian's own costs while also lowering the cost of competing analytics.

Dominant risk (competitive): Lenders, resellers and agent platforms capture the decision/scoring economics, paying Experian for fewer reports or retaining fees that its distribution previously earned.

Earliest observable: FICO's signed-partner reach is already a warning; commercial-deployment notices can arrive before Experian's next accounts. Read them by 23 October, then test issuer disclosures on 18 November. Comprehensive paid-unit/fee-loss evidence is undated and incomplete, so Rule 4 halves the allocation rather than pretending group growth measures the risk.

FICO's programme explicitly seeks to remove bureau mark-ups. Plaid already supplies alternative underwriting tools, but neither source establishes Experian reports displaced. FHFA expanded score choice on 9 September while retaining the current three-report framework; that is a limited present boundary, not a permanent moat. The distribution loss can develop before headline revenue falls.

Acquisition spending, capitalised software, consumer-services cyclicality and USD/GBP translation are secondary risks. The $1.465bn cash measure is before acquisitions; buybacks do not create additional operating cash.

Combined exposure: EXPN.L has 0% direct human-book weight in the complete signals.book.names list. It adds a distinct company but retains exposure to US credit activity; a London quote is not an escape from the human book's large US economic exposure. No private amount or invented combined weight is published.

What it does: Yum China operates and franchises restaurants in mainland China, principally KFC and Pizza Hut. It earns restaurant sales and franchise income, with food, staffing, premises and delivery costs paid from those revenues.

This run's ranking and allocation.

1. Order

BUY 2 shares of YUMC on NYSE, day limit $41.47, regular session on 22 September 2026, through Trading 212 Invest/Stocks ISA where eligible. Let an unfilled order expire; do not chase it. This is a proposal for Leo to execute.

A discretionary £125 starting allocation is halved to £62.50 under §7.2a: the historical valuation conclusion changes with the earnings basis. At snapshot FX, USD per GBP 1.3341, principal is £62.1693, FX fee £0.0933, total £62.2625. Enforce a £62.50 maximum debit including fees if FX changes. Position principal is 12.43% of £500 contributed, inside §4.2. No one-share or fee exception. The broker lists the ordinary share; it is not an ADR. Commission and custody are free, FX is 0.15%. Expected first-year holding costs are therefore 0.15%, with no purchase transaction tax or ADR custody charge on this order. An eventual conversion on sale would add another 0.15%, before any sale-side regulatory charges. Dividend withholding is an income tax, not broker commission. There is no flat commission to dilute by buying more; a third share exceeds the reduced allocation.

2. Thesis

Yum China offers an existing restaurant cash engine: filed FY2025 operating margin rose from 10.3% to 10.9%, and the local annual asset-turnover series improved alongside it (annual results, local capital history). At 15.19 times reported and company-adjusted trailing earnings, the price permits a small entry without requiring a return to its historical median. The opportunity is continuing operating efficiency across the existing estate, while P3 tests whether lower customer tickets and delivery competition consume those efficiencies; new store counts and purchased royalty savings are not proof that demand economics improved.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At Q3 results, locally estimated 4 November 2026, review by 6 November if KFC same-store sales turn negative while transactions remain positive, or its restaurant margin falls 100 basis points year on year. Apply the same tests to Pizza Hut, but compare margins after removing the actually disclosed benefit of the purchased royalty rights from the post-purchase period; no estimated benefit is silently booked as fact. Management expects a 2.8 percentage-point steady-state Pizza Hut margin benefit after VAT, so an unchanged unadjusted margin could hide deterioration (Q2 transcript, page 7). If the actual bridge is absent, that leg is unresolved and requires review; KFC and the sales/transaction tests remain independently observable.

Outside the company, check Meituan Core Local Commerce operating margin and incentive commentary quarterly, next by 1 December 2026. Its Q2 baseline is 7.9%; below 5%, accompanied by renewed spending on user incentives, is an independent warning about competitive pressure, not proof of a Yum market-share loss (Meituan filed Q2 result, pages 13 and 19). These thresholds are analyst choices, not issuer guidance.

Break: By 1 March 2027, propose an exit under §5.1 if the same brand has two successive post-entry quarters with negative same-store sales, positive transactions and a comparable restaurant-margin fall of at least 100 basis points in each. A 300 basis-point fall in one quarter independently breaks the case; apply the royalty adjustment rule above to Pizza Hut. This can fail while openings, buybacks and acquired savings lift group EPS. Separately, at FY2026 results, non-positive operating cash less capital spending breaks the cash-engine case; failure to cover common and minority dividends warns. Show acquisition payments and financing separately, and do not call borrowed money operating cash. Missing evidence is unresolved, never a pass.

4. Review date

6 November 2026, regardless of price. Confirm the issuer's results date when announced; the local 4 November date remains an estimate. External competition check by 1 December; two-quarter break review by 1 March 2027.

5. Numbers as of today

Prices fetched 2026-09-22 08:43:40 UTC. The regular US mark is from 21 September; the pre-market flag is not the valuation price.

6. The case against

Theses: none — T1–T3 do not directly describe restaurant pricing or delivery economics.

Dominant risk (competitive): Smaller customer tickets and delivery-platform competition can destroy restaurant economics while traffic, store count and purchased royalty savings keep headline growth positive.

Earliest observable: Brand-level sales, transactions and comparable restaurant margins at Q3, checked 6 November, plus Meituan's quarterly segment margin/incentives by 1 December. These are within two quarters, so Rule 4 does not independently require another haircut; §7.2a already halves the order.

The H1 cash measure covers dividends but not dividends plus buybacks. Purchased brand rights consume capital, and the expected royalty saving is a return on that purchase, not free organic growth. Food and staffing efficiency are plausible reasons for margins to persist, not contractual protection from competition. FX also matters: USD listing does not remove the CNY operating exposure for a GBP investor.

Combined exposure: No YUMC position appears in the public holdings roster; this starts a new company exposure and adds China consumer demand to the human book's 6.95% China classification (signals). Filed margins, asset use, cash and currency are explicit, and P3 can warn even when EPS rises. EUZ.DE — Eckert & Ziegler

What it does: Eckert & Ziegler supplies radioactive materials, components and services for nuclear medicine and industrial uses. Customers include radiopharmaceutical producers and users of radiation sources; it earns from products, manufacturing services and licensing.

This run's ranking and allocation.

1. Order

BUY 5 shares of EUZ.DE on Deutsche Börse Xetra, day limit €12.21, regular session on 22 September 2026, through Trading 212 Invest/Stocks ISA where eligible. Let an unfilled order expire. This is a proposal for Leo to execute.

A discretionary £125 starting allocation is halved to £62.50 under §7.2a, because the historical earnings basis is not certified after licensing effects. At local FX, EUR/USD 1.1444, GBP/USD 1.3341, principal is £52.3691, FX fee £0.0786, total £52.4477. Set a £62.50 maximum total debit if FX moves. A sixth share costs £62.8429 before fees, already over the reduced allocation. The unused allocation is £10.0523; cash after both this run's orders is £41.3498.

Principal is 10.47% of £500 contributed. No cap exception is used. The exact Xetra ordinary share is listed by Trading 212; the schedule gives zero commission/custody and 0.15% FX, so expected first-year holding costs are 0.15%. Purchase transaction tax £0; no ADR fee. Dividend withholding is separate income tax. A sale with conversion adds another 0.15% FX before any applicable sale charges. There is no flat fee for an extra share to dilute.

2. Thesis

Eckert & Ziegler supplies an existing medical-isotope business, rather than a single drug-development outcome, and H1 Medical adjusted EBIT rose about 7% to €24.9m (issuer release). At 15.26x reported trailing earnings and 13.07x annual operating cash flow, a small position can be supported by the operating franchise without valuing an unproven isotope shortage. The opportunity is the Medical business's contribution to group earnings, while the investment question is whether those earnings produce cash after expansion and related-party commitments; that is the risk P3 tests rather than assumes away.

3. Falsifier

Warning: Active at entry. H1 operating cash divided by parent-attributable profit is 0.573x, below my 0.80x warning line. At the 12 November 2026 nine-month release, re-read if it remains below 0.80x, or operating cash less purchases of equipment/intangibles and lease principal is non-positive. A reduction in the approximately €80m adjusted-EBIT outlook also warns. These cash definitions come from the interim statements; the thresholds are my investment rules.

Break: At 24 March 2027 full-year results, propose an exit under §5.1 if full-year operating cash / positive parent-attributable profit is below 0.80x, or cash after the same reinvestment and lease payments is non-positive. Non-positive attributable profit itself breaks the case. A full-year test allows working-capital seasonality; November is the earlier warning, not a reason to postpone review.

Independently, a disclosed impairment/default on Pentixapharm funding at either release, or additional related-party cash advances exceeding operating cash after equipment/intangibles and lease principal while net borrowing rises over the same period, breaks the capital-allocation case. This last rule is prospective: compare post-entry reporting periods on a consistent basis and show the opening/closing borrowing amounts. Separate an investment cash outflow from operating capex without ignoring it. If the components are unavailable, escalate the review as unresolved, not passed. These tests can fail while revenue and adjusted EBIT increase.

4. Review date

12 November 2026, regardless of price; full-year break check 24 March 2027. Both are dates on the issuer calendar.

5. Numbers as of today

Adjustments: The existing FY2025 €5m extraordinary licensing revenue entry in adjustments was rechecked against the issuer's H1 comparison. It remains arithmetic:false: revenue and the comparative licensing cash receipt are not after-tax attributable profit. No new direct adjusted EPS or separately quantified attributable adjustment was found; nothing was appended merely to duplicate existing evidence.

6. The case against

Theses: none — T1–T3 do not directly bear on isotope manufacturing and its cash requirements.

Dominant risk (financial): Expansion, working capital and related-party financing absorb the earnings, leaving shareholders with an attractive profit number but little cash.

Earliest observable: The nine-month cash-flow statement and related-party note on 12 November 2026. The warning is already active; a new seasonal reading is due within two quarters. Rule 4 does not require an additional haircut, while §7.2a and the cash concern support the reduced allocation.

H1 revenue was almost flat, and Medical's improvement coexists with weaker group adjusted EBIT. Specialist production and regulated customer supply chains may support margins, but do not guarantee attractive returns on additional capital. Licensing is episodic, and an isotope-demand story does not settle customer contracts, capacity utilisation or related-party recovery. The GBP investor also bears EUR exposure.

Combined exposure: EUZ is absent from the public holdings roster, so this adds a new company to the human book's 6.04% Europe classification (signals). The pot already holds AZN.L, so it adds healthcare exposure; isotope supply differs from a drug franchise but the sector overlap is real and is disclosed, not a ranking veto.

Why this is not 7532.T again: No value is assigned to a macro shortage alone. The case names current segment earnings, the thin cash bridge, capital productivity and FX, and makes poor conversion a reason to exit even if the headline medical story remains popular.

YUMC — Yum China

What it does: Yum China operates and franchises restaurants in mainland China, principally KFC and Pizza Hut. It earns restaurant sales and franchise fees; its NYSE security is common stock, not an ADR. Company filing.

This run's ranking and allocation.

1. Order

BUY 3 whole shares of YUMC on NYSE, through Trading 212 Invest/Stocks ISA, limit $41.12, regular session only. Currency USD. Use a day order on 21 September 2026; an unfilled order expires and requires fresh pricing before re-entry.

Allocate £93.85 including costs, after reserving £62.50 for the accompanying EUZ proposal. Principal at the limit and local USD/GBP 1.3386 is £92.1560; expected FX fee £0.1382, total £92.2942. Total 0.15% of principal, clearing both §4.1a and §4.1. This excludes an unplanned sale and personal dividend/income taxes. Availability and charges: T212 YUMC listing, broker schedule. No Rule 4 haircut: the dominant risk has quarterly unit and margin observations within two quarters. No §7.2a haircut: current issuer-adjusted EPS is sourced and agrees with reported TTM; the historical percentile is only a reference, and the operating-income classification discrepancy below is explicitly excluded from the falsifier's inputs. The allocation is nevertheless much smaller than the hard cap.

2. Thesis

Existing restaurants and a growing franchise estate produce cash that can finance further openings: FY2025 operating margin rose to 10.9% from 10.3%, on 4% revenue growth (annual results). The August completion of the Pizza Hut rights purchase changes the economics of subsequent openings, making the next reporting period a useful entry checkpoint (completion filing). My inference is that the market may be underweighting the combined contribution of existing-store cash and franchised expansion; I assign no value to a broad Chinese consumer rebound, and do not assume that buying rights guarantees an adequate return.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At Q3 results, locally estimated for 4 November 2026, re-read by 6 November if either KFC or Pizza Hut reports negative same-store sales with positive same-store transactions, or loses 100 basis points of restaurant margin year on year. These are analyst thresholds and can fire while openings and buybacks keep total sales and EPS growing. The relevant definitions and starting brand readings are in the Q2 release.

Independently, inspect Meituan's next quarterly filing by 1 December 2026: a Core Local Commerce operating margin below 5%, accompanied by management attributing the decline to renewed subsidies or incentives, triggers the same re-read. Its Q2 baseline is 7.92%, derived from RMB5.668275bn segment operating profit / RMB71.530555bn revenue (HKEX filing). This is an external competitive-pressure indicator, not a measurement of Yum China's market share.

Break: By 1 March 2027, two successive post-entry quarters in which the same brand has negative same-store sales, positive transactions and a restaurant-margin decline of at least 100 basis points year on year in each quarter break the unit-economics thesis and call for an exit proposal under §5.1. Independently, either brand losing 300 basis points in one post-entry quarter breaks it without waiting for a second report. These analyst rules test profitable demand directly, rather than treating a group EPS increase as a pass.

Separately, at FY2026 results by the same date, warn if operating cash minus cash capital spending fails to cover common and non-controlling dividends; break if that cash measure is non-positive. Track acquisition expenditure and borrowing separately, so purchased royalties do not masquerade as free growth. Missing brand or cash disclosures leave the test unresolved and require review; they never count as a pass.

4. Review date

6 November 2026, regardless of price. Check the estimated result date beforehand; if delayed, retain the review with “not reported”. The external competitive checkpoint is 1 December, and the two-quarter test is due by 1 March 2027.

5. Numbers as of today

Deep-dive run report — 21 September 2026, 09:30 UTC

Propose 3 YUMC and 6 EUZ.DE. At their limits and snapshot FX, total expected debit is £154.76, leaving £1.59. The EUZ limit is below its latest quote; it is not an instruction to chase a fill. Open the YUMC proposal and EUZ proposal for the orders, risks and review rules.

The run has £156.35 cash, £500 contributed and a £250 per-name cap, from positions, generated 09:04:59 UTC. Actual holdings are eight MWA, one TW and one AZN.L. Earlier drafts reserve no money. Read together: 21 September 09:10 Sweep, 20 September 12:03 Review, strategy, standing theses, origins and adjustments.

Prices were fetched at 09:22:13 UTC; Scan at 09:22:19 UTC uses that snapshot. There is no standing instruction: VIX is 14.98, below 40. US prices are Friday's regular closes, while EUZ is a Monday regular-session quote. The weekly bucket ending 25 September contains current observations, not future Friday knowledge. The Review retains MWA/TW and keeps AZN warned; no new sale is inferred from price movement.

Ranked watchlist: 32

All 32 names passing either valid earnings or operating-cash cheapest-decile screen receive a full row. Ranking is business judgement; allocation separately prefers fresh names under §4.5a. WAIT identifies a candidate retained under the rules but awaiting the specified dated evidence; it carries no order. Exclusions are this run's decisions, not permanent bans.

Origins below come from origins.json. “Intact” means the discovery premise remains plausible on the stated local or freshly checked evidence; it does not certify the original Sweep's whole thesis. Financial screen evidence is in the workings table.

EUZ.DE — Eckert & Ziegler

What it does: Eckert & Ziegler supplies radioactive materials and components used in medical imaging, cancer treatment and industrial measurement. It also develops and manufactures products for radiopharmaceutical customers, earning money from materials, equipment and services. Issuer description.

This run's ranking and allocation.

1. Order

BUY 6 whole shares of EUZ.DE on Xetra, through Trading 212 Invest/Stocks ISA, limit €12.12, regular session only. Currency EUR. Use a day order on 21 September 2026; if unfilled, obtain a fresh quote before another day order.

Ordinary discretionary target £125, below the £250 hard cap; halve it to £62.50 including costs under §7.2a. The historical licensing/perimeter adjustment is not a certified recurring earnings history. I also want a small position while the current cash warning is active. These are one shared haircut, not compounded quarter-sizing.

Six shares at the limit cost €72.72 = £62.3764, using USD/EUR 1.1482 and USD/GBP 1.3386. FX costs £0.0936, bringing expected debit to £62.4700. Maximum account debit £62.50: do not raise the limit or invade the companion YUMC allocation.

The local regular quote is €12.17. Six shares there would cost £62.73 including FX, above the reduced budget; €12.12 is the highest cent limit fitting that all-in budget at snapshot FX. A missed fill is acceptable. Seven shares at €12.12 would exceed the reduced allocation. A larger ticket would not reduce T212's proportional fee.

Expected first-year buy-and-hold costs: £0 commission, 0.15% FX, £0 custody and £0 ADR fee; no purchase transaction tax is expected for this German ordinary share. Total 0.15%, below the 0.5% broker-fee and 2% first-year ceilings. Personal dividend tax and an unplanned sale are separate. T212 exact instrument, broker costs. The limit controls the price paid across any market spread.

Cash left if only this fills: £93.88; if both proposals fill at the stated limits and FX: £1.59. This is 12.48% of £500 contributed, below §4.2. No whole-share or fee exception is used. This fresh name gets capital ahead of comparable pot top-ups under §4.5a.

2. Thesis

Medical-isotope supply and contract manufacturing already earn operating profit, giving exposure to treatment activity without requiring a successful drug-development outcome (issuer release). The relevant current change is Medical adjusted EBIT growth against nearly flat segment revenue, supported by growing lutetium and manufacturing activity (interim report). My inference is that the flat group sales comparison obscures a more valuable medical mix, but its shareholder value depends on the cash tests below and is not established by the isotope-demand narrative.

3. Falsifier

Warning: Already active at entry. H1 operating cash / attributable net profit is 0.573x, below my 0.80x threshold. At 12 November 2026, re-read if the nine-month ratio remains below 0.80x or cash after equipment/intangible purchases and principal lease payments is non-positive. A reduction in the issuer's roughly €80m adjusted-EBIT outlook is an additional warning. The ratio is an analyst rule, not management guidance.

Break: At FY2026 results on 24 March 2027, propose an exit under §5.1 if full-year operating cash / positive attributable net profit is below 0.80x, or cash after the same reinvestment and lease payments is non-positive. Non-positive attributable profit is itself a break, not a way to pass the ratio. This allows a complete seasonal cycle, while the November warning forces an earlier review.

Independently, at either the November or March result, a disclosed material impairment/default on related-party funding, or evidence that medical expansion requires recurring external funding despite growing reported profit, breaks the capital-allocation case immediately. Track Pentixapharm financing separately from operating capex: a financing outflow is not silently relabelled a recurring expense, and neither is it ignored.

Use matching year-to-date periods from the consolidated statements, with parent-attributable profit. A missing component makes the test unresolved and triggers review, not a pass. These tests directly respond to P6: revenue and adjusted EBIT may rise while they fail. The thresholds are my investment rules. Definitions: interim statements; dates: issuer calendar.

4. Review date

12 November 2026, irrespective of price; final annual test 24 March 2027. Both dates are on the issuer's calendar.

5. Numbers as of today

Local prices fetched 21 September 2026, 09:22:13 UTC. EUZ's regular-session quote was struck at 08:57:53 UTC that morning.

Local check: Local H1 revenue agrees. Summed local attributable profit is €22.368m versus €22.369m filed, a €1,000 rounding difference. Local operating profit totals €33.414m versus filed EBIT €33.591m and company-adjusted EBIT €33.318m; these are not interchangeable. P3 uses the issuer cash statement, not the local operating-profit field.

Adjustments: The existing EUZ FY2025 €5m licensing-revenue entry was reverified; it remains arithmetic:false because revenue is not after-tax attributable income. One historical year has cited evidence; zero has a certified arithmetic adjustment. No issuer-adjusted EPS was supplied by the release; a bridge for EBIT cannot manufacture it. No new qualifying EPS adjustment was writable, and none was inferred. There is no researchEps or certified adjusted percentile. The haircut prices this uncertainty. Store, interim report.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: The purchase rests on existing medical earnings and the capital behind them, not a promised demand surge. It is deliberately small under a cash warning, uses the EUR/GBP conversion correctly, and can fail even if the medical-growth story remains popular.

6. The case against

Theses: none — this is not a model vendor, seat-priced workflow or AI control-layer investment.

Dominant risk (financial): Medical expansion and related-party capital commitments consume cash faster than the shareholder earnings they generate.

Earliest observable: The warning already exists in H1 cash conversion; the next dated observation is the 12 November nine-month cash statement. It is within two quarters, so Rule 4 does not impose an additional haircut.

H1 cash after reinvestment and leases barely remains positive. The separate €4m Pentixapharm convertible-bond purchase further reduces cash available to shareholders; it is excluded from the operating cash definition, but included in the capital-allocation judgement (interim report). Medical growth must also offset weaker industrial activity. Supply demand alone establishes neither pricing power nor an adequate return on new facilities; regulatory or production interruptions could damage both.

Total exposure: No direct EUZ position appears in the human holdings, so direct existing weight is 0%. This adds to 6.11% Europe and 0.97% Healthcare in the human book; it is a new company, while the AI pot already owns AstraZeneca (holdings, Scan book, pot positions). Overlap is disclosed and did not change the ranking.

Decisions and allocation

  1. Propose 2 EXPN.L at a day limit of 2727p: £54.54 principal.
  2. Propose 4 EUZ.DE at a day limit of €12.12: £41.5915 principal plus £0.0624 FX.
  3. Hold £60.16 cash after expected £96.19 total outlay. Reserving a conservative 0.5% EXPN tax contingency leaves £59.88. Maximum debit instructions in the proposals leave at least £59.83 even with that reserve and modest EUR FX movement.

Each fresh name receives half the cash-feasible allocation that the £250 cap would otherwise allow, once, under the shared Rule 4/§7.2a mechanism; the rules do not instruct cumulative quarter-sizing. EXPN: £156.35 / 2 = £78.175, hence two £27.27 shares (three exceed the haircut). EUZ: remaining £101.81 / 2 = £50.905, hence four £10.397879 shares (five exceed the haircut). Both positions are well below 50% of contributed capital. The proposals do not assume a sale, a new contribution or acceptance of earlier drafts.

Cash was tested against the rest of the ranking: YUMC awaits post-purchase unit economics; LSEG awaits subscription monetisation evidence; NVO/NKE await their named operational checkpoints. TW/MWA/AZN are held and their Review/results questions remain; no top-up outranks the two comparable fresh opportunities under §4.5a. The other rows fail a stated business or funding rule. There is no third business here strong enough to spend the residual merely to reduce cash.

Shortlist reconciliations

EXPN: the proposal reconciles FY26 revenue, operating profit and attributable income to the issuer; uses annual diluted EPS separately from current trailing EPS; and makes no adjusted-percentile claim. Q1 B2B demand and cash after investment justify a small research position, while external substitution observability is weak enough to halve it. The declared T2/T3 issue is addressed in P3/P6, not assumed away as an AI moat.

EUZ: H1 revenue agrees; local summed operating profit does not exactly reproduce the interim report, so the proposal uses the filing. Annual P/OCF looks inexpensive while current H1 cash conversion is weak. The older licensing receipt and the Pentixapharm perimeter issue are not netted into fabricated EPS. No adjusted historical percentile is certified.

YUMC: Q2 issuer results show Pizza Hut transactions +13%, ticket -11% and restaurant margin 12.9% versus 13.3%. Local Q2 revenue $3.138bn and EPS $0.70 agree; local operating profit $360m differs from the issuer's $348m, which is used for judgement. Stored research TTM EPS $2.73 is issuer-adjusted, not owner earnings. The $1.2bn brand-rights purchase completed on 7 August; waiting for completion would be stale. I wait for evidence that transaction growth earns adequate returns after substituting purchase financing for royalty expense.

LSEG: H1 results report ASV growth 6.1%, retention 92.8%, operating cash £1.785bn and reported operating profit £1.428bn. Local half-year revenue including recoveries £4.985bn agrees. The 260bps constant-currency EBITDA margin gain includes 140bps from the SwapClear agreement, leaving 120bps underlying; engaged AI customers are not separately disclosed paid revenue. T1/T3 could support licensed-data distribution, while T2 can compress Workspace seats. Await the Q3 read, by 15 November, rather than claim those effects net positive. Appended issuer diluted adjusted EPS 243.9p (H1 2026) and 207.7p (H1 2025); those disconnected halves do not make TTM earnings or an adjusted percentile. Missing H2 is logged. Gross adjustments are not converted into after-tax owner earnings.

This is not the 7532.T mistake again: the two buys have explicit multi-year margins, capital returns, source-backed cash tests and currency-correct orders. Neither tourism, a rebound, AI enthusiasm nor an isotope headline substitutes for those tests. The EUZ cash weakness and Experian displacement blind spot are reasons for half allocations with observable review triggers, not fine print beneath a full-size buy.

EXPN.L — Experian

What it does: Experian collects credit and identity information and sells reports, scores and decision tools to lenders and other businesses. It also sells consumers credit-monitoring and related financial services, earning business data/service fees and consumer subscription revenue.

Run report, full ranking and joint cash allocation

1. Order

BUY 2 whole ordinary shares of EXPN.L on the London Stock Exchange, limit 2727p (£27.27), through Trading 212 Invest/ISA. Submit during the regular session on 21 September 2026, day expiry; do not chase an unfilled order. Quote currency GBp; settlement amount £54.54, with a maximum total debit £54.82. This is a proposal for Leo to execute.

Cash-feasible ordinary allocation is min(£250 position cap, £156.35 cash) = £156.35. Half allocation £78.175, under brief Rule 4 because direct displacement evidence has no reliable scheduled series, and §7.2a because no comparable adjusted history is certified. Apply the shared half-size mechanic once, not twice: floor(£78.175 / £27.27) = 2. Three cost £81.81 and exceed it. Deployment is 10.91% of £500 contributed capital, below the 50% cap; no whole-share exception is needed. Standalone cash after this order is £101.81 before a tax contingency; after the companion EUZ proposal it is £60.16.

Trading 212 lists EXPN.GB. Its fee schedule gives £0 flat commission, £0 custody and no FX on this GBP purchase: expected broker fee 0%, below §4.1a's 0.5%. No ADR fee. Expected transaction tax is £0: Experian's current FAQ identifies Jersey incorporation and a Jersey register; HMRC distinguishes overseas shares outside a UK register. That tax treatment is an inference from the two sources, not a broker order preview. Reserve £0.2727 (0.5%) if the actual tax assessment differs; first-year identified fees/tax remain at most 0.5%, below §4.1's 2%. The maximum debit covers rounding. Market spread is not separately quoted in this weekend snapshot; the limit caps purchase price. No financing or assumed sale is included.

2. Thesis

Experian's business data demand is growing while filed operating margins have stayed near 24%, and cash left after software, equipment and leases supports reinvestment rather than requiring a credit-cycle rebound. I infer that part of the 39.3% discount to the historical reported-P/E median prices T2-style agent/open-banking substitution as well as credit-cycle risk; the repository cannot identify the market's motive. I judge that discount too severe for the earnings and cash being generated now, supported by 9% Q1 B2B organic growth and continued three-bureau requirements, but whether substitute underwriting displaces paid Experian data is a separate, unresolved test in P3, not an assumed enduring moat.

3. Falsifier

Break: By the 18 November 2026 review, or any later monthly check, two independently named lenders have issuer-authored announcements explicitly describing that replacement, or Experian quantifies a year-on-year fall of at least 10% in comparable paid credit-data transactions while B2B nominal revenue remains non-negative. That would falsify the claimed durability of the current earning engine even if price/mix masks volume loss, and calls for an exit proposal under §5.1. These are analyst thresholds, not management guidance. An unreported unit series is unknown, not a passed test; do not manufacture a customer count.

External baseline checked on 20 September: Fannie Mae credit-score guidance and credit-report requirements retain three-bureau reports; FHFA's programme separates score-model modernisation from the transition to fewer reports. Plaid's underwriting documentation establishes a cash-flow report/score substitute capability, but supplies no comparable count of Experian reports displaced. These sources update on announcements, not a guaranteed quarterly adoption schedule. There is no clean displacement-rate baseline today; that limitation causes the half allocation.

A supplementary financial warning is an H1 outlook cut or B2B organic growth below 5%, checked against the issuer's next update. It does not replace the external displacement test.

Half of the ordinary cash-feasible allocation is £50.905 (reserved case £50.76865), giving four shares at £10.397879 each; five cost £51.9894 before fees and exceed either half allocation. §7.2a halves size for an uncertified earnings/perimeter comparison, once.
