Trading 212's EUZ.DE page confirms the listing; its fee schedule gives £0 flat commission, 0.15% FX and £0 custody. Expected purchase tax £0, no ADR custody fee. Entry broker costs are 0.15%, below §4.1a's 0.5%; identified first-year holding cost is 0.15%, or about 0.30% if sold and converted once at unchanged value, below §4.1's 2%. No financing cost is assumed. The weekend snapshot supplies no executable spread; the limit and GBP debit ceiling bound entry cost.

2. Thesis

Eckert & Ziegler sells the isotope inputs and manufacturing work needed by medical customers, with an earning engine that also includes industrial sources. The Medical segment's H1 adjusted EBIT growth and the last three years of improving filed group margins support a small investment in delivered operating earnings rather than an unpriced industry demand forecast. The business opportunity is to turn that medical production into durable shareholder cash, and today's allocation buys limited exposure while the next cash-flow statements test whether that conversion actually occurs.

3. Falsifier

Warning: The H1 starting position is already strained: cash from operations / attributable profit is about 57%, and cash after equipment/intangible capex and principal leases is only €0.634m. Re-read at 12 November 2026 if nine-month operating cash / attributable profit remains below 70%, or cash after those capex and lease payments is zero or negative. A cut to the issuer's €320m sales / €80m adjusted EBIT outlook is an additional immediate warning. These conversion thresholds are analyst rules, not issuer guidance.

Break: At FY2026 results on 24 March 2027, operating cash / positive attributable net income remains below 60%, or operating cash minus equipment/intangible capex and principal leases is zero or negative. An earlier disclosure that the medical expansion cannot generate positive cash without repeated external funding also breaks the case. This tests cash return on production directly, even when revenue and adjusted EBIT still grow; it calls for an exit proposal under §5.1.

Use the consolidated cash-flow statement and parent-attributable income for matching year-to-date periods, not an annualised quarter. Track loans/investments in Pentixapharm separately; they consume shareholder cash but are not equipment capex or recurring operating expense. If the November report omits a required line, the warning stays unresolved rather than passing by default. H1 statement; issuer results calendar.

4. Review date

12 November 2026, confirmed Q3 reporting date, regardless of price. Full-year cash-conversion break check 24 March 2027, confirmed FY2026 results date. Review any accounting-enforcement update when announced.

The medical-isotope discovery case remains plausible, but the local accounts still include industrial exposure and licensing/perimeter complications. Adjusted EBIT growth is not free cash flow. Cash committed to a spun-off company's convertible is a real allocation choice; an accounting presentation change would not recover it. Human-book overlap: No EUZ/Eckert & Ziegler holding in the public instrument list, hence 0% direct existing weight. YUMC — Yum China

What it does: Yum China operates and franchises restaurants in China, principally KFC and Pizza Hut. It earns sales from company-operated restaurants and fees from franchisees, and runs purchasing, delivery and restaurant-support operations.

Run report and full ranking.

1. Order

BUY 2 shares of YUMC on NYSE, day limit $41.12, regular session on 21 September 2026. Currency USD. Use Trading 212 Invest, which lists YUMC. Cancel unfilled shares at that session's close; no automatic replacement or price increase.

The £250 position cap exceeds the £83.5357 cash remaining after EUZ, so that cash is the allocation. No additional §7.2a reduction is applied: current EPS reconciles to issuer periods, the small historical investment gain is identified, and issuer margins replace the discrepant vendor field. This is a judgment that the residual earnings uncertainty is not material enough to halve this already small residual ticket; the limits of the historical basis remain disclosed. Two shares deploy $82.24 = £61.4052, using local GBP/USD 1.3393. Entry FX costs £0.0921, total £61.4973. Cash left idle is £22.0383, rounded £22.04. Principal is 12.28% of £500 contributed, below the cap. Sources: prices, positions, arithmetic.

Broker schedule: £0 commission, 0.15% FX, £0 custody. Expected purchase tax £0 and ADR fee £0: YUMC is common stock, not an ADR. Expected first-year buy-and-hold transaction/custody cost is 0.15%; income withholding is separate from that cost. No sale is assumed. A third share would require about £30.75 including FX and cannot fit the post-EUZ balance. No flat commission can be diluted by increasing this order.

Maximum actual debit £61.60, including FX. If unavailable, leave unplaced. The two proposals' combined maximum debit is £134.60, within recorded cash.

2. Thesis

Yum China's restaurant network has converted modest sales growth into improving issuer operating margins, rather than merely multiplying outlets: the FY2025 issuer margin was 10.9%, against 10.3% in FY2024 (annual release). The completed Pizza Hut brand purchase supplies a specific next step in economics because the previously paid royalty becomes an owned right, although the price paid and financing must earn their return (completion filing). My inference is that this operating change deserves a small investment now; the durability of traffic bought through lower tickets and delivery spending is what P3 tests.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At Q3 results, locally estimated for 4 November 2026, re-read by 6 November if either brand's same-store sales turn negative while its transactions still grow, or its restaurant margin falls at least 100 basis points year on year. This detects traffic purchased at worsening economics before consolidated growth breaks. Separately, at Meituan's next quarterly release, checked by 1 December 2026, re-read if Core Local Commerce operating margin falls below 5% and the filing attributes the decline to renewed incentives/competition. These are analyst thresholds, not issuer forecasts.

Break: By FY2026 results, checked by 1 March 2027, sell under §5.1 if two consecutive post-entry quarters show negative same-store sales alongside positive transaction growth for either brand, and that same brand loses at least 100 basis points of restaurant margin year on year in both quarters. This tests whether discount-driven volume destroys restaurant economics even while system sales and EPS grow. Missing unit or margin disclosure requires a re-read and an unresolved status, not a pass.

Royalty savings could mask Pizza Hut deterioration; therefore also compare its disclosed margin with the purchase's expected benefit and explain the movement. Never replace a failed unit-economics test with EPS growth. Sources for baseline definitions: Q2 release, Meituan's quarterly filing.

4. Review date

6 November 2026, regardless of price. The 4 November result date remains a local estimate, not an issuer-confirmed event. Additional external check 1 December 2026, final two-quarter check 1 March 2027.

5. Numbers as of today

Prices snapshot 2026-09-19T16:08:16.817Z, regular close dated 18 September.

Local check: Q2 EPS, sales and attributable income agree. Operating profit does not: local Q2 $360m versus issuer $348m, and local FY2025 $1,326m versus issuer $1,290m. Use issuer operating margins, and label the stored capital ratios as vendor screening metrics. Those annual ratios also predate the brand acquisition. The cash percentile is outside the cheapest decile, so this passes on earnings only; no denominatorDrift flag is raised, but cash is weaker confirmation.

Adjustments: Existing YUMC periods in adjustments already contain the company-adjusted annual and contiguous TTM figures; do not append duplicates. The FY2024 $0.08 investment-gain EPS evidence is also already recorded. One annual period has direct adjusted EPS, one different historical year has cited gain evidence; there is no certified rolling adjusted historical percentile. Research EPS is not owner earnings, and no new one-off adjustment was invented.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: The case tests ticket size against transactions and margins, prices the acquisition's additional capital explicitly, and sizes within the residual cash budget. It does not infer better returns from store openings, a consumer rebound or EPS buybacks.

6. The case against

Theses: none. General use of AI in restaurants is not enough to attach T1–T3, which address model economics, paid workflows and control products.

Dominant risk (competitive): Delivery-platform competition and discounts buy customer traffic while destroying restaurant margin.

Earliest observable: Q3 brand-level same-store sales, transactions and restaurant margins, expected early November; Meituan's quarterly Core Local Commerce margin and incentive commentary provide the external check. Its Q2 improvement partly reflected reduced incentives and seasonal delivery costs, not proof that the competitive threat ended (filing). The next observations are within two quarters, so Rule 4 does not require another timing reduction.

The royalty purchase can flatter operating margin while debt and capital employed increase. Refinancing, China consumption, regulation and CNY/USD/GBP translation remain secondary risks. An efficient supply network is a possible reason margins persist, not a demonstrated protection from a subsidy war.

There is no existing YUMC holding in the human book. This adds China consumer exposure to the existing 7.07% China weight, including other China-facing businesses; the economic exposure is Chinese despite NYSE execution (holdings, book weights). No combined monetary weight is inferred from sealed amounts.

2. Thesis

Supplying medical isotopes offers recurring product demand without having to choose a single successful drug, and Medical adjusted EBIT rose about 7% in H1 even as the industrial segment weakened (issuer update). The reason to consider entry now is improving medical mix alongside the multi-year improvement in local capital returns, rather than a prediction of a general nuclear boom. My inference is that the market may be giving too little credit to that mix change; whether the resulting earnings convert into investible cash remains the test, not an assumption.

At Q3 on 12 November 2026, re-read if the same year-to-date ratio remains below 0.8x, or the approximately €80m full-year adjusted-EBIT forecast is cut. These are analyst tests; 0.8x is not management guidance. The cash baseline comes from the H1 statements, guidance from the issuer update.

Expected first-year holding costs: £0 commission, £0.19 FX (0.15%), £0 custody and £0 ADR fees; no purchase transaction tax expected on this US common share. Broker fees and total holding costs are 0.15%, clearing both gates (broker schedule). This excludes an unplanned sale; another currency conversion would incur the published FX rate. Estimated debit £123.805, leaving £157.205 of current cash before the other proposals. After all three proposed orders, £4.26 remains. Maximum debit for this order is £125 including fees; if FX makes it exceed that, reduce the native limit or leave it unfilled. Do not substitute an IBKR fee assumption.

2. Thesis

The business case is an established restaurant network increasing its earning power: issuer annual operating margin rose from 10.3% to 10.9% in FY2025, while local asset turnover rose from 1.02x to 1.09x (FY release, capital). The completed Pizza Hut brand purchase changes a recurring cost rather than merely adding stores, with management expecting royalty savings to improve that brand's margin (completion). My inference is that these existing operations and the cost change merit a small investment at today's price; the claimed opportunity is not a broad China-consumption rebound, and competitive pricing remains an open test.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At Q3, locally estimated 4 November 2026, re-read if system same-store sales are flat/negative, or either KFC or Pizza Hut restaurant margin falls 100 basis points year on year. Independently, re-read if Alibaba's quarterly China Quick Commerce revenue grows at least 30% while Yum China's same-store sales are flat/negative: this is an external competitive-pressure flag, not proof of lost market share. Check the next Alibaba release by 30 November 2026, even if it follows Yum China's result.

Break: By 1 March 2027, sell under §5.1 if Q3 and Q4 both have negative system same-store sales and either brand's restaurant margin falls at least 100 basis points year on year in both quarters. Also break if Pizza Hut's margin alone falls at least 100 basis points in both, even with positive group sales: royalty savings must not hide deteriorating restaurant economics. Use like-for-like brand definitions and each quarter's own prior-year comparator. These are analyst thresholds, not company guidance; they can fire while expansion and buybacks still lift EPS.

4. Review date

5 November 2026, irrespective of price. Follow up on the external result by 30 November and the two-quarter test by 1 March 2027. Refresh the result calendar if the estimate moves.

Pizza Hut's Q2 ticket average fell 11% while its restaurant margin declined 40 basis points. That is an adverse baseline, not a risk disproved by more transactions (Q2 release). What the issuer checks establish

  • YUMC: the current reported and company-adjusted denominators differ slightly; issuer operating profit is below the local field. P5 uses issuer margins and records the disagreement. The completed brand acquisition is a concrete operating-cost change, not an assumption about Chinese consumption.
  • AZN: cash after PP&E and purchased intangibles has weakened even as Core grows. Its proposal starts under a cash warning. The low annual cash multiple cannot certify returns on new investment.
  • EUZ: the H1 report identifies Lutetium-177 and CDMO growth within Medical; the flat group top line therefore does not describe every business line. Cash conversion is poor, but the bridge identifies a larger tax-receivable balance and a prior licensing receipt rather than establishing that Medical demand has vanished. I accept a small starter under an active warning, with a standalone cash break.
  • RSGN: the 16 September final report confirms orders down 11.4%, sales down 13.1%, H1 EPS CHF0.60 versus CHF0.77, and EBITDA margin 19.0%. Local EPS CHF1.56 is still the older annual figure. The new report supplies no completed delivery recovery; it is a business exclusion, not a missing-EPS veto.
  • TW: the Q2 issuer reconciliation supports the stored adjusted quarter. Current research EPS is $3.79, giving 27.01x, versus reported 24.20x and vendor 24.49x. Only one annual adjusted period is stored; the current research denominator has no certified historical percentile. Existing exposure does not lower the business rank.
  • EXPN: Q1 FY27 gives 7% organic group growth, 11% North American B2B growth and a 2% contraction in North American Consumer Services. That is mixed evidence on T1/T2/T3, not proof that an AI discount is wrong.
  • BBW: Q2 revenue fell 7.2%. The drawdown and cash screen prompted a check; they did not turn adverse operating evidence into a buy.

No new writable earnings adjustment was found beyond existing records. Annual/direct adjusted EPS already stored was reused, with its limits disclosed. The new recurring-data request is the EUZ cash bridge and business-perimeter check, recorded in data wishlist.

FINRA TRACE supplies monthly market volumes on the third business day, next 5 October for September; check by 9 October. FINRA market volume is context, not an independently calculated Tradeweb share.

4. Review date

9 October 2026, irrespective of price, for September activity and market context. Then 30 October for fee economics. The Review lane may revisit sooner.

The local $4.19 reported TTM includes non-operating effects; $3.79 is the existing company-adjusted research series, not an invented owner-earnings reconstruction. The historical reported/vendor percentiles do not become adjusted percentiles by changing today's denominator. One filed annual adjusted period is stored; no full-window adjusted history is certified.

Adjustments: no duplicate appended. Existing TW entries already retain FY2025 Canton gains of $270.9m and Q2 2026 investment gains of $26.6m as non-arithmetic evidence, and the four issuer-adjusted quarters underlying researchEps. The gross gains are not after-tax attributable deductions.

Why this is not 7532.T again: the case relies on observed execution adoption, multi-year operating profitability and capital usage, not a macro rebound alone. Price, fees, currency, a contaminated earnings denominator and falling fee yield are all explicit; an apparently excellent margin cannot substitute for the P3 test.

6. The case against

Theses: T1, cheaper models can lower workflow costs but do not guarantee retained fees; T2, automated execution shifts the value of trading workflows and can compress the price of the service. T3 has no material role in this thesis.

Dominant risk (competitive): electronic trading grows while competitors and lower-fee portfolio protocols take away the economics per unit of activity.

Earliest observable: Tradeweb's quarterly fees per million and transaction-fee revenue versus ADV, next local results date 29 October; competitor fee yield and monthly FINRA activity provide independent context. This is observable within two quarters, so Rule 4 does not add another size reduction.

The August report explicitly associates fast-growing portfolio trading with lower fee yield. Network participation is a reason customers use the venue, not proof it can retain today's toll. The near-decile valuation can therefore be a rational discount for fee compression; the positive operating record supports a small purchase, not a claim that the risk has gone away. Canton-related earnings, acquisition accounting, controlling-shareholder relationships and missing standard ROIC all weaken the valuation evidence.

Combined exposure: no TW position in the public human-book instrument list, so existing direct human-book weight is 0%. This adds a US Financial Services holding to a book already 66.72% US and 7.57% Financial Services, while avoiding another direct megacap-tech position. holdings, signals book. AZN.L — AstraZeneca

What it does: AstraZeneca researches, develops and sells prescription medicines. Customers include healthcare systems and distributors; sales span oncology, cardiovascular and metabolic disease, respiratory disease and rare diseases. Annual results.

This run's ranking and allocation.

1. Order

BUY 1 AZN share on the London Stock Exchange through Trading 212 Invest, regular-session DAY limit 12,136 GBp (£121.36). Submit for 17 September 2026; expire unfilled at the close. Currency GBP; the quoted number is pence.

Allocation £125, half the £250 ceiling on £500 contributed under §7.2a. The research TTM now exists, but acquisition accounting distorts reported-history comparisons and only one annual Core observation is stored. Rule 4 is not an extra halving: the dominant cash risk is observable next quarter.

Trading 212 lists the London share; fees and tax schedule. Broker fees are 0%, tax separately 0.5%. Expected first-year buy-and-hold transaction/account costs are 0.5%, inside both cost rules. This is an ordinary share, with no ADR custody charge. Execution spread is controlled by the limit rather than assumed zero.

One share uses 97.09% of the allocation, leaving £3.64 before tax, or £3.03 after it. Two shares exceed the reduced allocation. Concentration is 24.27% of contributed capital, with no cap exception. Cash after this ticket alone is £235.23; cash after all three tickets is £34.81. The account debit must remain within £125. Pot book, local prices.

2. Thesis

The business has grown annual revenue from $45.811bn in 2023 to $58.739bn in 2025, with established marketed medicines rather than a single development-stage asset doing the earning (local years). The FY2025 issuer statement reports operating profit of $13.743bn, a 23.40% margin, making the question whether reinvestment produces durable cash returns, not whether the business has yet become profitable (annual release). My inference is that established-product growth merits a small holding at the current valuation, while the cash consumed by buying and developing the next products is the test that can invalidate it.

3. Falsifier

Define cash after reinvestment as reported operating cash inflow minus cash purchases of property, plant and equipment and intangible assets. This is an analyst measure, not company free cash flow; show acquisition and contingent-consideration payments separately so shifting expenditure between categories cannot hide it.

Warning: Already active. H1 cash after reinvestment was $1.581bn, or 5.15% of revenue, below my 8% warning line; operating cash was 83.99% of reported operating profit. At nine-month results, locally dated 30 October 2026, re-read if the first ratio stays below 8%, or operating cash flow falls year on year while Core operating profit rises. Either warns independently. H1 cash-flow and income statements.

Break: At FY2026 results, reviewed by 1 March 2027, sell under §5.1 if full-year cash after reinvestment is below 5% of revenue, or operating cash flow is below 80% of reported operating profit. Non-positive reported operating profit also breaks. These are independent analyst decision rules, not management guidance. Use the full year for the hard cash test to avoid turning H1 investment seasonality into a false sale. Explain material acquisitions and disposal proceeds; missing fields require review, not a green result.

Both tiers can deteriorate while Core EPS grows. They test growth that fails to fund itself, rather than substituting a guidance miss for that risk.

4. Review date

2 November 2026, following the locally dated nine-month release. The warning is accepted at entry and should remain visible in intervening reviews.

5. Numbers as of today

Local check: H1 revenue and operating profit agree with the sum of the two local quarters. FY2025 operating profit disagrees: local $13.327bn versus issuer $13.743bn; use the issuer's 23.40% margin, not the local 22.69%. FY2024 also differs: issuer $10.003bn versus local $10.251bn; the issuer-comparable margin rises from 18.50% to 23.40%. The stored ROIC is quoted as a local screening metric, not independently certified from a corrected operating-profit series. FY2025 reported EPS $6.60 in the issuer summary is basic; local $6.54 is diluted, so those are different bases rather than an unexplained discrepancy.

The old acquisition-amortisation burden made historical reported P/E high. Cash cheapness corroborates today's filter but annual OCF does not see the latest investment spending. Core EPS also excludes more than amortisation; its lower multiple is not automatically owner earnings. No reported or vendor historical percentile is assigned to Core EPS.

Adjustments: no duplicate appended. Existing AZN.L ledger contains FY2025 Core EPS $9.16, Q3 $2.38, Q4 $2.12 and H1 2026 $5.21, with Q2 separately recorded. The pipeline uses contiguous periods without double-counting H1 and Q2. Existing disposal/contingent-consideration gains remain arithmetic:false. One annual Core period is sourced; a comparable rolling historical Core percentile is not available.

Why this is not 7532.T again: the purchase separates existing product earnings from pipeline hopes, compares both cash and earnings valuations, discloses the accounting discrepancy and explicitly prices a cash-conversion warning into a half allocation. GBP quotation does not remove the company's international currency exposure.

6. The case against

Theses: none. T1–T3 do not supply a material thesis for owning this pharmaceutical business.

Dominant risk (financial): product growth requires increasingly costly reinvestment and fails to deliver cash available to shareholders.

Earliest observable: the next year-to-date cash-flow statement, locally 30 October 2026; the H1 warning has already fired.

Patents and regulatory exclusivity can sustain product margins for a time, but expiry, competing therapies and failed trials force continuing investment. The apparent margin improvement can therefore coexist with weaker economics. Other risks include pricing regulation, litigation and FX; the half allocation is not an assertion that a diversified pipeline eliminates them.

Combined exposure: existing direct AZN human-book weight is 0%, checked against the public instrument list. This adds Healthcare to a book with 0.88% Healthcare and 6.19% Europe under the Scan's classifications; the company itself is global, not a pure UK exposure. holdings, signals book.

Do not increase the limit to chase the separate $106 after-hours flag in prices.json.

2. Thesis

Tradeweb monetises institutional trading activity, and local annual operating margins rose from 37.0% in 2023 to 41.2% in 2025 while revenue grew. August's fully electronic US credit volume increased 32.5%, giving a current business reason to investigate continued adoption beyond a low multiple (August activity). My inference is that this adoption and recurring execution revenue deserve a small position while fee retention is tested, with Canton investment gains excluded from the earnings case.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At Q3 results, locally dated 29 October 2026, re-read if cash-credit variable fees per million fall more than 15% year on year, or if either fully electronic US high-grade or high-yield TRACE share falls at least one percentage point below the Q2 baselines of 19.0% and 8.5%. Either route warns independently. Q2 cash-credit fee decline was 11.4%; these thresholds are my decision rules, not management guidance. Q2 release.

Break: By 1 March 2027, after Q3 and Q4, sell under §5.1 if credit revenue declines year on year in both quarters despite positive fully electronic US credit volume growth, or if the same high-grade or high-yield fully electronic share is below its Q2 baseline by two percentage points in both quarters. This tests lost monetisation and lost customers separately; rising total revenue cannot hide either. Use the same share methodology and restated comparators; unavailable data triggers a re-read, never a pass.

External check: FINRA TRACE publishes prior-month market volumes on the third business day, next 5 October for September. Compare the market with Tradeweb's corresponding monthly credit volumes, preserving single/double-counting conventions. This is a market-growth cross-check, not an independently reconstructed Tradeweb share. Review by 9 October if one series is delayed. MarketAxess's Q2 release reports portfolio-trading ADV up 33% and credit fees per million down 7%; it also suspends monthly releases after the ICE agreement. Its next disclosure has no promised monthly date. Do not wait for a fictitious August competitor release.

4. Review date

9 October 2026, then 30 October 2026, irrespective of price. Test the two-quarter break by 1 March 2027.

Local ni $181.318m is attributable income; nic $181.274m reflects the common-share allocation. Neither is consolidated net income $206.686m. The Scan's comparison of research P/E with a vendor recurring floor mixes bases; I do not use it as a research percentile. One cited adjusted annual period and four quarters are stored. No adjusted historical percentile is certified.

Adjustments: Existing TW FY2025 Canton gain $270.9m and Q2 2026 minority-investment gain $26.6m remain evidence-only. Existing issuer-adjusted quarters total $3.79 and reconcile to the checked Q2 source. No new TW adjustment is needed; no entry was duplicated. Ledger.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: the argument uses operating margins, cash and paid transaction activity, with explicit fee/share tests. It does not assume higher trading volumes automatically improve shareholder economics. Missing ROIC is a limitation, and the size reflects it.

6. The case against

Theses: none. Tradeweb's transaction pricing is not the seat-priced workflow rent T2 targets; T1 and T3 are not material premises of this purchase.

Dominant risk (competitive): stronger rival execution networks and price competition take clients or force Tradeweb to give away the economics of growing volume.

Earliest observable: September credit participation against FINRA's October volume release, followed by Q3 fee and share disclosures on the locally recorded 29 October date. The competitor's next monthly release is unavailable because the series was suspended.

The announced ICE/MarketAxess combination may strengthen distribution and bundling; adoption alone does not rebut that. Non-GAAP earnings also exclude real compensation and acquisition costs. A 27.49× adjusted multiple needs sustained earnings growth even after the reported screen says cheap. Net margins should not be mistaken for returns on the large acquired asset base.

Combined exposure: TW has no direct position in the human book, confirmed from holdings.json, so its existing direct weight is 0%. It adds US financial-market exposure to an already predominantly US book; signals.json remains the percentage exposure source. A combined GBP weight cannot be calculated from public percentages alone.

Broker schedule; HMRC foreign-share treatment. The quoted broker schedule identifies no German purchase levy. The market spread is unknown, with the limit bounding execution. No flat fee argues for more shares. Cash after all three proposals: £42.63.

2. Thesis

Eckert & Ziegler has an existing profitable supply business rather than a pre-revenue drug-development bet, with local annual revenue and capital productivity improving through 2025. H1 Medical earnings held up as Lutetium-177 revenue more than tripled and contract manufacturing revenue nearly doubled, providing a company-specific reason to investigate the new Sweep lead (H1 report). My inference is that the market may be underestimating this mix change when it sees flat headline revenue, although neither EU policy nor the apparent historical discount establishes the return on new capacity.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At Q3 results, locally dated 12 November 2026, re-read if nine-month operating cash flow divided by consolidated profit is below 60%, or Medical adjusted EBIT divided by Medical segment assets falls more than 15% year on year on matched nine-month periods. These are analyst thresholds. H1 CFO/profit is already 56.96%, so the cash warning is active before entry; the purchase accepts that warning at reduced size.

Break: At FY2026 results, review by 31 March 2027, sell under §5.1 if full-year operating cash flow is below 50% of consolidated profit, or if full-year Medical adjusted EBIT divided by Medical segment assets declines more than 25% year on year. Either route breaks independently. Use positive profit denominators; a consolidated loss also breaks. Use the issuer's consistently defined segment assets at each year end, with any restatement applied to both sides; missing segment assets means unavailable, not a pass.

Cash collection and segment profit earned per euro of assets can deteriorate while revenue still grows. These tests therefore answer the stated capital-return risk. The cash thresholds use the reported cash flow, with no repeat of the previous licence receipt assumed. Sources and starting figures: H1 statement and segment note. The annual review deadline is an analyst deadline, not a claimed confirmed release date.

4. Review date

Dominant risk (financial): expansion ties up more capital than the Medical business earns back, while licence receipts make cash generation appear more recurring than it is.

Earliest observable: the weak cash ratio is visible now; the next cash-flow and segment-asset update is expected at the locally recorded 12 November result. Rule 4 requires no additional reduction because the test is observable within two quarters.

Flat aggregate Medical sales can coexist with fast growth in small product lines. Industrial demand and the product mix may weaken further, and supply projects invite competing capacity. The Pentixapharm financing relationship remains a capital-allocation risk. The market may be correctly pricing those issues; an apparent half-price historical multiple is not a rebuttal.

At the 29 October Q3 result, also warn if cash-credit variable fees per million decline by more than 15% year on year, or credit revenue is flat/down despite rising credit ADV. Break: At Q3 and then Q4 results, reviewed no later than 28 February 2027, either (a) fully electronic high-grade share below 17% in two successive monthly releases, or (b) credit revenue declining year on year in two successive quarters while credit ADV rises in each, breaks the execution-economics thesis under §5.1. A separate route is two consecutive quarterly GAAP operating margins below 35%: this catches deterioration outside credit. Do not require all three routes to fire.

Use Tradeweb monthly reports for share and quarterly results for fees/revenue. Cross-check the market denominator against FINRA TRACE monthly volume reports, published on the third business day after month-end, keeping the same bond/venue coverage. FINRA aggregate volume alone is not an independent Tradeweb share estimate.

External competitor evidence already bites: MarketAxess reports Q2 credit fees per million $129 versus $138, and has suspended monthly volume releases following its announced ICE transaction (competitor result). Review its quarterly filings while available and ICE's transaction updates at each monthly checkpoint; no invented August comparator. Missing disclosure triggers a re-read, not a pass.

4. Review date

2026-10-08, then 2026-10-30 after the issuer-confirmed 29 October results. The final two-quarter checkpoint is 2027-02-28.

Local FY2025 ni is $812.792m but nic is $812.156m; the issuer's attributable income is the former, while consolidated income is $921.500m (recorded source reconciliation). I do not treat these as interchangeable. The stored quarterly reported EPS sum to $4.18, versus the quote's $4.19; valuation above retains the quote and labels the separate research denominator. No hidden adjustment resolves either difference.

Adjustments: Rechecked the already recorded TW Q2 2026 company-adjusted EPS $0.97 and the $26.6m gross minority-investment gain, evidence only, against the issuer release. No duplicate appended. The ledger contains one adjusted annual period, FY2025, and four consecutive adjusted quarters through June 2026. Company-adjusted excludes compensation/acquisition and other charges too; it is not independently reconstructed owner earnings. The reported historical percentile is not a research percentile. §7.2a prices that remaining uncertainty through size.

Why this is not 7532.T again: The claim rests on a multiyear operating record and explicit fee/share tests. Rising trading volume is insufficient if monetisation fails; neither a technology story nor the low percentile overrides that.

6. The case against

Theses: T2, automation can lower the price of execution and associated workflow services even while activity grows; Tradeweb's transaction business is an adjacent exposure, not a pure seat-licence business. T1's model-price thesis and T3's mandated-control thesis are not material premises here.

Dominant risk (competitive): Rivals and cheaper automated protocols take fee income faster than electronic trading expands the addressable activity.

Earliest observable: September market share, checked by 8 October, followed by Q3 fee yield and credit revenue on 29 October. The competitor fee decline above is already an external observation. ICE's announced acquisition of MarketAxess proposes combining execution with data and analytics; it is pending, and its competitive benefit is not yet established.

August portfolio trading grew faster than overall credit trading and carries lower fees (August release). This could leave volume strong while economics weaken, which is why P3 tests both. The reported multiple is 56.3% below its own historical median, but part of that apparent discount comes from investment gains. T2 may explain another part: I am buying a small test of operating growth at 26.77× adjusted earnings, not asserting a return to the old 55.44× reported median. The fee decline is evidence against that test.

Combined exposure: No TW listing appears in public holdings, so direct human-book exposure is 0%; this adds financial-market activity to a human book already 66.95% US (signals.json). That overlap disclosure does not alter the rank.

A high margin is not treated as a moat. Tradeweb's fee yield can decline as its cheaper protocols grow; AstraZeneca has to keep buying and developing the next medicine. Those are the risks tested in the orders, rather than assumed away. Capital metrics missing for AstraZeneca and Experian have not been filled with operating margins.

Why the next pound stays in cash

MWA: The business remains a credible holding, but the latest quarterly release still attributes growth to price while consolidated volumes declined slightly. GAAP operating profit is $80.6m, not the larger figure before reorganisation charges. With new names funded first under §4.5a, I require the next volume and cash bridge before adding to this existing risk. The November checkpoint is a positive-evidence requirement for a top-up, not a finding that the held thesis is broken.

Experian: This is the closest unbought fresh candidate. The local 23.54× reported P/E is 36.5% below its 37.0703× median over 221 weeks from 2022-07-01. Translating the local share price to USD, while leaving issuer EPS unchanged, gives 23.50× FY2026 diluted reported EPS $1.634 and 21.49× Benchmark diluted EPS $1.787. The latter is already recorded, with FY2025, in the adjustment ledger; neither creates an adjusted historical percentile. Local FY2026 revenue $8.445bn, operating profit $2.045bn and attributable income $1.502bn agree with the issuer accounts, although the local annual EPS cell is absent. The issuer reports 17.2% adjusted ROCE, a different measure from missing local ROIC, and 93% Benchmark cash conversion.

The case for buying is Q1 9% B2B organic growth (Q1 update). The case against is a change in who collects the analytics and distribution margin: T2 is a possible reason for the discount itself. FICO's 13 August announcement says participants in its direct-licence programme represent 73.1% of mortgage reseller volume; that measures the participating network, not actual migrated transactions (FICO). The threat is already organised, even if revenue recognition lags adoption. FHFA's 9 September expansion of VantageScore eligibility changes score choice but explicitly does not initially change report requirements. This supports continued demand for underlying credit data, not necessarily the same resale markup or analytics pricing.

I cannot yet argue convincingly that a 36.5% de-rating overstates that economic change. Wait for the 18 November H1 result, the local calendar date, to assess the revenue/pricing bridge alongside direct-distribution adoption. If paying usage or retention remains unreported, that is not a green light. A future proposal could use the Rule 4 half size rather than veto the data gap; today's decision is that B2B growth alone does not rebut the price of disintermediation. No new adjustment was found beyond the already stored financing gain and Benchmark annual EPS.

UNFI: The new Sweep candidate trades locally at 33.17× reported EPS $1.34, versus 36.34× vendor recurring. It is at the 97.12th percentile of 104 profitable weeks from 2022-11-04, an indicative window. Its latest release confirms FY2026 EPS $1.34, whereas local annual accounts still end in FY2025 losses. Issuer-adjusted FY2026 EPS $2.65 gives 16.77× at the local price: a meaningful alternative, explicitly distinct from reported and forward earnings. That annual figure and Q4 $0.69, with their issuer comparatives, were appended to the adjustment ledger; two nonconsecutive quarters do not establish research TTM or adjusted history. Sales still fell 2.0% despite the cash repair. My rejection is that this price demands a durable operational recovery before underlying growth is established, not that the earnings data are incomplete; no adjusted historical decile is invented to override that judgement.

These decisions leave cash intentionally. The rule permits up to three proposals, not three obligatory purchases.

The normal £250 ceiling is halved to £125 under §7.2a: Core EPS is materially above reported EPS, no adjusted rolling history is certified, and local quarter/half-year EPS disagree. The £120 position is 24% of £500 contributed. No one-share cap exception is required. Two shares fit the unreduced ceiling but not this reduced allocation; zero commission gives no cost reason to double it.

2. Thesis

AstraZeneca has grown revenue and reported operating profit across four local fiscal years, with the most recent full-year operating margin above its earlier levels (local accounts). H1 Oncology growth of 15% at constant exchange rates, across the company's largest therapy area, makes the case broader than one newly approved medicine (H1 summary). My hypothesis is that the established medicine portfolio and successive launches can keep expanding the earning base; I assign no forecast sales to the Sweep's camizestrant catalyst, and require the cash retained after investment to demonstrate whether that growth creates shareholder value.

3. Falsifier

Define cash after investment as net cash from operating activities minus purchases of property, plant and equipment minus purchases of intangible assets, using the issuer cash-flow statement. It is a deliberately demanding analytical measure, not company-defined free cash flow; acquisitions and financing flows remain separate.

Warning: At the 30 October 2026 nine-month result, re-read if this cash measure is below 5% of nine-month revenue, or operating cash flow divided by reported operating profit is below 85%. H1 baselines are 5.15% and 83.99%: the latter is already a warning, not a newly discovered future trigger. The present proposal explicitly accepts that warning at half size; failure to improve at the next result requires a fresh decision. These are my thresholds, not management guidance.

Break: At FY2026 results, checked no later than 28 February 2027, cash after investment at or below zero, or operating cash flow below 70% of reported operating profit, breaks the cash-funded growth thesis under §5.1. Either route suffices, irrespective of Core EPS growth. Also break if reported operating profit is non-positive. A one-period investment surge can trigger this rule even with a promising pipeline; that is the chosen protection against continuously buying growth that fails to fund itself.

The cash-flow statement supplies each field. Compare like periods, retain the stated accounting basis and explain acquisitions separately. A missing field is unavailable evidence and triggers review, never an assumed pass.

4. Review date

2026-11-02, immediately after the issuer-confirmed 30 October Q3 result, regardless of price. Full-year deadline: 2027-02-28; that is my review deadline, not a claimed company announcement date.

6. The case against

Theses: none.

Dominant risk (financial): Growth requires enough continuing investment in drug assets and working capital that rising accounting earnings fail to produce cash for shareholders.

Earliest observable: Nine-month operating cash flow and purchases of tangible/intangible assets on 30 October 2026; P3 already recognises the weak H1 conversion.

Core EPS excludes costs that can recur economically. Patent expiry, pricing pressure and failed trials can make continued investment necessary merely to replace lost sales; an attractive reported historical comparison does not remove those risks. The absence of local capital-return metrics leaves an important part of §2.4 unproven, so the business is not described as a certified high-ROIC compounder. 2. Thesis

Tradeweb sells execution across an existing network, and local FY2023–25 revenue rose from $1.338bn to $2.052bn while operating margin rose from 37.05% to 41.18%, making operating scale the business case rather than a low multiple. August ADV was still growing 13.7% year on year, giving the next quarter a measurable activity base without assuming that every dollar of volume earns the same fee (August release). With the reported multiple 56.3% below its reported historical median, the market may be pricing T2's erosion of paid workflow economics; my narrower reason to judge part of that discount excessive is the observed operating-profit conversion alongside a second subscription revenue stream, while persistence of those economics remains the proposition P3 tests, not a premise.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At Q3 results, locally dated 29 October 2026, re-read if cash-credit variable fees per million fall 15% or more year on year, or the growth gap between total ADV and transaction-fee revenue exceeds 15 percentage points. Q2 baselines are a 11.4% cash-credit fee decline and 18.2% versus 8.3% ADV/transaction-fee growth. These are my thresholds, not company guidance; mix can cause a warning without proving lost pricing. In the same review, compare MarketAxess's quarterly fee yield, which fell 7% in total credit in Q2, to distinguish an industry shift from a Tradeweb-specific loss.

Break: Assess Q3 and Q4 separately, no later than 1 March 2027. Either transaction-fee revenue is flat or falling year on year in both quarters while ADV grows in each, or GAAP operating margin falls below 35% in both quarters. Either route independently breaks the investment case under §5.1; require neither a share loss nor both routes together. Missing metrics trigger investigation, not a green result. Q2 10-Q definitions and baselines.

4. Review date

30 October 2026, regardless of price. Check the results calendar beforehand; the deadline stands if the release moves. The fee-risk observable is quarterly, within two quarters, so Rule 4 adds no further haircut.

6. The case against

Theses: T2 bears on automated trading workflows and the price clients pay for execution; T1 is an indirect potential accelerator through cheaper automation, not evidence of lost fees; T3 has no separately demonstrated revenue contribution here.

Dominant risk (competitive): Automated, lower-fee execution substitutes for higher-fee activity, so volume grows while the economic return to the platform shrinks.

Earliest observable: Quarterly fee yield and transaction revenue in Tradeweb's 10-Q, next expected 29 October; MarketAxess's next quarterly fee release is the external comparison, reviewed by 15 November even if its date moves. MWA — Mueller Water Products

What it does: Mueller sells valves, hydrants, meters and other equipment used in water networks. Municipal utilities and construction customers buy its products to maintain or expand water systems. Company description and latest results.

Run report and complete ranking. Written 14 September 2026, 00:38 UTC. This is a top-up, not a new position or an instruction to sell the three shares already held.

1. Order

BUY 5 additional shares of MWA on the NYSE, limit $23.94, regular session only, valid through 18 September 2026. Currency USD. At USD1.3518 per GBP, deploy £88.55 of a £98.44 allocation, leaving £9.89 of that allocation unused before costs. Cancel rather than chase.

The pot already holds three shares. Conservatively marking those at the same limit uses £53.13 of the £250 maximum on £500 contributed, leaving £196.87 headroom. Halve that headroom under §7.2a to £98.44, because tariff benefits remain unquantified and the local operating-income classification is too generous. Five shares fit; six cost £106.26 and do not. The resulting eight-share position is approximately £141.68, 28.34% of contributed capital, below the 50% cap. No exception is needed.

§4.5a allocation: Tradeweb and Experian receive the first two allocations as fresh pot names. Their proposed sizes already reflect their own earnings and observable-risk haircuts; unused cash is not a reason to override those. MWA receives the third slot because its improving multi-year operating and capital returns support a modest addition, while the alternatives in the ranking either need a business repair or have a dated reason to wait. This does not take MWA to its cap.

Broker: Trading 212 Invest, with MWA availability confirmed. Commission £0, custody £0 and FX 0.15% give about £0.13 entry cost. No ADR fee and £0 US-share purchase tax under HMRC's foreign-share treatment. Expected first-year charges including conversion of dividends at the trailing yield are approximately 0.152% of the ticket, below both cost limits. A same-value sale with GBP conversion adds 0.15%; buying more shares does not lower the percentage. Spread is not known before execution; the price limit controls the entry. This order alone leaves about £358.63 cash after entry FX; all three proposals leave £172.20.

2. Thesis

Mueller's local FY2023–25 revenue increased from $1.276bn to $1.430bn, while operating income rose from $137.6m to $269.4m, a change in operating conversion that precedes the latest tax benefit (earnings.json). Local ROIC improved from 8.39% to 13.12% over those years, so there is evidence that higher margins have reached invested capital, although asset turnover declined (prices.json). My inference is that repeat network maintenance and better production economics can sustain a more profitable business than the old margin history suggests; declining physical volumes and slowing asset use are the opposing evidence, not assumed away by infrastructure spending.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At the FY2026 release, locally estimated 5 November 2026, re-read if the sales bridge again identifies declining consolidated physical volumes, or if full-year free cash flow is 70% or less of company-adjusted net income, missing management's stated conversion objective. Also warn if trailing GAAP operating income divided by average opening/closing total assets falls below 13%. That asset-return measure is pre-tax operating return on assets, not ROIC; calculate it directly from filed annual/quarterly accounts, without annualising a single quarter.

Break: At the first two results following this proposed purchase, checked no later than 28 February 2027, any of these independent routes calls for exit under §5.1: two consecutive quarters of falling consolidated volume with GAAP operating margin below 18% in each; GAAP operating margin below 16% in either quarter; or trailing GAAP operating income over average total assets below 11%. The last two tests stand alone so that price increases cannot keep a failing physical/asset business green indefinitely. These are my decision thresholds, not management guidance. Missing volumes or asset balances mean unobservable, not a pass. Use operating income after reorganisation charges.

These tests govern this proposed addition if accepted. The latest Review correctly retains the accepted September 8 thesis for the existing three shares; this file does not silently rewrite that accepted contract. Acceptance of a common position-level monitoring contract needs to be recorded explicitly.

4. Review date

10 November 2026, regardless of price. Check the estimated results date before then. The next filing can test volumes, cash and asset returns within two quarters, so Rule 4 needs no separate slow-risk cut.

5. Numbers as of today

Market snapshot: 11 September regular close at 20:00:02 UTC, fetched locally 14 September 00:33:25 UTC.

Local check: Price, revenue and reported EPS are locally covered. The $11.2m operating-income difference matches reorganisation and other charges in the issuer reconciliation; use filed $80.6m for current margin and falsifiers. The local annual trend and FY2025 capital measures are labelled local references, not independently certified adjusted history. Zero completed fiscal years have cited MWA adjustments; the recorded $0.06 belongs to the still-current FY2026. The own-basis multiple removes only that benefit and is not a fully normalised history. No percentile is attached to it.

Adjustments: Existing MWA FY2026 $0.06/share tax benefit and directly reported June 2025/June 2026 adjusted EPS are retained. The release does not separately quantify the tariff refund, so no new arithmetic entry can honestly be appended. This is the reason for the half allocation, not a reason to substitute the higher local margin.

6. The case against

Theses: none.

Dominant risk (financial): Physical demand weakens while the expanded asset base earns less; prices and one-off benefits temporarily conceal that deterioration.

Earliest observable: The next quarterly sales bridge, filed operating profit, cash flow and balance sheet, expected with FY2026 results around 5 November. P3 tests asset returns independently as well as volumes and margins, addressing the weakness identified by the latest Review.

Margins have improved but asset turnover has fallen from 0.848× in FY2023 to 0.777× in FY2025; pricing cannot be treated as evidence that capacity is productively used. Current tariff and tax benefits make extrapolating the latest quarter especially risky. A top-up before a post-entry report also increases exposure without new evidence since the original purchase; the reduced size and preference for the two new names are deliberate costs of that uncertainty.

The published signals.book rolls MWA into its small-name tail. A read-only check of decrypted holdings.json confirms its entire MWA quantity equals the three pot shares: separate human-only MWA exposure is 0%. The aggregate-book MWA weight is 0.0413%, calculated with the same price/FX method as the Scan. The purchase increases an existing pot holding and the 66.89% US exposure of the published book (signals.json). No private book amount is reproduced. Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: the case requires measured capital returns and explicit volume/cash tests; neither a water-spending narrative nor a reported earnings windfall is accepted as proof.

model: gpt-6-astra, lane: deepdive, 2026-09-14 00:33, 16m20s, 3,789,976 tokens (197,109 fresh, 3,566,464 cached, 26,403 out), stamped from the session log rather than self-reported

EXPN.L — Experian

What it does: Experian collects credit and other consumer and business data. It sells reports, analytics and decision services to lenders and other organisations, and provides consumers with credit information and marketplaces. FY2026 results.

Run report and complete ranking. Written 14 September 2026, 00:38 UTC.

1. Order

BUY 4 shares of EXPN on the London Stock Exchange, local symbol EXPN.L, limit 2,782p (£27.82), regular session only, valid through 18 September 2026. This deploys £111.28 of a £125 allocation, leaving £13.72 of that allocation unused. Currency GBp, settled in GBP; no foreign-currency conversion on the purchase. Cancel rather than chase.

The £250 normal maximum is halved under Rule 4 because company-wide paid decision volumes and retention have no reliable dated disclosure: the financial and external tests below are incomplete proxies for substitution. The uncertified adjusted earnings history under §7.2a also supports this same half allocation; no full-size override is claimed. The position uses 22.26% of £500 contributed capital. Five shares cost £139.10 and do not fit the reduced allocation. No cap exception is needed.

Use Trading 212 Invest, where EXPN is listed. Commission and custody are free; entry FX is £0. Purchase tax: £0 expected for the electronic transfer. Experian's specific shareholder tax guidance states that UK/Irish stamp duty and UK SDRT should not apply, subject to its stated exception for a UK-executed instrument of transfer. This is a listing-specific exception to the brief's generic UK-share 0.5% example; do not charge a tax solely because the listing is London. HMRC distinguishes UK-register and foreign shares.

Expected first-year explicit charges are less than £0.01, allowing 0.15% FX on USD dividends at the local trailing yield, approximately 0.003% of the ticket. No ADR custody fee, and a larger ticket brings no fee advantage. Bid–ask spread is not separately measurable before a quote; the limit caps the share price. Both cost gates pass. This order alone leaves £336.03 of current cash before negligible dividend FX; all three proposals leave approximately £172.20 after entry costs.

2. Thesis

Experian's existing credit-data and decision businesses produced growing revenue with local statutory operating margins of 23.87%, 23.83% and 24.22% in FY2024–26, while its latest trading update reports 9% global B2B organic growth (Q1 FY2027 update). The market may be discounting both weaker lending activity and T2's loss of paid workflow value: the local reported multiple is 38.1% below its 37.17× historical median, a large reduction for a business still growing its core B2B revenue. My reason for judging part of that discount excessive is narrower than an AI-proof moat: Fannie Mae's current implementation still requires tri-merge reports even as scoring models compete, giving the underlying credit-data franchise a present contractual use that a cheaper interface does not itself remove; permanence of that protection is tested below.

3. Falsifier

Warning: Review on 19 November 2026, following the locally dated 18 November half-year results. Re-read if North America B2B organic growth is below 6%, or if Experian reports shrinking decision/report volumes, material customer losses or price concessions despite positive revenue. Also trigger an immediate review, checked at least monthly from 14 October, if FHFA or Fannie Mae gives optional bi-merge an effective implementation date: removing one bureau report per mortgage changes demand even while revenue can be supported by prices.

Break: By 31 May 2027, or earlier when disclosed, exit under §5.1 if Experian identifies lost/repriced data or decision contracts causing at least 5% of annual B2B revenue loss, or if two non-overlapping reported periods show non-positive North America B2B organic growth while Equifax USIS Diversified Markets remains positive. Either route is sufficient; do not double-count a half-year and a quarter inside it. The 5% and 6% thresholds are my decision rules, not guidance. Separately, two comparable half-years with statutory operating margin below 20% break the claimed earning quality even if the external comparison stays positive.

The direct unit/customer test is incomplete because disclosures are discretionary; a missing number is unobservable, not a pass. Equifax's 6% Q2 Diversified Markets growth is a comparator, not an agent-adoption measure. Mortgage report policy is externally observable on an event cadence but covers only part of Experian. That limitation is why the order is halved. Existing disclosure gap.

4. Review date

19 November 2026, regardless of price, with the first external policy check by 14 October 2026. If the half-year date changes, keep the review date and explicitly mark unavailable evidence.

5. Numbers as of today

Local market snapshot: fetch 14 September 00:33:25 UTC, regular quote struck 11 September at 15:47:19 UTC. Reporting currency is USD; quote currency is GBp.

Local check: Revenue and both income figures agree. The local annual row lacks FY2026 EPS even though the issuer supplies it; the quote's 121p is a separate, rounded native-currency trailing field and gives a slightly different multiple. Use USD1.787 annual Benchmark diluted EPS, never the headline basic figure, for the company-adjusted comparison. Two cited annual adjusted years and zero quarterly research periods exist; no adjusted historical percentile is claimed. The 38.1% de-rating compares reported with reported, not the Benchmark multiple with the reported median. The ongoing-activities Benchmark margin is a different perimeter from statutory total operating margin.

Adjustments: Existing EXPN.L FY2025/26 Benchmark diluted annual EPS and the FY2026 $101m gross financing remeasurement gain were rechecked and retained. No new EXPN entry is needed. The latter remains arithmetic:false; four USD quarters must not be fed into a pipeline expecting GBp EPS. No annual figure was annualised from a quarter.

6. The case against

Theses: T2 threatens paid decision/workflow products even if raw data remains needed; T1 lowers the cost of competing analytics; T3 offers identity/governance demand, but no quantified incremental profit is assumed.

Dominant risk (secular): Customers need fewer paid reports or decision services as alternative scoring, agent workflows and reporting-rule changes reduce the value of the current bundle.

Earliest observable: FHFA/Fannie Mae policy changes, monitored monthly and when published; the next company half-year volume/customer commentary on the local 18 November date. A comprehensive dated unit series does not exist, so the risk cannot be certified away within two quarters.

The current tri-merge requirement is changeable and protects only one use case. Revenue growth can conceal price increases against declining units; that is why P3 includes policy and customer-loss routes rather than simply another revenue forecast. Acquisitions and adjusted earnings exclusions also make management's capital-return measure more flattering than the missing local measures might prove. The market's de-rating could therefore be correct; the small initial allocation buys a testable business case, not certainty about an AI moat.

Direct human-book EXPN weight is 0%. Although the local geography labels this Europe, Experian's latest update attributes 67% of group revenue to North America, so the purchase adds economically to a book already 66.89% US (company update, signals.json). Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: no AI product launch or credit-cycle rebound is treated as earnings; the case uses the existing business, separately labelled accounts and a half-size order that admits the substitution test's limits.

model: claude-opus-5, lane: deepdive, 2026-09-13 18:23, 15m08s, 12,739,545 tokens (798,067 fresh, 11,782,342 cached, 159,136 out), stamped from the session log rather than self-reported

TW — Tradeweb Markets Inc.

Ranked first in the run report for this cycle, which accounts for all 93 watchlist names.

What it does: Tradeweb runs electronic marketplaces where institutions trade bonds, interest-rate swaps, ETFs and money-market instruments. Asset managers, hedge funds, insurers and central banks sit on one side and dealer banks on the other, and Tradeweb matches them through a set of trading protocols — request-for-quote, click-to-trade, portfolio trading and session-based auctions. It earns a fee on each executed trade, mostly variable and scaled to the notional amount traded, plus smaller fixed subscription and market-data fees.

1. Order

BUY 1 share of TW on Nasdaq, limit $102.00. Currency USD. £75.39 deployed at the limit, £74.97 at Friday's close, against a reduced allocation of £62.50. Cash left idle from this ticket: none — one share costs more than the allocation. Pot cash after this and the EXPN.L order: £315.54.

Expected first-year costs. Broker assumed is Trading 212, which lists TW and is the §10 default wherever it can trade a name.

ItemAmount% of ticket
Commission£0.000.00%
FX conversion, 0.15% GBP→USD£0.110.15%

US dividend withholding, 15% under W-8BEN on ~£0.40 of dividends£0.060.08%
§4.1 first-year total (under 2%)£0.170.23% — clears

Withholding is a tax and is stated separately from the broker-fee gate, per §4.1a. Trading 212's charge is proportional at any size, so buying more shares would not improve the cost ratio — the flat-fee consideration that applies to an IBKR ticket does not arise here.

Size, and why it is half. The base allocation is £125. This ticket takes half under §7.2a: the reported trailing EPS of $4.19 that produces the headline 24.21× is not the $3.79 the company itself reports on an adjusted basis, a 10.5% difference in the denominator, and prices.json carries no ROIC and no gross profit over assets for TW at all. Two of the three things §2.4 asks about the capital are simply not visible, so the position is smaller rather than the argument louder.

One share at £75.39 exceeds the £62.50 half allocation. A fraction cannot be bought, so one share is the smallest placeable position — the same rounding-up logic §4.2a applies to the 50% cap, applied here to an allocation. No cap is in play: £75.39 is 15.1% of £500 contributed capital against a §4.2 ceiling of £250, and nothing needs to unwind. The overshoot is £12.89 and is disclosed rather than hidden by rounding the allocation up to meet it.

2. Thesis

Institutional fixed income is still moving off the telephone and onto screens, and Tradeweb is where a large share of that flow has gone: FY2025 revenue grew 18.92% to $2,052.4m and filed operating margin rose for a third consecutive year, 37.05% to 39.73% to 41.18%, which is growth and improving profitability at the same time rather than one bought with the other. Why now is that the market has re-rated the franchise from a 53.15–66.39× band in FY2024 and 35.79–64.63× in FY2025 to 23.09–36.39× so far in FY2026, a halving of the multiple inside two fiscal years while those filed accounts were being produced. What the market may be missing is on the balance sheet rather than the income statement: asset turnover rose from 0.237× to 0.251× as revenue grew 18.92%, so the network was extended without a proportionate call on capital — modest in absolute terms, but moving in the right direction in the one capital measure this company discloses.

3. Falsifier

Warning — at the Q3 2026 results, a confirmed date of 29 October 2026. Any one of these triggers a re-read, not a sale:

  • Transaction-fee revenue growth trails total ADV growth by 15 percentage points or more. The Q2 2026 baseline is ADV +18.2% against transaction-fee revenue +8.3%, a gap of about 10 points, so this asks whether an existing gap is widening.
  • Cash-credit fees per million fall 15% or more year on year. Q2 2026 was −11.4%.
  • Filed GAAP operating margin below 38%, against 41.18% in FY2025.

All three are revenue-per-unit-of-volume or profitability measures rather than market-share measures, deliberately: the dominant risk in P6 is that Tradeweb keeps winning the market while the toll on it shrinks, and a share statistic would stay green throughout that.

Break — assessed at the FY2026 10-K, checked no later than 1 March 2027. Either route alone calls for exit under §5.1, and they must not be required to fire together:

  • (a) Total transaction-fee revenue is flat or falling year on year in both Q3 and Q4 2026 while total ADV grows in each. That is the toll shrinking on a growing network, which is the dominant risk arriving in the accounts.
  • (b) Filed GAAP operating margin below 35% in both quarters, independent of volumes. This route exists so that growth in another asset class cannot conceal lost pricing in credit.

External evidence (Rule 3). The dominant risk is secular, so it is checked outside Tradeweb's own filings as well as inside them:

SourceMetricCadenceBaseline
MarketAxess quarterly resultstotal-credit fees per million, total commission revenue, portfolio-trading ADVquarterly, next checked by 15 November 2026Q2 2026: portfolio-trading ADV +33%, commission revenue −3%, total-credit fees per million −7%
FINRA TRACE volume reportsmarket-wide corporate bond volumemonthly, third business daythe independent denominator; Tradeweb's published shares are issuer estimates

MarketAxess's Q2 is the single most useful fact here and it cuts against this proposal: automation grew its activity 33% while the revenue it collected fell. Read the two firms' directions, never splice their fee levels into one series — the product mixes differ. If MarketAxess stops publishing because of the announced ICE transaction, that is unavailable evidence, not a pass, and it escalates to a re-read.

4. Review date

30 October 2026, the day after the confirmed Q3 release, regardless of price.

5. Numbers as of today

Local check: agree. Every figure above is the repo's own and none was overridden. The one disagreement worth naming is internal to the local data rather than against it: eps is $4.19 and researchEps is $3.79, because FY2025 and Q4 2025 carry large below-the-line investment gains — filed Q4 2025 GAAP EPS was $1.51 against $0.87 company-adjusted, and FY2025 net income of $812.8m sits against operating income of $845.1m, a conversion no ordinary tax rate produces. I size on 26.77×, the company-adjusted figure, and quote 24.21× only as the number the Scan's percentile was computed on. The 1.15th percentile belongs to the reported series and is not transferred to the adjusted denominator.

Adjustments: no new entry was writable in this run. adjustments.json already carries TW's four company-adjusted quarterly EPS figures under normalizedEps.TW, each with its Tradeweb release, and the FY2026 $26.6m gross minority-equity gain recorded with arithmetic: false as evidence rather than as a subtraction — it is a gross consolidated figure and cannot be removed dollar-for-dollar from after-tax income attributable to common shareholders. No Tradeweb release has been published since those entries were made on 13 September, so there is nothing new to reconcile. No research low or percentile is claimed: one adjusted TTM cannot replay a 261-week rolling denominator, so the historical distribution stays on the reported basis and is labelled as such wherever it appears above.

6. The case against

Theses: T2 bears, on its tailwind side — Tradeweb charges per unit of notional executed and has never sold a seat, which is T2's own description of who gets paid when buyers stop paying for seats. T1 and T3 do not bear: Tradeweb neither sells nor resells models, and it is not a governance vendor. A tailwind thesis is not a reason to buy and is declared here so it cannot quietly become one.

Dominant risk (secular): electronification compresses the price of an executed trade faster than it grows the volume executed, so Tradeweb can go on winning the market while the revenue per unit of what it wins falls — Q2 2026 already shows ADV +18.2% against transaction-fee revenue +8.3%, with cash-credit fees per million down 11.4%.

Earliest observable: the transaction-fee-to-ADV growth gap and cash-credit fees per million, in the Q3 release on 29 October 2026 — six weeks away and well inside two quarters, so Rule 4's timing reduction does not apply. The half size comes from §7.2a and the missing capital measures instead, as P1 states.

Then the secondary arguments, and they are not weak ones:

  • The trend is already against the thesis, not merely a risk to it. Fees per million have been falling for several quarters and MarketAxess's Q2 shows the same category-wide shape. A proposal that buys into a visible compression is betting that operating leverage outruns it — a bet the falsifier in P3 tests directly and which this document deliberately does not assert in P2.
  • Two of three capital measures are blank. Leo's §2.4 extension is explicit that a margin is profit over sales and he invests capital. For TW the repo gives only asset turnover, and at 0.251× that is low in absolute terms: the balance sheet is heavy with goodwill and intangibles from acquisitions, so a large part of the asset base is purchase accounting rather than working capital. I cannot say what the capital earns, and I have not substituted the 41.18% margin for it.
  • A 41% operating margin is a question, not a comfort. It has risen three years running in a business whose unit price is falling, which is exactly the combination that invites a competitor to price below it. The P3 break at 35% exists for that.
  • Related-party dependency. LSEG is both a large shareholder and a distribution and data partner. That relationship is a material part of how Tradeweb reaches customers and prices data, and its renewal terms are not a figure this repo carries.
  • Combined exposure with the human book: none. holdings.json holds no Tradeweb and no fixed-income venue. The nearest adjacencies are Blackrock at 1.86% and Visa at 1.28% of the book, both different businesses. This buy therefore adds a genuinely new exposure rather than doubling one, which is the one thing §3.3's warning about overlap is not triggered by here.
  • Concentration within the pot. At £75.39 this would be the pot's largest position at 15.1% of contributed capital, ahead of MWA's 10.6%. Inside every limit, and worth seeing.

Why this is not 7532.T again. That regret was a top-line rebound story bought without the fundamentals, the valuation, the forward outlook or the currency. Here the case is filed margin over three years, filed revenue growth, and the one capital measure the repo has; the valuation is a filter this name passed and is deliberately not the argument; the forward test is a dated company disclosure six weeks out; and the currency exposure is a straight USD ticket priced at a stated FX rate. What is genuinely uncertain — what the capital earns — is named in P1 and paid for with half the position rather than argued away.
