model: claude-opus-5, lane: deepdive, 2026-09-13 18:23, 15m08s, 12,739,545 tokens (798,067 fresh, 11,782,342 cached, 159,136 out), stamped from the session log rather than self-reported

Run report — two reduced orders, £315.54 cash retained

The run proposes 1 TW share and 2 EXPN.L shares. It declines the MWA top-up that the morning run made, and holds the rest of the cash against two dated events on 16 September. These are drafts for Leo to execute, not trades.

⚠ Do not execute these alongside the 08:30 drafts. Three unexecuted proposals from this morning name TW, EXPN.L and MWA. This run reaches the same two fresh names independently and sizes both smaller. If both sets are placed, the TW and EXPN.L positions are bought twice. Treat 2026-09-13-0830-TW and 2026-09-13-0830-EXPN.L as superseded by these, or place the earlier pair and discard these — not both.

What this run had to work with

InputState
Pot cash / contributed capital£447.32 / £500, positions, generated 18:09:16 UTC
Actual holding3 MWA shares, £71.28 cost. Pending drafts are not positions
Sweep18:18 UTC, no new candidate; the 08:13 sweep raised 6936.HK and EXPN.L
Review18:11 UTC, hold MWA, no instruction
Pricesprices.json 18:23:41 UTC, carrying Friday 11 September regular-session closes
Scansignals.json 18:23:42 UTC. VIX 15.84, 28 valuation signals, one drawdown (BBW), one review-due (MWA). No standing-order instruction
Universe93 watchlist names = 18 ranked + 75 excluded, each appearing exactly once

Nothing in the data has moved since the 08:22 run. It is Sunday, the closes are Friday's, the later Sweep added no name and the later Review changed no verdict. So this run's only real content is whether an independent ranking on the same evidence reaches the same place. It largely does, and the ranking below was rebuilt from prices.json and earnings.json rather than read off the morning's table. Where it differs is the allocation, and that difference is argued rather than inherited.

What this run decided, and where it departs

DecisionThis runThe 08:30 run
TWPROPOSE 1 share, £75.39 at limitPROPOSE 1 share, £75.39 at limit
EXPN.LPROPOSE 2 shares, £56.00 at limitPROPOSE 4 shares, £112.00
MWA top-upEXCLUDE for this allocationPROPOSE 5 shares, £88.88
Cash retained£315.54£170.81

EXPN.L is halved again because the base allocation this pot works to is £125 and a half allocation is £62.50, which buys two shares at 2,782p and not four. Four shares is £112, which is the full allocation wearing a reduced label.

The MWA top-up is declined on evidence, not on §4.5a alone. §4.5a prefers a fresh name at comparable merit, and two fresh names cleared. Beyond that: the Review published seven minutes before this run says the accepted MWA thesis "has no asset denominator, so falling asset returns are invisible, and pricing that holds margin at 18% can let declining volumes pass indefinitely." Adding to a position whose own falsifier was just judged unable to see its dominant risk is the weakest use of this cash on the table. The better monitoring in the morning's top-up draft is a reason to re-propose the falsifier, which the Review says explicitly, not a reason to buy more shares under the old one.

The residual £315.54 is a position (§4.4), and it has a date on it. Two ranked names report on 16 September: R&S Group's full H1 report and Trip.com's results, the latter confirmed by HKEXnews notice. Both are three days away and both are WAIT below. Spending that cash on a top-up now, rather than on whichever of those the evidence supports on 17 September, is the choice this run declines to make.

Ranking

A name is ranked when it clears §6.1's cheapest-decile filter on positive reported earnings, and excluded otherwise. A low percentile admits research; it never supplies a thesis (§2.4).

VerdictRankTickerReason
PROPOSE 1 share1TWFiled operating margin rose three years running to 41.18% on 18.9% revenue growth, and asset turnover rose with it (0.237× to 0.251×). The de-rating is large and the dominant risk — fee compression outrunning volume — is directly falsifiable from quarterly fee-per-million disclosure and an external competitor series. Half size: reported $4.19 EPS is not the $3.79 company-adjusted figure, and ROIC and gross profit over assets are both blank locally.
PROPOSE 2 shares2EXPN.LThree years of ~24% filed operating margin with 12.26% revenue growth, and organic growth that has held or risen (group 7%, B2B 9%, North America B2B 11% in the June quarter) while the multiple roughly halved. Half size under Rule 4: the Q1 update publishes no unit, customer or transaction count, verified this run, so T2's first fingerprint has no dated source.
WAIT3RSGN.SWThe best capital economics in the ranking — FY2025 ROIC 37.76%, gross profit over assets 66.02%, turnover 1.45× — at the 0th percentile against a 33.26× median. The full H1 report lands 16 September, and the preliminary already shows sales down 13% and EBITDA down 23%. Buying three days before the report that decides it is the 7532.T mistake in its purest form. Review 17 September. Note 145 weeks from 2023-12-15 makes the percentile indicative.
WAIT49961.HKResults filed for 16 September on an HKEXnews notice, not an estimate. Reported 5.78× against vendor recurring 11.85× is a gap too large to size on before the release resolves it. FY2025 ROIC 7.69%, gross profit over assets 18.81%, turnover 0.233× are modest. Review 17 September. Held in the human book at 1.12%.
EXCLUDE5MWAHeld. §4.5a and the reasoning above: fresh names first, and the accepted falsifier needs re-proposing before the position is enlarged under it. The business itself keeps improving — ROIC 8.39% to 11.01% to 13.12%, operating margin 10.79% to 16.26% to 18.84% — which is why this is a deferral and not a rejection.
EXCLUDE6NVO§2.4, on the capital rather than the margin. Total assets went DKK 241.3bn to DKK 542.9bn over three years while the latest year's revenue grew 6.43%; ROIC fell 56.62% to 41.09% to 30.61%, gross profit over assets 62.48% to 46.10%, turnover 0.739× to 0.569×. Every capital measure has halved into a doubling asset base. A 10.53× multiple against a 31.04× median is what that profile is worth, not a discount to it.
EXCLUDE7REL.L§2.4 and Rule 5. The economics are genuinely good (ROIC 25.74%, gross profit over assets 43.08%, operating margin rising to 31.11%), but revenue grew 1.65% and T2 names seat-priced legal and scientific information exactly. I cannot argue the discount is wrong without asserting the moat, which Rule 2 forbids as a premise. EXPN.L carries fresher disclosed growth for the same category bet.
EXCLUDE8INTU§2.4 and Rule 5. Margin 23.66% to 26.22% to 28.80%, growth 13.90%, ROIC 14.86% — a good business at the 4.93rd percentile. But its own FY2026 release has US TurboTax units down 2% with growth from price and mix, which is T2's stated early shape in Leo's own words. The cheapness is the thesis, priced; I have no argument that it is mispriced.
EXCLUDE9PDD§2.4. Operating margin fell 27.53% to 21.56% and ROIC 29.01% to 18.30% in the latest filed year on 9.65% revenue growth. Merchant-subsidy competition is doing that, and an 8.26× multiple does not establish when it stops.
EXCLUDE106862.HK§2.4. The asset productivity is striking (turnover 1.96×, gross profit over assets 51.16%, ROIC 28.29%) but revenue grew 1.10% and operating margin fell 14.15% to 12.01%. Cheap and flat is not a recovery.
EXCLUDE116936.HK§2.4. FY2025 operating margin 4.97%, down from 5.41%, on 8.37% growth, and no local capital fields at all. The Sweep's own H1 evidence has international revenue up 15.6% producing RMB 30m of segment net profit. Growth that does not earn is not the thesis; 95 weeks from 2024-11-29 also makes the percentile indicative.
EXCLUDE12034230.KS§2.4. Operating margin 13.55%, still below FY2023's 14.66%, on 7.25% growth, with no local ROIC, gross profit over assets or turnover. A Korean tourism recovery without demonstrated capital returns is the 7532.T shape.
EXCLUDE136690.HK§2.4. Operating margin slipped 8.22% to 7.75% on 5.71% growth, and no capital fields locally. A 6.41% yield is the attraction; that is an income argument, not a compounding one.
EXCLUDE14LULU§2.4. Operating margin fell 23.67% to 19.91% while growth slowed to 4.86%, and no local capital fields. An 8.15× multiple at the 0th percentile prices a brand problem that the accounts confirm rather than deny.
EXCLUDE15WLY§2.4 and Rule 5. Operating margin recovered to 17.66%, but revenue fell 0.06% and the whole filed series is flat to down, with no local capital fields. T2 and content substitution can explain the 0th percentile; an AI-licensing story is not a disclosed revenue line.
EXCLUDE16BBCA.JK§2.4 cannot be applied as written — a bank has no meaningful operating margin and no industrial ROIC, and the local fields are correctly blank. Turnover 0.07× is a banking balance sheet, not a productivity reading. EXPN.L — Experian plc

Ranked second in the run report for this cycle, which accounts for all 93 watchlist names.

What it does: Experian keeps credit files on consumers and businesses — repayment histories, balances, defaults, company records — collected from the lenders who contribute them, in the United States, the United Kingdom, Brazil and about thirty other countries. It sells access to those files and the decisions built on top of them: credit scores, affordability and fraud checks, identity verification, and the software lenders use to run those checks inside an application. Banks, credit-card issuers, motor and telecoms lenders and insurers are the paying customers, and a smaller consumer arm sells memberships directly to individuals who want to see and improve their own file.

1. Order

BUY 2 shares of EXPN.L on the London Stock Exchange, limit 2,800 GBp. Currency GBP. £56.00 deployed at the limit, £55.64 at Friday's close, against a reduced allocation of £62.50. Cash left idle from this ticket: £6.50 of the allocation, which is whole-share rounding. Pot cash after this and the TW order: £315.54.

Expected first-year costs. Broker assumed is Trading 212, which lists the name.

Stamp duty is a transaction tax, identical at every broker, so it is stated on its own line and excluded from the §4.1a gate and included in the §4.1 total, per §4.1a. The 0.5% is assumed, not sourced. Experian plc is incorporated in Jersey, which ordinarily puts a share outside UK SDRT, but no broker or HMRC schedule was obtained to confirm it, so the conservative charge is carried and the question is logged to data-wishlist.md. It is £0.28 and changes no gate either way.

Size, and why it is half. The base allocation is £125 and this ticket takes half under Rule 4. The dominant risk in P6 is that AI agents reduce the number of paid credit decisions Experian is asked for. I checked the company's most recent disclosure directly for this proposal: the Q1 FY27 trading update, covering the three months to 30 June 2026 and published 16 July 2026, publishes organic revenue growth percentages and nothing else — no customer count, no unit volume, no transaction volume, for the group or for any region. The metric that would move first under the dominant risk is therefore not published on any cadence at all, which is Rule 4's "lives entirely outside any dated source" limb. Half the allocation, by default, rather than the full size with a caveat.

A second reason points the same way: prices.json carries no capital fields whatsoever for EXPN.L — no ROIC, no gross profit over total assets, no asset turnover. The only capital figure available is Experian's own post-tax ROCE, on the issuer's definition, which is evidence and not the repo's measure.

£56.00 is 11.2% of £500 contributed capital, against the §4.2 cap of £250. No cap is in play.

2. Thesis

Experian sells the same underlying asset to a broad set of lenders year after year, and the accounts show that repeating steadily: revenue grew 12.26% to $8,445m in the year to March 2026, and the filed operating margin has sat at 23.87%, 23.83% and 24.21% across the three filed years, which is consistency rather than an elevated margin needing a story to defend it. Why now is the price: the multiple has roughly halved across two fiscal years, from a 35.88–60.10× band in FY2025 to 26.73–43.72× in FY2026 and 21.73–30.65× so far in FY2027, putting today's 22.99× at the 1.81st percentile of 221 weeks against a 37.20× median. What the market appears to be pricing is a fade in B2B decisioning economics as lending workflows automate — and the disclosed direction of that exact segment has not faded but firmed: group organic growth was 8% in FY2026, and in the June 2026 quarter group organic was 7%, B2B 9% and North America B2B 11%, so the de-rating is steeper than anything Experian has yet reported.

That last sentence is the whole of the Rule 5 answer and it is deliberately narrow. It says the price has moved much further than the disclosure has. It does not say the disclosure can see the risk — P6 says it cannot, and P1 sizes for that.

3. Falsifier

Warning — at the half-year results, locally dated 18 November 2026, reviewed by 19 November. Any one triggers a re-read:

  • North America B2B organic growth below 6%, against 11% in the quarter to 30 June 2026.
  • The half-year commentary attributes B2B growth to price and mix with no volume or transaction statement, while Equifax's USIS Diversified Markets organic growth over a comparable period is 6% or better. Revenue rising on price while a same-market comparator grows is T2's stated early shape, in Leo's own words in theses.md: "revenue growth that comes from price and mix while unit or customer counts flatten is this thesis arriving early."
  • The FY27 expectation, currently "unchanged", is withdrawn or reduced.

Break — the first assessable pair checked by 31 January 2027, then at FY27 results. Either route alone calls for exit under §5.1:

  • (a) Two successive non-overlapping reported periods of non-positive North America B2B organic growth while Equifax Diversified Markets stays positive. Do not manufacture two observations from a half-year total and a quarter inside it; if only one comparable period exists, that is one observation.
  • (b) A disclosed loss or repricing of a core data or decisioning contract reducing B2B annual revenue by 5% or more of the FY2026 base, or a legal or regulatory loss of access to a core dataset that forces withdrawal of a material lending product. The second breaks the premise on disclosure alone, whatever revenue has done to date.

External evidence (Rule 3). The dominant risk is secular, and Experian's own filings cannot settle it, so:

SourceMetricCadenceBaseline
Equifax quarterly resultsUSIS Diversified Markets organic growthquarterly6% in the June 2026 quarter. Total USIS growth of 17% is mortgage-driven and is not the comparator
FICO quarterly resultsB2B Scores segment volumes and pricequarterlythe one large peer that discloses a volume alongside a price
Experian annual report risk factorsyear-on-year wording on automation and disintermediationannual, Maya company's own changing language is the cheapest available early signal

This falsifier is weaker than TW's and the weakness is the point. Revenue growth and a competitor's revenue growth are both revenue measures, and the dominant risk is a volume risk. Neither can certify that agents are not already reducing paid decision volume; they can only show the revenue consequence once it arrives. Silence is not green. If the half-year passes with a revenue beat and still no unit disclosure, the correct action is to keep the reduced size and log the missing evidence again, never to size up on a beat.

4. Review date

19 November 2026, the day after the locally dated half-year results, regardless of price.

Local check: agree. Every local figure is quoted from the repo unchanged. Three disclosures belong with it rather than buried:

  1. The percentile's span is not five years. peHistory gives 5y, 10y and all as the same 221 weeks from 2022-07-01, because the file holds no earlier weeks for this ticker. Experian has been listed since 2006, so this is a fetch-depth limit, not a business-start one, and it does not belong in HISTORY_FROM. It matters to the argument in P2: the 37.20× "median" is a 2022–2026 median struck over a period of unusually high information-services multiples, so the de-rating measured against it flatters this proposal. I quote the span every time and do not call it a five-year history.
  2. Two earnings bases, and they are not the same measure. The reported 121 GBp trailing EPS gives 22.99×; Experian's own Benchmark diluted EPS of USD 1.787, which excludes amortisation of acquisition intangibles among other items, gives 21.06× on the same price translated at 1.353. Both are shown. The 1.81st percentile belongs to the reported series only and is never attached to the Benchmark denominator — there is no adjusted history to replay it over.
  3. The multiple is a filter this name passed, not the case for owning it (§2.4). P2 stands on filed margin consistency and disclosed organic growth.

Adjustments: no new entry was writable in this run. adjustments.json already carries EXPN.L's two annual company Benchmark diluted EPS figures in USD under normalizedEps, with the FY2026 results announcement as their source, and the FY2026 $101m gross financing gain recorded as evidence with arithmetic: false — it is a gross figure and cannot be subtracted from after-tax income attributable to shareholders. No quarterly series may be added until researchTtm() handles a filer reporting in a currency other than its quote's, which is already on the data wishlist; feeding four USD quarters to a GBp listing would silently publish a wrong denominator. No Experian release has appeared since those entries were made this morning, so there is nothing new to reconcile, and no research low or percentile is claimed.

6. The case against

Theses: T2 bears directly — Experian sells B2B decisioning whose unit of work (pull a file, score it, return an answer) is precisely the kind an agent performs end-to-end, and part of its B2B revenue is subscription rather than per-transaction. T3 bears on the tailwind side — its Activate and Agent Trust work is the non-human-identity and permissions layer T3 describes — but T3's own caution applies: the launch release disclosed no adoption and no revenue, so this is optionality, not the thesis arriving, and it receives no credit in P2 or in the sizing. T1 does not bear.

Dominant risk (secular): AI agents reduce the number of paid credit decisions and data pulls Experian is asked to serve, or move buyers from subscription to outcome pricing, and Experian's own disclosure cannot show it — the company publishes organic revenue growth percentages and no customer, unit or transaction counts at all, verified in the Q1 FY27 update for this proposal.

Earliest observable: North America B2B organic growth at the half-year results, locally dated 18 November 2026 — two months away, so the date is close. But it is a revenue measure standing in for a volume risk, and the volume measure is published nowhere on any cadence. Rule 4 applies on that limb and P1 takes half the allocation. The nearest thing to a direct observable is external and imperfect: Equifax's USIS Diversified Markets organic growth, quarterly.

Then the secondary arguments:

  • The thesis rests on a metric its own dominant risk says is blind. P2 argues the de-rating outruns the disclosed deceleration. If units are already falling and price is carrying revenue, P2's evidence would look exactly as it does now. That is the strongest single objection to this proposal and it is answered with size rather than with prose.
  • Not the geographic diversification the London listing suggests. Roughly 67% of group revenue is North American, per the FY26 results as read by the 08:13 Sweep. Leo's book is already 66.89% US (signals.json book.byGeography), so this adds US exposure wearing a UK ticker.
  • Consumer Services grew 2% in the June quarter against B2B's 9%. Nearly a third of the business is growing at barely the rate of inflation, and it is the half most exposed to a direct consumer relationship that an aggregator or a bank app can intermediate.
  • $792m of FY26 acquisitions to integrate, per the FY26 results as read by the Sweep. Acquired growth is not organic growth, and the filed operating margin has to absorb the amortisation that the company's own Benchmark EPS removes.
  • The capital measures are entirely missing. Leo's §2.4 extension asks what the capital earns and how hard the assets are worked, and for this name the repo answers nothing at all. The 17.2% ROCE quoted is Experian's own definition on Experian's own numbers. Blank is an answer and it is not replaced here by the 24.21% margin.
  • US consumer-credit cycle. A large part of B2B volume moves with lending activity, which is cyclical and currently facing 4.79% five-year yields. A volume decline from the cycle and one from T2 would look identical in the only figures Experian publishes.
  • Combined exposure with the human book: none. holdings.json holds no Experian and no credit bureau, and RELX — the nearest information-services comparator — is watchlist only, not held. This adds a new exposure rather than concentrating one.

Why this is not 7532.T again. The regret was buying a top-line rebound without the fundamentals, the valuation, the forward outlook or the currency. Here the case is three years of filed operating margin within 40 basis points of itself, 12.26% filed revenue growth, and a dated forward expectation the company has left unchanged; the multiple is a filter, quoted with its real 221-week span and with the flattering-median caveat stated; and the currency is a GBP ticket on a GBp line with no conversion. What is missing — every local capital measure, and any disclosure of paid volume — is named in P1 and in the risk above, and paid for with half a position rather than explained away.

TW — Tradeweb Markets

Run report and complete ranking

What it does: Tradeweb operates electronic markets on which banks, asset managers and other investors trade bonds, interest-rate products, equities and money-market instruments. It earns transaction fees, subscriptions and data fees.

1. Order

BUY 1 share of TW on NASDAQ, limit $102.00, regular session only, through Trading 212 Invest/Stocks ISA. Order currency USD. Use a day order on 14 September 2026; an unfilled order expires rather than chasing a higher price.

The normal £250 maximum is halved to £125 under §7.2a: the current company-adjusted denominator is sourced, but the historical distribution is materially contaminated by non-operating gains. One share at the limit deploys £75.39, leaving £49.61 of the allocation undeployed before fees. Two shares would exceed the reduced allocation. There is no §4.2a exception: this position is only 15.08% of £500 contributed, before costs.

Expected entry commission £0, custody £0, FX 0.15% = £0.11, purchase tax £0, ADR charge £0. Expected first-year buy-and-hold broker costs are £0.11, 0.15% of the ticket, passing both §4.1a and §4.1. A sale or another currency conversion would add costs; no sale is assumed in this estimate. The exchange spread is not a separately guaranteed cost; the limit caps the purchase price. Broker schedule.

At USD/GBP 1.353 from prices.json, the all-in ticket is £75.50. Standalone cash remaining is £371.82; all three proposals together leave £170.81 at their limits. Refresh FX and cash before placement; do not exceed £125 all-in. These are proposals against the same £447.32 cash, not independently spendable balances.

2. Thesis

Tradeweb sells execution across an established network, and the operating record shows revenue rising from $1.338bn to $2.052bn over FY2023–25 while operating margin rose from 37.0% to 41.2% (local filed series). August's fully electronic US credit volume grew 32.5%, which makes continued migration of trading onto the platform a live business opportunity rather than a bet on another volatility spike (August activity). My inference is that the market may be underpricing the cash earned from that migration, but the reported 56.4% discount to its historical median overstates the valuation argument because Canton gains enlarged earnings; the investment depends on monetisation surviving the tests below, not on recovery to an old multiple.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At Q3 results on 29 October 2026, re-read if transaction-fee revenue growth trails total ADV growth by 15 percentage points or more, or cash-credit variable fees per million fall 15% or more year on year, or fully electronic high-grade TRACE share is below 18.0%. These are analyst thresholds, not guidance. Q2's transaction-fee growth was 8.28% against ADV growth of 18.2%, and cash-credit fee yield fell 11.4%: deterioration can therefore trigger before revenue falls. Monthly share observations are an earlier warning, checked by 8 October, but a single monthly print is not a sale.

Break: By the FY2026 release, checked no later than 1 March 2027, sell under §5.1 if both Q3 and Q4 show flat or falling transaction-fee revenue while ADV grows; separately, sell if fully electronic high-grade share is below 17.0% in both quarters, even if pricing holds revenue up. Either route breaks the execution-network argument. Do not require both routes to fire. Q2 filing baseline, confirmed Q3 date.

External competitive check: MarketAxess Q2 results report portfolio-trading ADV up 33%, but total commission revenue down 3% and total-credit fees per million down 7%. This is actual evidence that automation can expand activity without expanding the toll collected. Read those same measures quarterly alongside Tradeweb, by 10 November 2026 for the next comparison; different product mixes mean their absolute fee levels are not comparable. Missing or acquisition-discontinued reporting is unavailable evidence, not a pass.

4. Review date

8 October 2026 for September activity, then 30 October 2026 for Q3 results regardless of price. The first date is a review deadline, not a promised company publication date.

5. Numbers as of today

Prices were fetched 13 September 2026, 08:22:43 UTC; TW's regular-session observation is 11 September, 20:00 UTC. Sunday is not a new trading session.

Local check: Revenue, operating income and diluted EPS for Q2 agree. Local ni $181.318m is attributable to Tradeweb, not the filing's $206.686m consolidated net income; local nic $181.274m differs slightly again, so it is not substituted for the filing's attribution. I opened filing-dates.json specifically to trace the trough's $4.05 denominator: it is the reported TTM available after Q1 2026, $0.71 + $0.86 + $1.52 + $0.96, rather than FY2025's $3.78. The $1.52 Q4 value is derived in that file and differs by one cent from Yahoo's directly stored $1.51. This explains the annual/TTM difference; it is not a demonstrated pipeline error. Use $3.79 researchEps for current valuation and retain historical multiples solely as labelled screening references. One annual period and four quarters have cited company-adjusted EPS; no comparable adjusted historical window is certified.

Adjustments: Existing normalizedEps.TW already records the four sourced quarters and FY2025; no duplicate added. Appended FY2026 $26.6m unrealised minority-equity gains, found in the Q2 release, as arithmetic:false because no after-tax common-shareholder amount is stated. Canton losses in that quarter do not erase the earlier gain evidence and no existing entry was changed.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: The case is tested against revenue per unit and platform share, rather than extrapolating a thematic rebound. Rising margins alone do not prove reinvestment quality: missing ROIC remains a limitation, historical earnings uncertainty halves the allocation, and a limit prevents paying any price for the story.

6. The case against

Theses: T2, automated workflows may increase executions while compressing what can be charged per execution; T1, cheaper models make automation easier but do not establish which trading venue captures the value. T3 is not a material part of this thesis.

Dominant risk (competitive): Automated and portfolio trading grow fastest in low-fee channels, so execution volumes can rise while competing venues and customers compress Tradeweb's economics.

Earliest observable: September share/mix data, checked by 8 October; Q3 transaction fees and fee yields on 29 October; MarketAxess's next quarterly comparison by 10 November. These answer the risk directly. FINRA's monthly TRACE report supplies an external market-volume denominator on the third business day of the following month, but a matched August download was not obtained here; Tradeweb's share is not independently replicated.

Network liquidity may support margins, but customers can split flow between venues and new automation may lower switching costs. The competing platform's announced ICE acquisition also deserves monitoring, rather than assuming today's fragmented competition persists. Company-adjusted EPS excludes more than Canton gains, including specified acquisition and compensation items, so 26.77× is not independently reconstructed owner earnings.

Human-book overlap: No direct TW instrument is present in holdings.json, so existing direct weight is 0%; this adds US financial infrastructure to a book already 66.89% US and 7.66% Financial Services in signals.json. Fund look-through exposure is not quantified by name. Overlap is disclosed and has not reduced the rank.

MWA — Mueller Water Products, modest top-up

Run report and complete ranking

What it does: Mueller makes valves, hydrants, meters and other equipment used in water networks. Utilities, municipalities and contractors buy the equipment to repair, replace or build those networks.

1. Order

BUY 5 additional shares of MWA on NYSE, limit $24.05, regular session only, through Trading 212 Invest/Stocks ISA. Use a day order on 14 September 2026; leave it unfilled rather than increase the limit. This would take the pot from 3 to 8 shares.

The £250 position cap has £196.92 of room after valuing the existing three shares at the local $23.94 and USD/GBP 1.353. §7.2a halves that remaining allocation to £98.46 because tariff benefits are not separated and local operating income excludes charges present in the filing. Five shares at the limit deploy £88.88, leaving £9.58 of the allocation idle before fees; six would cost £106.65 and fail the reduced budget. The resulting position is about £141.96, 28.39% of contributed capital, marking old shares at the close and new shares at the limit. Marking all eight at the limit gives £142.20, still below £250. No cap exception is used.

Expected commission £0, FX 0.15% = £0.13, custody £0, purchase tax £0 and ADR fees £0: £89.01 all-in. First-year buy-and-hold broker costs are 0.15%, passing both gates; a later sale/conversion is extra. No separately quantified spread is assumed; the limit constrains the price. Broker schedule. Standalone cash remaining is £358.31, and £170.81 after this run's three proposals. Refresh cash/FX and keep the ticket within £98.46 all-in.

§4.5a: Fund fresh TW and EXPN first. They receive the first two slots and their own reduced allocations. MWA is the third slot because an established repair/replacement business with improving operating returns is preferable here to NVO's falling capital efficiency, the consumer turnarounds and software names without a persuasive answer to displacement. This does not take MWA to the 50% cap and does not silently enlarge either fresh name beyond its risk allowance. The Review still says hold the existing shares; no new result has arrived since entry. This proposal supplies a better falsifier for the additional capital, not evidence that the old thesis has already succeeded.

2. Thesis

Mueller sells equipment whose repair and replacement demand extends beyond a single construction cycle, while its local FY2023–25 accounts show sales rising from $1.276bn to $1.430bn and improving profitability (earnings.json). The investable opportunity is for the enlarged manufacturing base to produce more cash from that installed demand, with local FY2025 ROIC of 13.12% versus 8.39% in FY2023 providing a starting question about capital productivity rather than proof it will persist (prices.json). My inference is that modest exposure is warranted while the cash conversion commitment is tested, but lower physical volumes and a charge-sensitive margin mean a further top-up needs separate volume, margin and asset-return exit routes.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At FY2026 results, estimated locally for 5 November, re-read by 10 November 2026 if physical volumes decline again, if free cash flow is 70% or less of company-adjusted net income, or if trailing operating profit divided by average total assets falls below 13%. Any one warns. The cash threshold is management's stated commitment; the asset-return threshold is my decision rule. Use the release's volume bridge when a percentage is not supplied; missing disclosure is unknown, not growth. Q3 release.

Break: Sell the position under §5.1 if either of the first two post-entry quarters reports a GAAP operating margin below 16%, or if both quarters have declining physical volumes and GAAP operating margins below 18%. Independently, sell if trailing operating profit divided by average total assets falls below 11% at either of those reports. Review the two-quarter test by 28 February 2027. These thresholds are analyst choices: the separate margin and asset-return routes prevent rising prices from hiding falling capital productivity.

For the asset test, use filed TTM operating income after all operating charges / mean of total assets at the TTM beginning and end. This is a pre-tax operating return on assets, not ROIC and not annualised single-quarter profit. Obtain the comparable filings at each review; if the beginning balance or a quarter is unavailable, report the test as unavailable and escalate the review rather than substituting local adjusted operating income. Today's nine-month filed operating income is $217.7m and June total assets $1,953.3m, but those are not a TTM ratio. Q3 10-Q.

These improve the proposed monitoring terms; the existing accepted proposal is not rewritten by an unaccepted top-up. If Leo accepts this proposal, use these tests for the resulting eight-share position.

4. Review date

10 November 2026, regardless of price; then 28 February 2027. The local 5 November result date is an estimate, not a confirmed issuer commitment.

5. Numbers as of today

Local check: Sales and reported EPS agree. Local operating income exceeds filed GAAP income by the $11.2m strategic reorganisation charge; use filed $80.6m for present margin and every P3 test. Local capital ratios remain useful screening references, not verified GAAP returns. The $1.40915 own EPS starts with vendor normalisation; subtracting $0.06 from reported $1.42 would instead give $1.36, or 17.60×, and still would not remove unquantified tariffs. Do not describe either as complete owner earnings. Zero complete fiscal years have a fully sourced one-off reconciliation; one current-year tax adjustment is cited.

Adjustments: Existing FY2026 amountPerShare:0.06 is retained. Appended company-adjusted diluted EPS $0.34 for 2025-06-30 and $0.50 for 2026-06-30 from the release. The latter includes the tax benefit, so it must not be called tax-benefit-free. Two nonconsecutive quarters cannot produce researchEps. No separate tariff amount was quantified, so none was invented or subtracted. The nine-month adjusted EPS is not mislabelled as a quarter.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: Replacement demand is not enough: falling turnover, actual GAAP charges, cash conversion and a capital denominator all remain in the decision. The top-up is reduced, and the monitoring can fail even while reported sales grow.

6. The case against

Theses: none.

Dominant risk (financial): The expanded asset base earns less as physical demand weakens, while pricing and temporary benefits keep reported sales and margins looking healthy.

Earliest observable: FY2026 volume direction, cash conversion and filed TTM asset return at the next results, reviewed by 10 November. P3 independently tests both the income statement and the assets behind it. The next two post-entry quarters are September and December; June cannot be counted towards their break condition.

Tariff refunds, the tax benefit and pricing are not repeatable volume growth. New housing weakness can persist, capacity carries fixed costs, and the local capital-return improvement partly relies on a classification that needs reconciliation. Buying more shortly after entry without new results is an allocation choice, not confirmation of the thesis; the small top-up and fresh-name priority constrain it.

Human-book overlap: MWA appears among public instrument identities, but the book weights fold small names into a tail and do not expose a separate MWA percentage. The three recorded shares belong to the AI pot; a distinct human-book MWA weight is unavailable, not asserted to be zero. This buy raises pot exposure from about 10.62% to 28.39% of contributions and adds to a book reported as 66.89% US and 7.25% Industrials (positions, signals). Exact combined monetary exposure is not published.

EXPN.L — Experian

Run report and complete ranking

What it does: Experian collects and combines credit, identity and other data for lenders, businesses and consumers. It sells data, fraud checks and decision tools, and earns fees from consumer services and financial-product marketplaces.

1. Order

BUY 4 shares of EXPN.L on the London Stock Exchange, limit 2,800 GBp (£28.00), through Trading 212 Invest/Stocks ISA. Use a regular-session day order on 14 September 2026; do not raise the limit if unfilled.

Rule 4 halves £250 to £125 because paid decision volumes, customer losses and the share of revenue exposed to agents are not disclosed on a dependable schedule. §7.2a independently supports that reduced size because a comparable issuer-adjusted history is unavailable; I apply one half-size, not an invented compounded quarter-size. Four whole shares deploy £112.00, leaving £13.00 of the reduced allocation idle; five cost £140 and do not fit. Resulting position is 22.4% of £500 contributed, with no concentration exception.

Expected commission £0, FX £0 on a GBP-funded GBP trade, custody £0, ADR fee £0. Broker fees are 0%, below §4.1a. Expected transaction tax is £0: Experian states its ordinary transfers should not incur UK/Irish stamp duty or SDRT, subject to the stated instrument-of-transfer exception. That agrees with HMRC's distinction for foreign companies without a UK register; an LSE listing alone does not settle the tax. Broker fees, issuer share-tax information, HMRC.

Expected first-year buy-and-hold trading/custody cost is £0, 0%; this excludes an unobservable market spread and personal income taxes. If the broker nevertheless quotes 0.5% purchase tax, reserve £0.56 separately: £112.56 still passes the 2% first-year gate and £125 budget, but do not call that tax a broker fee. Standalone cash remaining is £335.32, or £170.81 after all three orders at their limits and expected fees. Use £170.25 as the three-order cash remainder if that tax is charged.

2. Thesis

Experian's existing data business increased statutory revenue from $7.097bn to $8.445bn over FY2024–26 while operating margin held near 24%, and Q1 FY2027 B2B organic growth was 9% (local accounts, Q1 update). The reported P/E is 38.4% below its historical median, a discount consistent with fears that agents commoditise distribution and decision software, but the last major renewal cycle produced longer contracts and higher values while the company already derived over 90% of B2B revenue from proprietary data (FY26 report). My inference is that this current contract evidence makes a blanket software-displacement discount too severe for a small position; persistence of that advantage is the hypothesis P3 must test, and I assign no earnings to Activate, Agent Trust or regulatory promises.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At the half-year update, locally dated 18 November 2026, trigger a re-read on any disclosed fall in B2B paid transactions, customer retention or contract value despite rising revenue; a price increase masking fewer units is a warning, not an excuse. Also warn if North American B2B organic growth drops below 6% while Equifax USIS Diversified Markets still grows at least 6% over a comparable period. Experian's current baseline is 11% North American B2B organic growth; Equifax's June-quarter Diversified Markets baseline is 6%, while its mortgage-driven total USIS growth of 17% is not the comparator. These are analyst thresholds, not market-share calculations. Experian Q1, Equifax Q2.

Break: Sell under §5.1 on an issuer or customer disclosure that lost/repriced data or decision contracts reduce annual recurring revenue by 5% or more of the FY26 B2B base, or on two successive reported periods of non-positive North American B2B organic growth while Equifax Diversified Markets remains positive. Review the first possible pair by 31 January 2027, using non-overlapping reported periods where available; otherwise do not manufacture two observations from a half-year total and one quarter inside it. Separately, a legal loss of access to a core dataset that forces withdrawal of a material lending product breaks the data-ownership premise when disclosed, irrespective of revenue to date.

The named contract-loss threshold is my decision rule, not a prediction or a presently disclosed loss. Experian's unit/retention data and the competitive split may remain unavailable. Neither revenue nor the Equifax proxy can certify that T2 is absent, and silence is not green: keep the Rule 4 reduced size, log the missing evidence at each review, and seek customer/competitor disclosures. There is no automatic permission to increase size after a revenue beat.

4. Review date

19 November 2026, regardless of price; earlier on a material contract or data-access disclosure. Check the local 18 November results date before the event; it has not been independently confirmed here. Follow up on 31 January 2027 for the next trading update and 31 May 2027 for annual cash conversion and capital returns.

The local $1.502bn attributable figure differs from $1.508bn consolidated profit, so those are not mixed. Historical EPS and current quote conversions are not a certified Benchmark history. Two annual company-adjusted figures are now cited; no adjusted rolling window is claimed.

Adjustments: Appended normalizedEps.EXPN.L.annual for 2025-03-31, $1.555, and 2026-03-31, $1.787, explicitly labelled USD Benchmark diluted EPS, plus FY2026 $101m financing fair-value gains as arithmetic:false. The release's financing bridge is not a separately attributable common-shareholder adjustment. These annual records have an empty quarterly series: the current consumer has no currency conversion for research EPS, so USD quarterly values must not later be fed straight into a GBp multiple. That gap is recorded in the wishlist; it is not repaired by FX-converting a filed EPS here.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: Existing contracts, organic growth and capital returns carry the case; an AI launch carries no revenue in the valuation. Trading in GBP does not remove USD/Brazilian operating exposure. The limits and reduced size leave room for the displacement thesis to prove right.

6. The case against

Theses: T2, agents could displace decision-workflow interfaces and distribution; T1, cheaper models lower competitors' analytics costs as well as Experian's; T3, identity and permissions might create demand, but paid adoption is unquantified and no compulsory-revenue assumption is made.

Dominant risk (secular): Agents and alternative data routes can commoditise Experian's decision interface, allowing paid volumes or contract economics to weaken before price-supported revenue does.

Earliest observable: Dated customer/contract disclosures when they occur, then November's Experian and Equifax releases. There is no reliable date for a direct paid-unit series, which is why Rule 4 halves size even though the financial proxies arrive sooner than two quarters. Equifax's 6% Diversified Markets growth is an external operating baseline, not evidence that Experian has already lost share.

Renewals support the decision today but do not guarantee future bargaining power; lenders can use multiple data sources. Acquisitions, buybacks and software investment compete for the same cash, and Benchmark earnings add back costs that shareholders have borne. A warning on these financial measures does not substitute for the contract/usage test.

Human-book overlap: No direct EXPN instrument is in holdings.json, so direct weight is 0%. Nevertheless 67% of Experian revenue is North American (Q1 disclosure), so this adds to the economic region already dominant in a 66.89% US human book (signals.json); European listing geography is not economic diversification. Fund exposure by name is unquantified. This disclosure has not reduced the rank.

Run report — 12 September 2026, 12:30 UTC

One proposal: BUY 3 NVO, £95.51 of the £447.31 in the pot — a restatement of this morning's conclusion on an unchanged snapshot, written rather than suppressed because the brief says a pending draft must not stop a top-ranked name being proposed.

The substantive work of this run is elsewhere, and it is in three places. The Sweep's lead re-look, 7532.T, is a WAIT and the reason is in our own local file, not in the filing the Sweep read. The 00:32 run's headline finding on Tradeweb was reached by comparing an adjusted numerator against an unadjusted floor, and the store now disagrees with it. And the fetch-prices.js gap that run logged to the wishlist has already been closed in code — the loop the pot was built to run has run.

What this run had to work with

  • Cash £447.31; contributed capital to date £500 across 4 and 8 September; holdings 3 MWA at $23.76, £53.09 at the current mark, so a pot of £500.40. pot/positions.json, generated 2026-09-12T12:21:00Z. The 00:32 NVO proposal is undecided and unexecuted — the cash is unchanged, which is why it is ranked again below.
  • The newest Sweep, 12 September 12:15: three candidates — Hotel Shilla (008770.KS), a 7532.T re-look, and a Trip.com re-look — off a genuinely new observation, that Japan's inbound count is shrinking (−1.7% ytd) while its headline is flat, because China is −56.3% and lower-spending neighbours have filled the gap. It handed 7532.T to this lane explicitly: "the honest answer is that this needs a Deep dive, not a sweep verdict."
  • The newest Review, 11 September 23:46: hold MWA, no instruction.
  • The Scan, signals.json generated 2026-09-12T12:23:10Z over prices struck the same moment: 6.1 valuation fired on 26 names, of which 16 are watchlist names, one is the held MWA and the rest are Leo's own book. 6.2 drawdown fired on BBW alone. 6.3 results, 6.4 dry powder, 6.6 news proxy and the 11.1 VIX standing order are all quiet — VIX 15.84.
  • pot/theses.md — T1 and T2, bearing on REL.L, INTU and WLY, all three ranked below, and on nothing proposed. The Sweep's own read was that neither of its candidates touches either thesis, and having done the work I agree: a Japanese discount retailer is not a seat-priced workflow tool and does not buy frontier inference.

The finding: 7532.T is cheap for a reason our own file already holds

The Sweep put Pan Pacific International — Don Quijote, UNY, Leo's stated regret — in front of this lane at ¥726.1, a 52-week low, −29.06% over a year and −21.62% in a month, firing 6.1 valuation at the 0.08th percentile of 207 weeks from 2022-09-30 and 9.1% below a floor last struck on 2022-12-23. That is the deepest below-floor reading anywhere in this scan. Its case was that the tourism damage is priced and the flat FY2027 guide is the new information, and its open question was whether that flat guide is Olympic integration cost or core margin.

I can answer it, and the answer is neither. It is the exit rate.

earnings.json carries all four quarters of the year to 30 June 2026, and they sum exactly to what the company filed — revenue ¥2,445,260m and profit ¥110,088m, to the million. That makes the quarterly split checkable, and it has not been checked by anyone:

quarter torevenuenet incomenet marginEPS
30 Sep 2025¥573,283m¥28,477m4.97%¥9.49
31 Dec 2025¥636,839m¥35,257m5.54%¥11.81
31 Mar 2026¥616,412m¥30,232m4.90%¥10.11
30 Jun 2026¥618,726m¥16,122m2.61%¥5.39

The June quarter earned ¥16.1bn on flat revenue — sales were higher than March's, and net income fell 47%. It is 14.6% of the full year's profit. The celebrated "+21.6% profit growth" is Q1 to Q3; the quarter the company actually exited the year on ran at roughly ¥64bn annualised against the ¥110.5bn FY2027 is guided to. So the flat guide is not conservatism and it is not Olympic dilution — it already requires a recovery from the exit rate, and nothing in the outlook says what delivers it.

The honest limit on that. earnings.json holds only FY2026's four quarters for this name, with no year-ago June quarter, so I cannot test how much of the drop is ordinary seasonality — the April–June quarter is structurally the weakest in Japanese retail. I am not claiming a collapse. I am claiming the single most important number in the case is one nobody has looked at and I cannot yet interpret, which is a reason to wait four weeks, not to buy today. Logged to the wishlist.

The second check, and it is the company's own. PPIH publishes monthly sales on a roughly ten-day lag (IR monthly page). August 2026, posted 10 September: comparable-store domestic retail 101.4%, discount stores 101.6%, UNY 100.4% — against +5% comparable-store growth for the discount business across FY2026. And underneath it, comparable traffic is 99.8% with spend per customer 101.6%. Customers are falling and price is carrying the line. That is the exact pattern the brief teaches this lane to distrust, and it is visible now, before the regulatory change lands.

Which makes the dated risk worse, not better. From 1 November 2026 Japan's tax-free system stops being an exemption at the till and becomes a refund claimed at departure after Customs confirms export. Tax-free sales were ¥228.6bn in FY2026, +31.2% — about 9.3% of group sales, and the highest-basket cohort. PPIH's FY2027 Business Outlook does not mention the change at all. Seven weeks out, on a line whose checkout economics it alters mechanically.

Is the discount wrong? No thesis in theses.md bears here, so Rule 5 does not formally bind — but the same question does, and the answer is that I cannot argue it yet. What I can say is that the market's stated reason for the discount is the wrong one: this company grew tax-free sales 31.2% to a record while Chinese arrivals fell 56%, in its own words "not reliant on any single country". It out-ran the thing it is being marked down for. The real risks — a June quarter at half the run rate, comparable traffic already negative, and an unpriced 1 November mechanic — are the ones neither the market narrative nor the guidance has addressed.

Why this is the 7532.T mistake if bought today. Leo's regret on this exact ticker was being "blinded by the tourist rebound without looking at the fundamentals, valuation, forward prospectus and yen depreciation carefully." Three of those four now argue against buying. The forward prospectus guides EPS down, ¥36.84 → ¥36.61. The fundamentals show an exit quarter at half the run-rate. Only the valuation is attractive, and §2.4 says a filter never argues you in. The yen has flipped sign — USD/JPY 153.554, −4.00% over three months — which is a cost tailwind to an importer-retailer and a headwind to tax-free receipts at once; the FY2027 guide already shows it, with ordinary income falling 1.2% while operating income rises 2.4%, a ¥6.4bn swing in non-operating items that is the currency arriving. Buying the 29% discount on the one leg that looks good is the mistake performed twice.

WAIT, and the wait is cheap and dated: September monthly sales ~10 October, October monthly ~10 November, Q1 FY2027 results 12 November (company-confirmed, not an estimate), and the first month containing the tax-free change reported ~10 December. Four dated observations in twelve weeks, all free, all from the company.

The second finding: this morning's Tradeweb verdict does not survive the store

The 00:32 run's headline was that TW is not cheap — that $270.9m of Canton Coin gains sat in trailing earnings, that the corrected multiple was "~28.9× against a 23.09× floor, 25% above it and nowhere near the cheapest decile", and that twelve TW proposals had been written on a wrong denominator. It wrote the adjustment to pot/adjustments.json with the company's own release as its source.

That entry has now been picked up, and the store's answer is not the one the run reached by hand:

basisfloortoday's percentilesource
filed23.091×1.1st of 261 weekssignals.json
own37.109×4.30thprices.json peLowOwn, pePctileOwn

The difference is a methodology error worth naming, because the brief already warns about it: the hand calculation corrected the numerator and compared it against a floor computed on the uncorrected basis. Both sides of a multiple have to be on the same basis. The store rebuilds the whole distribution — every weekly bar in the window recomputed with FY2025 net income reduced — and on that consistent basis TW sits at the 4.3rd percentile of its own own-basis history, which is inside the cheapest decile, not 25% outside it.

This does not make TW a buy, and it does not restore the twelve proposals. On any basis ~35× is not a cheap absolute multiple, and the business question those proposals kept circling — whether fees per million are eroding faster than volume grows — is untouched by any of this. But the verdict this morning recorded, EXCLUDE — §2.4, was reached the wrong way, so I am recording WAIT and the reason, rather than inheriting a conclusion or reversing it on the same thin arithmetic. Q3 results are 29 October.

The third finding: the gap logged this morning is already fixed

The 00:32 run's §5 said adjustedYears() matches only filed annual rows, so an adjustment recorded against the current, unfiled fiscal year does nothing precisely when a one-off is freshest — and logged it to the wishlist rather than calling it a bug.

fetch-prices.js now carries an ownTtmEps() function that does exactly that job, with a comment citing the 12 September finding and the reasoning for why the current year specifically is safe to apply to a trailing multiple: "an unfiled fiscal year has at most four filed quarters, so every one of them is inside the last four." MWA's entry — fiscal 2026, which does not end until 30 September — is no longer inert: peLowOwn is 19.451× against a filed peLow of 16.859×, with its own low date.

NVO is the exception, and it is why that proposal sizes at half. Its peLowOwn and pePctileOwn are identical to the filed figures to the last digit, so the DKK 26.8bn 340B entry is still doing nothing and the 12.3–12.9× in the proposal remains a hand derivation the store has not corroborated. §7.2a's answer to an earnings base you cannot certify is half the allocation, and that is what P1 takes.

Noted for the record: fetch-prices.js is modified in the working tree, so the figures above are from the current prices.json and the code that produced it.

The ranking

Ranked: 16. Excluded: 70. Total: 86, which is every name in watchlist.json. The line between the tiers is objective, not chosen: a name is ranked if 6.1 valuation fired on it in the 12:23 UTC scan — the repo's own implementation of §2.4's cheapest-decile filter — and excluded if it did not.

Two names are ranked that are not on the watchlist, marked †: 7532.T and 9961.HK are Sweep candidates this cycle and holdings in Leo's own book, so they are judged here but do not count toward the 86.

The Sweep's lead candidate cannot be researched yet, and that is the right answer

008770.KS — Hotel Shilla — is barred by §7.2, not by judgement. It entered watchlist.json this morning and prices.json carries no eps for it at all: price ₩41,100, peBands covering only 2024 and a 13-week stub of 2025, no capital block, no percentile that means anything. The brief says to say so and pick another, and this is that case.

The Sweep reached the same conclusion from the other direction and deserves credit for it: every Shilla figure in its own write-up came from trade press rather than DART, it said so in §4, and it wrote "that alone bars a Deep dive until fetched." Two lanes stopping at the same line for two independent reasons is the system working. The unblock is a DART API key, already on the wishlist; Korea is 1.46% of the book and the watchlist now carries five Korean lines.

What the run decided, and why

NVO, three shares, £95.51. After it the pot holds £351.80. The brief says keep going while cash remains and a candidate still clears — and none does.

Ranks 2 through 9 and both Sweep re-looks are WAIT, and in every one of them the missing thing has a date I can name: R&S's H1 and Trip.com's H1 on 16 September (four days), Intuit's investor day on 17 September (five days), PPIH's September monthly around 10 October, RELX's nine-month update on 22 October, Tradeweb's Q3 on 29 October, MWA's FY2026 on 5 November, PPIH's Q1 on 12 November, PDD's Q3 on 18 November. Three of those land inside a week. This lane runs several times a day; waiting is very nearly free, and §4.4 makes holding the cash a position rather than an omission. The 11.1 standing order is quiet with VIX at 15.84 — that cash is what it will need if it is not.

Ranks 10 through 16 fail on the venue, on capital returns, on absolute price, or on the business.

Two things appended this run. Nothing to pot/adjustments.json: no one-off was reconciled here that is separately quantified in a company's own document. PPIH's June-quarter weakness is a level, not a disclosed exceptional item, and Yahoo's norm runs 9–16% above filed net income in every one of 7532.T's four filed years — a systematic vendor adjustment with no citation behind it, which is precisely what this store exists not to be. Writing an entry I cannot source would be worse than writing none. Two entries went to pot/data-wishlist.md, below.

§5 — data quality

  • earnings.json carries no year-ago quarter. It holds the trailing four or five quarters per name, so a quarter cannot be compared with the same quarter a year earlier. On 7532.T this is the difference between "the exit quarter halved" and "April–June is always the weak one", and it decided a verdict. Wishlisted.
  • PPIH's monthly sales history is not retrievable. The company publishes the series and the current month renders, but prior months sit in PDFs that do not extract, so a trend cannot be built from the one reading available. Wishlisted.
  • The 00:32 run's adjustedYears() finding is closed — ownTtmEps() now applies a current-year adjustment to the trailing multiple, and MWA's and TW's own bases have moved as a result. NVO's has not, which is stated in its P5 and is why it sizes at half.
  • peWeeks is under three years for four ranked names — RSGN.SW 144, GME 129, AMSC 84, and on the excluded side GWRE 46 and MRVL 41 — while peWindow says "5y" for all of them. 7532.T's 207 weeks is over three years and its percentile is usable, but it begins 2022-09-30, not five years ago, and is quoted that way above. Stated so the label is never read as a measurement.

model: claude-opus-5, lane: deepdive, 2026-09-12 12:23, 13m41s, 9,764,259 tokens (858,980 fresh, 8,751,766 cached, 153,513 out), stamped from the session log rather than self-reported

NVO — Novo Nordisk A/S (New York-listed ADR)

What it does: Novo Nordisk discovers, manufactures and sells prescription medicines, almost all of them injectable or oral peptides. Two families carry the company: GLP-1 medicines for type 2 diabetes and for obesity — Ozempic, Rybelsus, Wegovy and an oral Wegovy tablet — and insulins. It sells to national health systems and hospital groups, and in the United States to insurers and pharmacy benefit managers at rebated list prices, increasingly also direct to patients for cash. It makes the active ingredient and the injection devices in its own plants in Denmark, the United States and France. Revenue is patented drug sales; the cost is a very large and still-growing factory estate.

Ranking for this run: 2026-09-12-1230-ranking.md.

This restates the conclusion of the 00:32 run on an unchanged price snapshot, and says so rather than suppressing it. The brief is explicit that a pending draft is not a position and must not stop a top-ranked name being written up; NVO is still the best fresh candidate that clears, so it is proposed again. Every figure below was re-derived from local data in this run rather than carried across, and two things did change overnight — see the own-basis note in P5.

1. Order

BUY 3 shares of NVO on the NYSE, £95.51 of a £125 allocation, market order. Currency USD. Cash left idle: £351.80 (pot cash £447.31 before the order).

  • Why £125 and not £250. §4.2 caps a position at 50% of contributed capital to date (£500), which is £250. I am taking half of that under §7.2a. Rule 4 does not bite — the dominant risk in P6 has a dated observable inside two quarters. §7.2a does: zero of the four filed years carry a cited adjustment, the one adjustment this repo holds for NVO is inert (P5), and the multiple I am valuing on is a hand derivation the store has not reproduced. Half the allocation is the written default for exactly that, and I am not arguing my way out of it.
  • Resulting concentration: £95.51 is 19.1% of the £500 contributed to date, and 17.5% of the pot's £500.40 mark including the three MWA shares. Inside §4.2; §4.2a and §4.2b are not engaged.

Two honest gaps. The ADR depositary's service fee is not sourced. Novo's programme charges an annual pass-through per ADS and I could not reach the depositary's own schedule, so I have bounded rather than stated it — even at $0.05 per ADS that is $0.15 a year on three shares, 0.12% of the ticket, and it cannot move the answer. It is already on pot/data-wishlist.md. The 27% Danish withholding is the statutory rate; a retail holder can in principle reclaim to the 15% treaty rate and in practice usually does not, so 27% is the conservative figure and the one used.

The flat-fee consideration does not apply here. T212 charges 0.15% at any size, so a fourth or fifth share would change the cost percentage not at all. There is no arithmetic argument for a bigger ticket; the only argument would be conviction, and §7.2a has already answered that.

2. Thesis

Novo Nordisk earned an operating margin of 42.3%, 44.2%, 44.2% and 41.3% in the four filed years to December 2025, on revenue compounding from DKK 176,954m to DKK 309,064m — 20.4% a year — and it earned that on capital rather than only on sales: ROIC 30.6%, gross profit over total assets 46.1%, asset turnover 0.569× in FY2025, after four years in which total assets more than doubled to DKK 542,902m to build the capacity this category needs. Why now: the company has raised its own 2026 outlook twice this year, most recently on 4 August 2026 from −4%/−12% to 0% to −6% at constant exchange rates on both adjusted sales and adjusted operating profit, and Q2 adjusted operating profit grew +11% CER after Q1's −6%.

What the market may be missing is arithmetic rather than opinion. The de-rating from a 31.0× median to 12.3–12.9× prices the loss of this category's economics as something already decided, and the filed accounts do not contain it yet: FY2025's operating margin is one point below FY2022's, and the decline the company itself guides for 2026 is nought to six per cent, not a collapse. The two most recent quarters are distorted in opposite directions — a DKK 26,800m non-cash 340B provision reversal inflates Q1 2026, DKK 6,300m of pipeline impairments depress Q2 2026 — so the screen that flagged this name and the headlines written about it are reading two different companies, and neither is the one filing the accounts. P5 corrects both, and the correction leaves the name in the cheapest part of its own range rather than removing the reason to look.

3. Falsifier

Both tiers test the price-versus-volume question P6 names. Neither tests a revenue line that a volume-led defence would keep green, which is the failure the brief documents on NVDA.

Warning. At the Q3 2026 result — locally dated 4 November 2026 in prices.json and flagged estimate: true, so my check deadline is 6 November 2026, not a company-confirmed date — re-read on either: (a) Novo cuts the 0% to −6% CER 2026 adjusted outlook it raised on 4 August 2026, on adjusted sales or on adjusted operating profit; or (b) the quarter's adjusted operating profit growth at CER is negative, against Q2 2026's +11%. A miss against management's own published range is the earliest hard evidence that exists, and because Novo reports sales net of US rebates, a price war reaches this line directly — it cannot hide behind volume. A warning triggers a re-read, not a sale.

Break. Assessed at the FY2026 result (check by 10 February 2027) and the Q1 2027 result (check by 12 May 2027), exit under §5.1 if either route trips:

  • (a) Price falling faster than volume, from Novo's own disclosure. Reported North America Operations obesity-care sales decline year on year at CER in two consecutive quarters while the company's own IQVIA-sourced US GLP-1 prescription-volume disclosure is flat or higher in both. That is the dominant risk stated as a number: units held, money lost. It needs no margin collapse and no guidance miss.
  • (b) The substitute taking the category — external, per Rule 3. Eli Lilly's own reported US Zepbound plus Mounjaro revenue grows year on year in both Q3 2026 and Q4 2026 (Lilly quarterly releases, Q3 late October 2026, Q4 early February 2027) while Novo's obesity-care sales decline at CER over the same two quarters. Deliberately outside Novo's filings: a category shrinking for everyone is a different fact from a rival taking it, and only the second breaks this thesis.

A redefinition of Novo's geographic or therapy-area segments, or withdrawal of the prescription-share disclosure, is a re-read and an explicit "unavailable" — never an assumed pass.

4. Review date

6 November 2026, regardless of price.

5. Numbers as of today

The own-basis derivation, shown so it can be checked. Trailing four filed quarters of net income from earnings.json: 20,006 + 26,891 + 48,557 + 20,989 = DKK 116,443m, on summed quarterly EPS of 26.19 DKK, implying 4,446m shares — which matches Novo's actual share count and confirms the arithmetic ties. Converting at rates.DKK 0.1552 gives $4.065, against the $4.09 the local file holds; the two agree to within rounding. Removing the 340B reversal at Novo's own guided 21.5% tax rate — 26,800 × 0.785 = DKK 21,038m — leaves DKK 95,405m, EPS 21.46 DKK = $3.330, a P/E of 12.93×. Adding back the Q2 impairment on the same basis (6,300 × 0.785 = DKK 4,946m) gives DKK 100,351m, EPS 22.57 DKK = $3.503, a P/E of 12.30×. Both sit 20–26% above the 10.228× floor, a little above the window's 12.019× fifth percentile, and 58–60% below the 31.045× median.

Local check — I disagree with the local figure and am using my own. prices.json holds trailing EPS of $4.09 and signals.json fired at 10.53×; that EPS contains the DKK 26,800m 340B reversal in full. I am valuing on 12.3–12.9×, not 10.53×, and the entire gap is that one non-cash item. Yahoo's normEps of $4.06 does not help: the vendor's norm for the Q1 2026 quarter equals filed net income to the krone, so it removed nothing.

Adjustments. The entry this name needs already exists and was written by the 00:32 run — NVO, fy 2026-12-31, amount DKK 26,800,000,000, sourced to Novo's own Q1 2026 announcement filed with the SEC. I have not appended a duplicate; the rule against editing the store cuts both ways.

What changed since it was written is worth stating, because it is the reason P1 sizes at half. fetch-prices.js has since gained an ownTtmEps() path that applies an adjustment recorded against the current, unfiled fiscal year to the trailing multiple — the gap the 00:32 run logged to the wishlist, now closed in code. It has taken effect on other names: TW and MWA both now carry a peLowOwn that differs from peLow. It has not taken effect on NVO — peLowOwn is 10.228× and pePctileOwn 5.5%, identical to the filed figures to the last digit. So the 12.3–12.9× above remains my hand derivation, uncorroborated by the store, across a 181-bar distribution I cannot correct name-by-name. That is a material earnings-base uncertainty, and §7.2a's answer to it is half the allocation, which is what P1 takes.

Going the other way and not recordable in this store, which only holds income to remove: Novo's DKK 6,300m of Q2 2026 pipeline impairments. It is quantified in the table and carried through the derivation above, so both corrections are visible and not only the flattering one.

Why this is not 7532.T again. Leo's stated regret was being "blinded by the tourist rebound without looking at the fundamentals, valuation, forward prospectus and yen depreciation carefully" — a real macro story, a stock that had already discounted it, and no work on the numbers underneath. The shape here is close enough to say out loud: obesity drugs are the most-narrated story in healthcare. Four differences. The narrative on this name is negative, not positive — the stock sits at a 5.5th percentile multiple, so this is not a rebound already in the price. The fundamentals are the reason for the buy and they are filed, not projected: four years of 41–44% operating margin and 30–57% ROIC. The valuation has been corrected against the company's own disclosure rather than taken off the screen, and the correction moved it 22% in the unfavourable direction — which is the test the 7532.T mistake failed. And the forward prospectus is the risk itself, not an afterthought: it is what P6 names and what P3 tests, with the rival's own numbers as the external check. This run also looked hard at the actual 7532.T, on the actual evidence, and ranked it WAIT — see the ranking.

6. The case against

Theses: none. T1 concerns the price of frontier-model inference and the margin of whoever sells it; Novo neither sells nor resells models, and buys no material AI input whose price is the question. T2 concerns software priced per seat where the seat maps to a task; Novo sells a manufactured molecule under patent to health systems, with no seat and no per-user pricing anywhere in the model. Neither bears — and because neither bears, Rule 5 does not bind: this cheapness is not a declared thesis showing up as a discount. I have argued the discount anyway in P2, because a de-rating from 31× to 12.5× deserves an explanation whichever rule is in force.

Dominant risk (competitive): Eli Lilly's orally dosed orforglipron and its next-generation injectable take the marginal obesity patient, and Novo defends on price — so US prescription volumes hold or grow while realised net price per script falls faster, contracting revenue and the 41% operating margin together.

Earliest observable: Novo's own Q3 2026 result, which gives North America Operations obesity-care sales at CER together with the company's volume-versus-price split — locally dated 4 November 2026 (prices.json, estimate: true, so my deadline is 6 November). Eli Lilly's Q3 2026 release, carrying US Zepbound and Mounjaro revenue, arrives in late October 2026. Both are inside two quarters, so Rule 4 does not size this down; the half allocation in P1 comes from §7.2a alone.

Then the secondary arguments, written to persuade rather than to dismiss:

  • The de-rating may be right and early rather than wrong. Novo's ROIC has fallen in a straight line for three years — 56.6% → 41.1% → 30.6% — while total assets more than doubled. A 41% margin invites competition by definition, and this is what the first stage of that looks like on a balance sheet. The P2 case rests on returns that are, on the record, in decline. "Still 30%" is a comfort, not a trend.
  • US pricing is under attack from more directions than Lilly. The 340B reversal in P5 is itself evidence of how much of Novo's US revenue is a negotiated rebate rather than a price; most-favoured- nation pricing proposals and direct-to-consumer cash channels push the same way. A company whose reported sales can move DKK 26,800m on a provision estimate is a company whose realised price is not a fact you can read off a label.
  • Patent expiry is dated and known. Semaglutide's protection lapses first outside the US — Canada and China from 2026 — before the US cliff early in the next decade. Generic entry in large non-US markets is not a risk to discover; it is a schedule.
  • The pipeline write-off. DKK 4,000m of the Q2 impairment was monlunabant, a compound the company was presenting as a pipeline asset a year ago. Writing off your own next thing is the most expensive sentence in a results release.
  • What this does to Leo's total exposure — the §3.3 disclosure. Novo Nordisk appears nowhere in the human book: not in signals.json → book.names, which prices 60 of 60 positions totalling £128,687, nor in byCompany. So this adds an exposure rather than concentrating one — the opposite of NVDA's case, which sits at 7.15% of the book and has been proposed seven times. On geography the book is 66.88% US; a Danish issuer bought through a US depositary receipt is a European economic exposure in a US-listed wrapper. Healthcare appears nowhere in the book at a weight worth naming. This is a disclosure and not an argument — diversification is not a thesis either, and the name still has to win on the numbers in P2 and P3.

Run report — 12 September 2026, 00:32 UTC

One proposal: BUY 3 NVO, £95.51 of the £447.30 in the pot. The substantive finding of the run is not that one. It is that Tradeweb's cheapness is a crypto token mark, and that the store built to catch exactly this had sat empty of both its flagged entries for four days while the name was proposed twelve times.

What this run had to work with

  • Cash £447.30; contributed capital to date £500 across 4 and 8 September; holdings 3 MWA at $23.76, £53.09 at the current mark. pot/positions.json, generated 2026-09-11T23:42:10Z.
  • The newest Sweep, 11 September 23:55: five candidates, of which it told you to buy none — Wärtsilä as the only genuine new name, Lancashire and CF as re-looks, Saipem as "watch, do not buy", Beazley for completeness. Its own closing judgement on the energy void was that "the obvious vehicles have already run".
  • The newest Review, 11 September 23:46: hold MWA, no instruction, and one explicit hand-off — "the $0.06 was never written where fetch-prices.js could subtract it… It is an open loop for the Deep dive."
  • The Scan, signals.json generated 2026-09-12T00:25:27Z over prices struck the same moment: 6.1 valuation fired on 25 names, of which 14 are watchlist names and one is the held MWA. 6.2 drawdown fired on BBW. 6.3 results, 6.4 dry powder, 6.6 news proxy and the 11.1 VIX standing order are all quiet — VIX 15.84.
  • pot/theses.md — T1 and T2. Between them they bear on REL.L, INTU and WLY, all three of which sit in the ranked tier below, and on nothing that was proposed.

The Sweep's five candidates all fail §2.4 before any business work is needed, and it is worth saying plainly rather than burying it in the excluded list: Wärtsilä 25.8× against a 17.4× floor and the 12.5th percentile, Lancashire the 89.1st, CF the 96.7th, Saipem the 84.4th, Beazley the 99.5th. That is not a criticism of the Sweep — it said as much about four of the five itself, and the prices were provisional when it wrote. It is the confirmation, now that all three new names are locally covered, that this week's candidate flow and this week's valuation filter point in opposite directions. §4.4 makes leaving that cash a position; the pot did.

The ranking

Ranked: 15. Excluded: 67. Total: 82, which is every name in watchlist.json. The line between the tiers is objective rather than chosen: a name is ranked if 6.1 valuation fired on it in the 00:25 UTC scan — the repo's own implementation of §2.4's cheapest-decile filter — and excluded if it did not.
