25.8× against a 17.4× floor, so the 27% fall from its high has not made it cheap on its own history · SPM.MI — 84.4th, a Sweep candidate already labelled "watch, do not buy" at +82.6% over a year · BEZ.L — 99.5th, a Sweep candidate listed by the Sweep itself as a benchmark rather than a buy, at its 52-week high.

15 ranked + 67 excluded = 82 = the watchlist count.

What the run decided, and why

Tradeweb is not cheap, and has not been since February

This is the finding. signals.json fires TW at 24.21×, the 1.1st percentile of 261 weeks, 4.8% above a 23.09× floor. That multiple is computed on trailing EPS of $4.19, and the four quarters behind it include Q4 2025.

In Q4 2025 Tradeweb booked $205.4m of realised and unrealised gains on Canton Coin holdings in Other income (loss), net — a non-operating line — inside total non-operating other income of $207.1m. For the full year the figure was $270.9m, against operating income of $835.3m. Its own release states income before taxes of $1,174.974m, a 21.6% effective rate, consolidated net income of $921.500m and $812.792m attributable to Tradeweb Markets Inc. (Q4/FY2025 release, 8-K exhibit 99.1). At 31 December 2025 it held 1.6 billion Canton Coins worth $242.7m.

Tax-effecting the Q4 gain at the quarter's own 19.6% rate and allocating it in the same 88.5% proportion the filing uses for that quarter leaves roughly $146m of the $897.2m trailing attributable net income that is a token mark. Trailing EPS becomes about $3.51 rather than $4.19, and the multiple ~28.9× against a 23.09× floor — 25% above it, out of the cheapest decile and nowhere near a signal. Yahoo's norm for FY2025 equals filed attributable net income to the dollar, so the vendor removed nothing and the oneOff flag never fired.

Twelve TW proposals have been written on that number, each one refining thresholds on fees per million and TRACE share while the denominator underneath was wrong. The entry is now in pot/adjustments.json with the company's own release as its source, so the next fetch-prices.js run will build a peLowOwn/pePctileOwn band for TW — fy 2025-12-31 exists in earnings.json, so unlike the other two entries written today this one will actually bite.

Nothing here is a sell instruction: no TW proposal was ever accepted and the pot holds none.

The two open loops are closed

pot/adjustments.json went from one entry to four this run.

  • MWA, fy 2026-09-30, amountPerShare $0.06 — "a one-time tax benefit resulting from the recognition of a loss on a foreign subsidiary investment", the company's own words in its Q3 FY2026 release. Found by the 8 September run, re-derived and discarded by every run since, flagged by last night's Review and by Leo's own note. Corrected, MWA is 17.60× against its 16.859× floor. The same release quantifies no separate tariff-refund amount — it names tariff refunds only as one of several drivers of higher pricing — so no second entry was writable, which is the answer to a question three proposals have left open.
  • TW, fy 2025-12-31, $270.9m, as above.
  • NVO, fy 2026-12-31, DKK 26.8bn — the 340B rebate-provision reversal, from Novo's own Q1 2026 announcement.

§5 — a data-quality finding worth more than one proposal

pot/adjustments.json keys on filed fiscal-year rows; the multiple that fires 6.1 does not. adjustedYears() in fetch-prices.js matches an entry when a.fy === y.date for a year row in earnings.json. Two of the three entries written today — MWA's fiscal 2026, which ends 30 September 2026, and Novo's 2026 — fall in fiscal years that are not filed yet, so they match no row and do nothing until those accounts land. Both one-offs are nevertheless sitting inside the trailing four quarters that produce the EPS the signal fires on, today.

So the store cannot correct the screen in precisely the window where a one-off is freshest and the agent is most likely to be fooled by it. The entries are still worth writing — they stop the work being thrown away a fifth time, and they will apply on schedule — but the gap is real and it is logged to pot/data-wishlist.md rather than asserted as a bug, because it may be a deliberate choice about only adjusting audited years.

Second finding, smaller: peWeeks is under three years for five ranked or near-ranked names — RSGN.SW 144, GME 129, AMSC 84, GWRE 46, MRVL 41 — and peWindow says "5y" for all of them. RSGN.SW is the one already handled through HISTORY_FROM; the others are simply short vendor histories rather than business changes, so nothing needs adding to fetch-prices.js. Stated here so the label is never read as a measurement.

Why only one proposal

After NVO the pot holds £351.79. The brief says keep going while cash remains and a candidate still clears — and none does. Ranks 3 through 9 are all WAIT, and in six of the seven cases the thing that is missing arrives on a date I can name: R&S's H1 on 16 September, Intuit's investor day on 17 September, RELX's nine-month update on 22 October, MWA's FY2026 on 5 November, PDD's Q3 on 18 November. Ranks 10 through 15 fail on capital returns, on absolute price, or on the venue.

§4.4 makes holding the rest a position rather than an omission, and the 11.1 standing order is quiet with VIX at 15.84 — that cash is what it will need if it is not.

NVO — Novo Nordisk A/S (New York-listed ADR)

What it does: Novo Nordisk discovers, manufactures and sells prescription medicines, overwhelmingly injectable and oral peptides. Two product families carry it: GLP-1 medicines for type 2 diabetes and for obesity (Ozempic, Rybelsus, Wegovy, including an oral Wegovy tablet), and insulins. It sells to national health systems, hospital groups and, in the United States, to insurers and pharmacy benefit managers through rebated list prices and increasingly direct to patients for cash; it manufactures the active ingredient and the devices in its own plants in Denmark, the US and France. Revenue is patented drug sales; cost is a very large and still-growing factory estate.

Ranking for this run: 2026-09-12-0032-ranking.md.

1. Order

BUY 3 shares of NVO on the NYSE, £95.51 of a £125 allocation, market order. Currency USD. Cash left idle: £351.79 (pot cash £447.30 before the order).

  • Price $43.07 → £31.8353 at prices.json rates (USD 1 ÷ GBP 1.3529). 3 × £31.8353 = £95.51. A fourth share would cost £127.34 and break the £125 allocation, so the order stops at three and £29.49 of the allocation is left undeployed alongside the £351.79 of unallocated cash.
  • Why £125 and not £250. §4.2's cap is 50% of contributed capital to date (£500), which is £250. I am taking half of that under §7.2a, not under Rule 4. Rule 4 does not bite — the dominant risk in P6 has an observable inside two quarters (Novo's Q3 2026 result, locally dated 4 November 2026). §7.2a does bite: see the Adjustments paragraph in P5. One of the four filed years carries a cited adjustment and it is not even a filed year yet, so the 5.5th-percentile screen reading is computed on a base I have corrected for today and cannot correct across the 181 weekly bars behind it. Half the allocation is the written default for exactly that, and I am not arguing my way out of it.
  • Resulting concentration: £95.51 is 19.1% of the £500 contributed to date, and 17.5% of the pot's £500.39 mark-to-market including the three MWA shares. Comfortably inside §4.2; nothing here invokes §4.2a or §4.2b.

Expected first-year costs — broker assumed is Trading 212, which lists NVO as a US-listed ADR, so §10's default applies and the IBKR schedule is not the relevant one.

Two honest gaps in that table. The ADR depositary's service fee is not sourced in this run — Novo's ADR programme charges an annual pass-through per ADS and I could not reach the depositary's own schedule, so I have bounded rather than stated it: even at $0.05 per ADS per year it is $0.15 on three shares, 0.12% of the ticket, and it cannot move the answer. It is logged to pot/data-wishlist.md. The Danish withholding rate of 27% is the statutory rate; a retail holder can in principle reclaim down to the 15% treaty rate and in practice generally does not, so 27% is the conservative number and the one I have used.

On the flat-fee consideration (§4.1-adjacent): it does not apply. T212 charges 0.15% at any size, so buying a fourth or fifth share changes the cost percentage not at all, and there is no arithmetic argument here for a bigger ticket. The only argument for more shares would be conviction, and §7.2a has already answered that.

2. Thesis

Novo Nordisk has earned a 41–44% operating margin in each of the last four filed years — 42.3%, 44.2%, 44.2%, 41.3% on revenue that compounded from DKK 176.9bn to DKK 309.1bn, a 20.4% annual rate — and it earned that on capital, not just on sales: ROIC 30.6%, gross profit over total assets 46.1%, asset turnover 0.569× in FY2025, after four years in which total assets more than doubled to DKK 542.9bn to build the capacity the GLP-1 category needs. Why now: the company has raised its own 2026 outlook twice this year, most recently on 4 August 2026 from −4%/−12% to 0% to −6% at CER on both adjusted sales and adjusted operating profit, and Q2 adjusted operating profit grew +11% CER after Q1's −6% — while the shares trade at 12.3–12.9× recurring earnings against a 31.0× five-year median, a 60% de-rating.

What the market may be missing is arithmetic rather than opinion: the de-rating prices the loss of this category's economics as already decided, and the filed accounts do not yet contain it. The operating margin in FY2025 was one point below FY2022's. The decline the company itself guides for 2026 is nought to six per cent, not a collapse. And the two most recent quarters are distorted in opposite directions — a DKK 26.8bn non-cash 340B provision reversal inflates Q1 2026, DKK 6.3bn of pipeline impairments depress Q2 2026 — so the screen that flagged this name and the headlines written about it are reading two different companies, neither of which is the one filing the accounts. Correcting both is what P5 does, and it leaves the name still in the cheapest part of its own range rather than removing the reason to look.

3. Falsifier

Both tiers test the price-versus-volume question P6 names, not a revenue line that a volume-led defence would keep green.

Warning. At the Q3 2026 result — locally dated 4 November 2026 in prices.json, flagged estimate: true and therefore my check deadline of 6 November 2026, not a company-confirmed date — re-read on either: (a) Novo cuts the 2026 adjusted outlook of 0% to −6% CER on adjusted sales or adjusted operating profit that it raised on 4 August 2026; or (b) the quarter's adjusted operating profit growth at CER is negative, against Q2 2026's +11%. A miss against management's own published range is the earliest hard evidence that exists, and because Novo reports sales net of US rebates, a price war reaches this line — it does not hide behind volume the way NVDA's financed demand hid behind revenue. A warning triggers a re-read at the next review, not a sale.

Break. Assessed at the FY2026 result (check by 10 February 2027) and the Q1 2027 result (check by 12 May 2027), exit under §5.1 if either route trips:

  • (a) Price falling faster than volume, from Novo's own disclosure. Reported North America Operations obesity-care sales decline year on year at CER in two consecutive quarters while the company's own IQVIA-sourced US GLP-1 prescription-volume disclosure is flat or higher in both. That is the dominant risk stated as a number: units held, money lost. It requires no margin collapse and no guidance miss.
  • (b) The substitute taking the category — external, per Rule 3. Eli Lilly's own reported US Zepbound plus Mounjaro revenue grows year on year in both Q3 2026 and Q4 2026 (Lilly quarterly releases, Q3 late October 2026, Q4 early February 2027) while Novo's obesity-care sales decline at CER over the same two quarters. This is deliberately outside Novo's filings: a category that is shrinking for everyone is a different fact from a rival taking it, and only the second one breaks this thesis.

A redefinition of Novo's geographic or therapy-area segments, or the withdrawal of the prescription-share disclosure, is a re-read and an explicit "unavailable", never an assumed pass.

4. Review date

6 November 2026, regardless of price.

5. Numbers as of today

The own-basis derivation, shown so it can be checked. Trailing four quarters of filed net profit (earnings.json): 20,006 + 26,891 + 48,557 + 20,989 = DKK 116,443m, on 26.19 DKK of summed quarterly EPS, implying 4,446m shares — which matches Novo's actual share count and confirms the arithmetic. Removing the 340B reversal at Novo's own guided 21.5% tax rate: 26,800 × 0.785 = DKK 21,038m, leaving DKK 95,405m, EPS 21.46 DKK = $3.331 at rates.DKK 0.1552, a P/E of 12.93×. Adding back the Q2 impairment on the same basis (6,300 × 0.785 = DKK 4,946m) gives DKK 100,351m, EPS 22.57 DKK = $3.503, a P/E of 12.30×. Both sit 20–26% above the 10.228× floor, a little above the window's 12.019× fifth percentile, and 58–60% below the 31.045× median.

Local check — disagree, and I am using my own figure. prices.json holds trailing EPS of $4.08 and signals.json fired at 10.56×; that EPS contains the DKK 26.8bn 340B reversal in full. I am valuing on 12.3–12.9×, not 10.56×, and the whole gap is that one non-cash item. Yahoo's normEps of $4.06 does not help: the vendor's norm for the Q1 2026 quarter equals filed net income to the krone, so it removed nothing. This is the third name in two days where the vendor's "recurring" figure and the filed figure are the same number with different labels.

Adjustments. Appended to pot/adjustments.json in this run:

  • NVO, fy 2026-12-31, amount DKK 26,800,000,000 — the 340B rebate-provision reversal, sourced to Novo's own Q1 2026 announcement filed with the SEC. Pre-tax, by the same convention as the LULU entry. FY2026 is not yet a filed year in earnings.json, so this entry matches no row and is inert until the FY2026 accounts land — which is a limitation of the store, not of the reconciliation, and is written up in the ranking file's §5 and logged to the wishlist.
  • Two further entries were written in the same run for names ranked but not proposed: TW, fy 2025-12-31, $270.9m of Canton Coin gains, and MWA, fy 2026-09-30, amountPerShare $0.06. The TW one changes that name's verdict; see the ranking.
  • Going the other way and not recordable in this store, which only holds income to remove: Novo's DKK 6.3bn of Q2 2026 pipeline impairments. It is quantified in the table above and carried explicitly through the derivation, so the reader can see both corrections rather than only the flattering one.

Why this is not 7532.T again. Leo's stated regret was being "blinded by the tourist rebound without looking at the fundamentals, valuation, forward prospectus and yen depreciation carefully" — a real macro story, a stock that had already discounted it, and no work on the numbers underneath. The shape here is close enough to say out loud: obesity drugs are the most-narrated story in healthcare. Four differences. The narrative on this name is negative, not positive — the stock is down to a 5.5th-percentile multiple, so I am not buying a rebound that is already in the price. The fundamentals are the reason for the buy and they are filed, not projected: four years of 41–44% operating margin and 30–57% ROIC. The valuation has been corrected against the company's own disclosure rather than taken from the screen, and the correction moved it 22% in the unfavourable direction, which is the test the 7532.T mistake failed. And the forward prospectus is the risk, not an afterthought: it is what P6 names and what P3 tests, with the rival's own numbers as the check.

6. The case against

Theses: none. T1 is about the price of frontier-model inference and the margin of who sells it; Novo neither sells nor resells models. T2 is about software priced per seat where the seat maps to a task; Novo sells a manufactured molecule under patent to health systems, with no seat and no per-user pricing anywhere in the model. Neither bears, and because neither bears, Rule 5 does not bind here — the cheapness is not a declared thesis showing up as a discount. I have argued the discount anyway, in P2, because a de-rating from 31× to 12.5× deserves an explanation whichever rule is or is not in force.

Dominant risk (competitive): Eli Lilly's orally dosed orforglipron and its next-generation injectable take the marginal obesity patient, and Novo defends on price — so US prescription volumes hold or grow while realised net price per script falls faster, contracting revenue and the 41% operating margin together.

Earliest observable: Novo's own Q3 2026 result, giving reported North America Operations obesity-care sales at CER and the company's volume-versus-price split — locally dated 4 November 2026 (prices.json, estimate: true, so my deadline is 6 November). Eli Lilly's Q3 2026 release, with US Zepbound and Mounjaro revenue, arrives in late October 2026. Both are inside two quarters, so Rule 4 does not size this down; the half allocation in P1 comes from §7.2a and nothing else.

Then the secondary arguments, written to persuade:

  • The de-rating may be right and early rather than wrong. Novo's ROIC has fallen in a straight line for three years — 56.6% → 41.1% → 30.6% — while total assets more than doubled. A margin of 41% invites competition by definition, and this is what the first stage of that looks like on the balance sheet. The P2 case rests on returns that are, on the record, in decline; "still 30%" is a comfort, not a trend.
  • US pricing is under attack from more directions than Lilly. The 340B reversal in P5 is itself evidence of how much of Novo's US revenue is a negotiated rebate rather than a price, and most-favoured-nation pricing proposals and direct-to-consumer cash channels all push the same way. A company whose reported sales can move DKK 26.8bn on a provision estimate is a company whose realised price is not a fact you can read off a label.
  • Patent expiry is dated and known. Semaglutide's protection lapses first outside the US — Canada and China from 2026 — before the US cliff early in the next decade. Generic entry in large non-US markets is not a risk to discover; it is a schedule.
  • The management change and the pipeline. DKK 4.0bn of the Q2 impairment was monlunabant, a compound the company was presenting as a pipeline asset a year ago. Writing off your own next thing is the most expensive sentence in a results release.
  • What this does to Leo's total exposure — the §3.3 disclosure. Novo Nordisk appears nowhere in the human book: it is not in signals.json → book.names, which prices 60 of 60 positions totalling £128,690, nor in byCompany. So this adds a new exposure rather than concentrating an existing one — the opposite of NVDA's case, which sits at 7.15% of the book and has been proposed seven times. On geography the book is 66.88% US against 6.29% Europe, and a Danish issuer bought through a US depositary receipt is a European economic exposure in a US-listed wrapper. Healthcare does not appear in the book's sector tail at any weight worth naming. This is a disclosure and not an argument: diversification is not a thesis either, and the name has to win on the numbers above, which is what P2 and P3 are for.

TW — Tradeweb Markets

What it does: Tradeweb operates electronic marketplaces where banks, asset managers and other institutions trade bonds, rates products, derivatives and money-market instruments. It earns transaction fees on that activity plus subscriptions for access, market data and analytics. Company release.

Decision dated 11 September 2026, 17:15 UTC. This run's ranking and allocation.

1. Order

BUY 1 share of TW on Nasdaq, limit $102.00, through Trading 212 Invest/ISA, regular session 11 September 2026; cancel at the close if unfilled, do not chase.

At rates 1.352 USD/GBP, deploy at most £75.44 before fees from a £125 allocation. FX ~£0.11; total debit ~£75.55. Cash £447.29 → £371.74 if this alone fills, £282.66 if the companion MWA order also fills. Retain the £125 all-in budget if FX moves.

Normal allocation is £250 (50% of £500 contributed). §7.2a halves it to £125 because neither local earnings basis reliably removes the FY2025 investment gains (below), so the multiple is provisional. One share is 15.1% of contributed capital; two would cost £150.88 before FX, past the reduced allocation, for no change in the percentage fee. TW takes priority over the MWA top-up under §4.5a as the fresh name.

Expected first-year costs: £0 commission, 0.15% entry FX, £0 custody, no ADR fee — ~0.15% of the ticket. No UK stamp duty on a US share; transaction tax £0. Clears the 0.5% broker gate (§4.1a) and 2% first-year ceiling (§4.1). Sources: T212 availability, fees, FX, HMRC, cash, FX.

2. Thesis

Tradeweb sells access to trading counterparties and execution, so electronic migration flows into transaction revenue rather than depending on selling more software seats. Local annual revenue rose $1.338bn (2023) → $2.052bn (2025) and corrected filed operating margin rose 39.28% (FY24) → 40.70% (FY25): this is an existing profitable franchise, not a bet on an AI market forming. The reported multiple is ~56% below its local five-year median, plausibly discounting lasting fee compression; the case that the discount is too severe rests on continued conversion of electronic activity into operating profit — supported by the August volume data below but explicitly conditional on P3, not on an assumption that automation cannot erode the franchise.

That is the 7532.T check: no trade-volume headline substitutes for fees, filed operating income, or the capital required to earn them. Capital productivity is only partly visible locally (turnover 0.25×, ROIC and gross-profit-over-assets blank), so a high margin does not earn a full allocation.

3. Falsifier

My decision thresholds, not management guidance. They test monetisation and customer loss even if total volume keeps growing — i.e. they answer the competitive dominant risk directly, not revenue-vs-guidance.

Warning: Review the September monthly activity release by 12 October 2026. Re-read if fully electronic US high-grade TRACE share falls below 17.0% (August 19.0%), or Tradeweb reports an adverse change to transaction pricing. At Q3 results, dated 29 October, also warn if credit revenue growth is non-positive or lags credit ADV growth by more than 12 percentage points (the Q2 gap was ~10). A mix change may explain a warning; it does not erase it.

Break: By 28 February 2027, exit under §5.1 if either (a) Q3 and Q4 each show falling year-on-year credit revenue despite non-declining credit ADV, or (b) company-wide filed GAAP operating margin is below 35% in both quarters, independent of volumes. A further break is fully electronic US high-grade share below 15% in three consecutive post-entry monthly reports. Separate routes, so healthy headline volume or another division cannot conceal lost pricing or customers.

Outside-company check (Rule 3, competitive): MarketAxess quarterly credit fee per million, $129 vs $138 in Q2; next by 15 November 2026. A ≥10% YoY fall warns of category-wide pricing pressure even if TW's share holds. FINRA monthly TRACE volumes are the independent market denominator — Tradeweb's published shares are issuer estimates. Compare directions; never splice the two firms' different product mixes into one fee series.

4. Review date

12 October 2026 (monthly release), then 2 November 2026 for Q3 economics, regardless of price. The 28 Feb 2027 break assessment is a review deadline, not an announced earnings date.

5. Numbers as of today

Local snapshot 11 September 2026, 17:03 UTC; the TW price carries the prior US regular close.

Local check — material disagreement on operating-income classification. Local FY2025 opinc is $845.124m, including a $9.786m tax-receivable adjustment sitting below operating income; use $835.338m for the operating thesis (FY2024 has the matching $7.730m difference). Q2 agrees. The issuer's adjusted EPS excludes investment gains but also adds back costs — a comparison, not certified owner earnings — so I do not assign its ~26.8× a percentile from a different basis. The local screen is provisional evidence sufficient for the reduced allocation under §7.2a, not a certified historical bargain.

Adjustments: FY2025's release identifies $205.4m of Q4 Canton Coin gains, before tax and minority allocation. No safe net-income adjustment is writable from that gross figure alone, so nothing is appended to adjustments.json and zero TW years carry cited adjustments. No amount is subtracted from filed EPS here; the uncertainty is priced by the half allocation.

6. The case against

Theses: T2 — automated workflows can compress research/access pricing and execution fees; T1 — cheaper models lower the cost of building competing trading interfaces. Both are hypotheses about economics, not proof that transaction-based execution is equivalent to seat software.

Dominant risk (competitive): execution becomes easier to substitute and lower-fee protocols capture the growth, so activity expands without enough profit for shareholders.

Earliest observable: Tradeweb's monthly share/protocol mix (next 12 October) and MarketAxess's quarterly credit fee per million (by 15 November), per P3. The August release already flags portfolio trading as lower-fee; both observables are within two quarters, so Rule 4 imposes no extra haircut. T1 has no separately attributable adoption series for TW — it is a possible cause of the same pricing pressure, not a claimed measured tailwind, and Rule 2 keeps that answer in P3 rather than in the thesis.

Secondary: LSEG control, investment gains obscuring ordinary earnings, and a weakly observed return on the acquired asset base (ROIC and GPA blank locally). A trading network may defend margins through counterparty access and integrations — a hypothesis to keep testing, not a guarantee.

Combined exposure: TW is absent from the human book (0%); the pot does not hold it either. The buy adds to a book already 66.9% US (book.byGeography), but a different business from the four large tech positions. Disclosure, not a gate.

MWA — Mueller Water Products

What it does: Mueller supplies valves, hydrants, meters and related equipment for water systems, mainly across North America. Utilities and distributors buy the gear to build, maintain and measure water networks. Company release.

Decision dated 11 September 2026, 17:15 UTC. This run's ranking and allocation. A new top-up thesis; it does not replace the accepted three-share position's falsifier or the latest Review verdict.

1. Order

BUY 5 additional shares of MWA on NYSE, limit $24.05, through Trading 212 Invest/ISA, regular session 11 September 2026, cancelling at the close if unfilled. The pot would then hold 8 shares.

At rates 1.352 USD/GBP, deploy at most £88.94, plus ~£0.13 FX, total ~£89.07. The three held shares mark at 3 × $24.00 ÷ 1.352 = £53.25, so incremental headroom to £250 is £196.75. §7.2a halves that to a £98.37 allocation because tariff benefits and operating-income classification (below) weaken the apparent earnings quality. Unused allocation after the ticket: ~£9.43. Cash £447.29 → £358.22 if this alone fills, £282.66 if TW also fills.

Eight shares are 28.4% of £500 contributed, comfortably below the 50% cap; no one-share or fee exception is used. A sixth share would exceed the reduced allocation for no fee benefit. §4.5a: TW, the fresh name of comparable merit, takes its allocation first; this smaller top-up follows because the other fresh candidates (RELX, INTU, NVO, RSGN) each still await a dated checkpoint. It does not take MWA to the cap.

Expected first-year costs: £0 commission, 0.15% FX, £0 custody, no ADR fee — ~0.15% of the ticket. Transaction tax £0 (US share). Clears §4.1a (0.5%) and §4.1 (2%). Sources: availability, fees, FX, HMRC, prices, book.

2. Thesis

Water-network replacement gives Mueller a recurring physical use case, while expanded foundries create room to earn more from the existing product and distribution base. Filed FY2023–25 operating margin improved 9.99% → 13.82% → 18.23% as sales rose $1,275.7m → $1,429.7m — evidence across several years, not one strong quarter. The proposed return comes from converting that operating improvement into cash on the factory investment; the market may under-credit that conversion, but the newest quarter's price-led sales and exceptional benefits make it a testable opportunity at reduced size, not a finished success.

Why this is not 7532.T: essential infrastructure is the opening observation, not the buy argument. The corrected margin series, explicit capital and cash denominators, half allocation and a standalone cash break stop the "water spending" story standing in for earnings quality. Equipment compatibility and utility qualification could support persistence; they do not make the margin unassailable.

3. Falsifier

New-share decision thresholds, except the 70% cash-conversion reference, which is management's stated full-year expectation. They do not amend the accepted trade's conditions.

Warning: At FY2026 results, locally estimated 5 November (review by 10 November 2026), re-read if consolidated volumes decline again, or FY free cash flow ÷ company-reconciled adjusted net income is 70% or less, or the asset-return measure below is under 10%. Use GAAP operating income after restructuring and impairments. Define the asset-return check as trailing-four-quarter GAAP operating income × 0.75 ÷ average of opening and closing total assets — an after-tax operating return on assets (the 0.75 is a fixed analytical factor, not a claimed tax rate), giving factory investment a denominator margin lacks. Record the FY baseline at the November review.

Break: Sell the five-share tranche under §5.1 if any one occurs: (a) FY2026 free cash flow is below 50% of reconciled adjusted net income; (b) the asset-return measure is below 8% at both 30 Sep and 31 Dec 2026; or (c) filed GAAP operating margin is below 18% in both post-entry quarters. Assess September at FY results, December at Q1 FY2027, no later than 28 February 2027. None requires volumes to fall too — pricing cannot keep a failing capital/cash test green. This is the standalone capital-return break the 10-Sep Review asked for. Missing accounts prompt an urgent re-read, not a fabricated ratio.

4. Review date

10 November 2026, regardless of price (the local 5 November date is an estimate). Final two-quarter assessment by 28 February 2027, a review deadline not an announced result date.

6. The case against

Dominant risk (financial): expanded factories absorb capital while pricing and exceptional benefits make the income statement look stronger than the underlying cash return.

Earliest observable: FY2026 cash conversion and assets in the November annual release, then December-quarter accounts by February 2027 — within two quarters, so Rule 4 adds no reduction. P3 can break on poor cash conversion or falling asset returns while sales and margins still look healthy.

The latest release attributes part of the improvement to price and refunds while consolidated volumes were lower; there is no assurance utility spending fills the new capacity economically, and today's local ROIC is not a clean filed return. Adding to a recently bought holding raises the cost of being wrong before any post-entry result exists — the limited top-up is a choice, not a reward for a one-day move.

TW — Tradeweb Markets

What it does: Tradeweb runs electronic marketplaces where banks, asset managers and other institutions trade bonds, derivatives and other securities. It earns transaction fees and subscriptions for trading access, market data and related services. Company description.

Decision dated 11 September 2026. This run's ranking and allocation.

1. Order

BUY 1 share of TW on Nasdaq, limit $102.50, through Trading 212 Invest/ISA, during the regular session on 11 September 2026. Cancel at that session's close if unfilled; do not chase. This is a proposal for Leo to execute.

At local USD-per-GBP 1.3507, deploy at most £75.89 before fees from a £125 allocation. FX costs approximately £0.11; total debit £76.00. Unused allocation after fees: £49.00. Cash from the current £447.22 book becomes £371.22 if this alone fills, or £283.36 after the companion MWA order also fills. FX can change: retain the £125 all-in budget.

Normal allocation is £250, 50% of £500 contributed. §7.2a halves it to £125 because neither local earnings basis reliably removes the investment gains below. One share is 15.18% of contributed capital. No concentration exception is used. Two shares would cost £151.77 before FX, exceeding the reduced allocation, while leaving the percentage fee unchanged. TW receives priority over the MWA top-up under §4.5a.

Expected first-year dealing and holding costs: £0 commission, 0.15% entry FX, £0 custody and no ADR fee, approximately 0.15% of the ticket for buy-and-hold. No UK stamp duty on this US share purchase; transaction tax £0. Dividend withholding is tax on income, not a broker charge. A future sale is not instructed or included. The bid/ask spread is not known; the limit bounds the purchase price. Both the broker-fee ceiling of 0.5% and first-year cost ceiling of 2% clear. Sources: TW availability, broker fees, FX schedule, HMRC, cash, FX.

2. Thesis

Tradeweb sells access to trading counterparties and execution, giving electronic migration a route into transaction revenue rather than relying solely on selling more software seats. Local annual revenue rose from $1.338bn in 2023 to $2.052bn in 2025, while the corrected filed operating margin rose from 39.28% in 2024 to 40.70% in 2025: this is an existing profitable business, not a forecast of an AI market. The reported multiple is 55.9% below its local historical median, plausibly discounting lasting fee compression; the argument that this discount is too severe rests on continued conversion of electronic activity into operating profit, supported by the latest observations below but explicitly conditional on P3, rather than an assumption that automation cannot undermine the franchise.

That is the 7532.T check: no trade-volume headline substitutes for fees, filed operating income or the capital required to generate them. Capital productivity is only partly measured locally, so a high margin does not earn a full allocation.

3. Falsifier

The thresholds below are my decision thresholds, not management guidance. They test monetisation and loss of customers even if total trading volume keeps growing.

Warning: Review the September monthly release by 12 October 2026. Trigger a re-read if fully electronic US high-grade share falls below 17.0%, versus August's 19.0%, or if Tradeweb reports an adverse change to transaction pricing. At Q3 results, locally dated 29 October, also warn if credit revenue growth is non-positive, or lags credit ADV growth by more than 12 percentage points. The Q2 gap was about 10 points. A mix change may explain a warning; it does not silently erase it.

Break: By 28 February 2027, exit this proposed position under §5.1 if either (a) Q3 and Q4 each show falling year-on-year credit revenue despite non-declining credit ADV, or (b) company-wide filed GAAP operating margin is below 35% in both quarters, independently of volumes. A further break is fully electronic US high-grade share below 15% in three consecutive post-entry monthly reports. These are separate routes, so healthy headline volume or another division cannot automatically conceal lost pricing or customers.

Outside-company check: read MarketAxess's quarterly credit fee per million, $129 versus $138 in Q2, next checked by 15 November 2026. A year-on-year fall of at least 10% warns of category-wide pricing pressure even if TW's market share holds. Compare directions, never splice the two firms' different product mixes into one fee series. FINRA's monthly TRACE volumes provide the independent market denominator; Tradeweb's published shares remain issuer estimates. Missing or redefined disclosures require a re-read, not an invented pass.

4. Review date

12 October 2026, regardless of price, then 2 November 2026 for Q3 economics. The 28 February 2027 break assessment is a review deadline, not an announced earnings date.

5. Numbers as of today

Local check: material disagreement in earnings quality and operating-income classification. Local FY2025 opinc is $845.124m, including the $9.786m tax-receivable liability adjustment below operating income; use $835.338m for the operating thesis. FY2024 has the matching $7.730m difference. Q2 figures agree. The issuer's adjusted EPS excludes investment gains but also adds back costs; it is a comparison, not certified owner earnings. I do not assign its 27.04× a percentile from a different basis. The local screen is provisional evidence sufficient for the reduced allocation under §7.2a, not a certified historical bargain.

Adjustments: FY2025's release identifies $205.4m of Q4 Canton Coin gains, before tax and minority allocation. No safe net-income adjustment is writable from that gross figure alone, and zero TW years carry cited adjustments in the shared store. No amount is subtracted from filed EPS here. The report records the reconciliation and the brief's proposals-only write restriction; it does not falsely claim the store was updated.

6. The case against

Theses: T2, automated workflows can compress research/access pricing and execution fees; T1, cheaper models lower the cost of building competing interfaces. These are hypotheses about economics, not proof that transaction-based execution is equivalent to seat software.

Dominant risk (competitive): Execution becomes easier to substitute and lower-fee trading protocols capture the growth, so activity expands without sufficient profit for shareholders.

Earliest observable: Tradeweb's monthly share/protocol mix, next assessed 12 October, and MarketAxess's quarterly credit fee per million, next assessed by 15 November, from the sources in P3. The August release already says portfolio trading has lower fees; these observations are within two quarters, so Rule 4 does not impose an additional haircut. T1 has no separately attributable adoption series for TW: it is a possible cause of the same observable pricing pressure, not a claimed measured tailwind.

Secondary risks include LSEG control, investment gains obscuring ordinary earnings, and a weakly observed return on the acquired asset base. Missing ROIC and gross-profit productivity remain missing. A trading network may support margins through counterparty access and integrations, but this is a hypothesis to keep testing, not a guarantee that today's margin persists.

Combined exposure: TW is absent from the human holdings, so existing direct weight is 0%. This adds US exposure to a human book already 66.69% US, though it adds a different business from the four large technology positions. Sources: holdings, Scan book.

Findings that changed the judgement

TW: earnings gains are real, their repeatability is not. The Scan has no oneOff annotation on TW, but the FY2025 issuer reconciliation identifies Canton Coin gains. Its ordinary operating-income line is lower than local opinc; the local field includes a separate tax-receivable adjustment. Current local vendor EPS stays close to reported EPS and cannot be treated as a certified removal. The proposal compares an approximately 27.04× issuer-adjusted TTM with local 24.46× reported / 24.51× vendor, without transplanting a percentile across bases. The business earns its small order through execution economics, not the crypto uplift. MarketAxess's own fee decline also makes competition a concrete observable rather than a token paragraph.

MWA: a stronger capital test, not a retrospective sell rule. The Review's annual classification finding is independently confirmed in the annual statement. The new P3 has standalone cash, asset-return and margin breaks. It cannot stay green merely because price increases hold up revenue. The existing accepted tranche keeps its original conditions; a future tranche-specific sell may therefore differ from a verdict on the original shares.

LULU: the saved adjustment is assigned to the wrong fiscal year and its description understates the components. The quarterly filing places $134.5m of tariff refunds in cost of sales and $4.1m of related interest in other income in the quarter ended 2 August 2026. The store instead subtracts $134.5m from the annual row ending 2026-01-31, and describes it as including interest. Therefore this run does not rely on LULU's own-basis percentile as certified. The amounts are before tax, not automatically an after-tax net-income adjustment. Independently of that error, current company results show Americas comparable sales down 12% and Q3 sales guidance down 10–11%; the refusal is about declining customer demand, not incomplete data.

RELX and INTU: name what could explain the discount. T2 attacks their customer/workflow pricing, while T1 can lower competitors' input cost. RELX's reported 19.89× is about 41.7% below its local 34.1008× median; INTU's 19.01× is about 69.0% below its local 61.3044× median. These are reported-basis comparisons with the spans in the table, not target prices. RELX's current results describe growing AI-enabled products, but that does not isolate retained users from price and mix. Intuit's release discloses falling US TurboTax units. I have not established that the discounts are wrong, so neither gets a buy justified merely by cheapness. This is an evidence-based wait on the business mechanism, not a permanent exclusion of software.

Venue checks do not delete a business. RMS.PA's one share costs about £1,213.10, above available cash. A scan of local primary mappings finds no alternative for Hermès; the depositary identifies HESAY, but it has no local quote/EPS/bands and cannot receive an order under §7.2. No invented price or ADR fee is used. XIACY is the locally covered alternative to 1810.HK, and BYDDY to 1211.HK. They are judged on earnings quality below, not rejected on an assumed Hong Kong board lot. No non-US ticket is proposed; unknown lot and broker costs are not labelled as verified passes.

Excluded watchlist entries

These 63 entries were screened from local data without fetching company filings. Percentiles below are quoted with their reported-window span, solely to explain the failed filter. Missing operating-company P/E bands fail local coverage. Funds and the VIX are not being forced through an operating-company earnings test; no separate fund purchase case arose in the Sweep and there is no standing-order instruction.

__EXCLUDED_LIST__

Data and instruction audit

  • The brief's final rule is “Write only pot/proposals/…. Touch nothing else.” Its earlier requests to append adjustments and wishlist items conflict with that boundary. This run follows the narrow write scope: the findings and outstanding records are preserved here, not claimed as applied to pot/adjustments.json or pot/data-wishlist.md. No design rule was changed, so there is no new pot-design decision to record.
  • MWA pending record: one-time tax benefit, amountPerShare: 0.06, USD, FY ending 2026-09-30, sourced to its Q3 release. That annual row is not yet present; tariff refunds need separate quantification. Do not attach this to FY2025 to make it match an existing row.
  • TW pending reconciliation: FY2025 investment gains need their attributable after-tax effect before insertion into a net-income adjustment store. No invented tax rate or minority allocation is used. Correct opinc classification separately from recurring-EPS adjustments.
  • LULU pending correction: preserve the old entry's audit trail, reverse the wrong-period adjustment through a supported correction, and associate only correctly reconciled after-tax amounts with the actual fiscal year. Simply appending another positive adjustment would double-count rather than repair it. The present data model and the proposals-only scope do not permit claiming that correction was completed here.
  • Wishlist records retained here: matched TW monthly fee/share history with FINRA denominators; issuer-attributable gains for TW; quantified MWA refund and average-assets history; HESAY local coverage and actual venue costs; matched-country/year Netflix viewing observations; paid-user/retention data for RELX and INTU. No unsupported number replaces a gap.
  • RSGN's quote starts 2023-12-15, after its de-SPAC; its 144 weeks are indicative. No newly discovered pre-business price contamination is asserted. GME's 129 and PLTR's 150 positive-earnings observations likewise do not establish a full-cycle distribution. Zero or negative earnings, including 0823.HK's negative current EPS despite a zero stored percentile, are not a cheap P/E.
  • The broader book contains the three tagged MWA shares. The MWA proposal separates them from untagged human exposure, avoiding double-counting. Other overlap is disclosure, never a ranking penalty. The two proposed names do increase exposure to an already US-heavy book.
  • Source hierarchy followed: local market/account data, company/regulator filings, broker schedules and HMRC. Filings were fetched for specific shortlist decisions and discrepancies, not for all 79 names. No prohibited aggregator is used as a factual source. No older unexecuted proposal was used as a reason to suppress a current decision.

Only this report and its two linked proposals are this run's deliverables. The market files already had unrelated changes; they were not edited or regenerated by this run.

MWA — Mueller Water Products

What it does: Mueller supplies valves, hydrants, meters and related equipment for water systems, mainly in North America. Utilities and distributors buy the equipment to build, maintain and measure water networks. Company release.

Decision dated 11 September 2026. This run's ranking and allocation. This is a new top-up thesis; it does not retrospectively replace the accepted three-share position's falsifier or its latest Review verdict.

1. Order

BUY 5 additional shares of MWA on NYSE, limit $23.70, through Trading 212 Invest/ISA, regular session 11 September 2026, cancelling at the close if unfilled. The pot would hold 8 shares.

At USD-per-GBP 1.3507, deploy at most £87.73, plus approximately £0.13 FX, total £87.86. Normal incremental headroom is £250 minus the current three-share mark of £52.62 = £197.38. §7.2a halves that to a £98.69 allocation because unquantified tariff benefits and operating-income classification weaken the apparent earnings quality. Unused allocation after fees: £10.83. Cash becomes £359.36 if this alone fills, or £283.36 if TW also fills.

At the limit, eight shares represent 28.07% of £500 contributed, comfortably below 50%. No one-share or fee exception is used. A sixth additional share would put this ticket above the reduced allocation, without reducing the percentage fee. The £98.69 all-in budget remains binding if FX changes.

TW, a fresh name of comparable merit, receives its allocation first under §4.5a. This smaller top-up follows because the other fresh candidates do not yet offer the same combination of an understandable business and dated evidence to test it. It does not take MWA to the cap. The 10 September Review holds the existing three shares and identifies weak capital-return coverage in their original break; P3 below directly addresses that concern for the proposed new shares.

Expected first-year buy-and-hold costs: £0 commission, 0.15% FX, £0 custody, no ADR fee, approximately 0.15% of the ticket. Transaction tax is £0 for the US share purchase. Dividend withholding is separate tax on income. Spread is unmeasured but the limit caps the share price; no future sale is assumed. Both cost gates clear. Sources: MWA availability, fees, FX, HMRC, local prices, book.

2. Thesis

Water-network replacement gives Mueller a recurring physical use case, while expanded foundries create an opportunity to earn more from the existing product and distribution base. The filed FY2023–25 operating margin improved from 9.99% to 13.82% to 18.23% as sales rose, so the business case has evidence across several years rather than one unusually strong quarter. The proposed return comes from converting that operating improvement into cash on the factory investment; the market may be giving too little credit to that conversion, but the newest quarter's price-led sales and exceptional benefits make it a testable opportunity at reduced size, not a completed success.

Why this is not 7532.T again: essential infrastructure is the starting observation, not the buy argument. The corrected margin series, explicit capital and cash denominators, half allocation and standalone cash break prevent the water-spending story from standing in for earnings quality. Compatibility with installed equipment and utility qualification could support persistence; they do not establish an unassailable margin.

3. Falsifier

These are new-share decision thresholds, except the 70% cash-conversion reference, which is management's stated full-year expectation. They do not amend the conditions already attached to the accepted trade.

Warning: At FY2026 results, locally estimated for 5 November, review by 10 November 2026 if consolidated volumes decline again, or FY free cash flow divided by company-reconciled adjusted net income is 70% or less. Also warn if the consistently defined asset-return measure below is below 10%. A volume bridge's explicit direction is usable; undisclosed volume is unavailable evidence. Use GAAP operating income after restructuring and impairments.

Define the asset-return check as trailing-four-quarter GAAP operating income × 0.75 / average of opening and closing total assets. The 25% tax factor is a deliberately fixed analytical assumption, not a claimed tax rate. This is an after-tax operating return on assets, not ROIC; do not substitute the local ROIC series or a changing tax rate. It gives factory investment a denominator that margin alone lacks. Calculate and record the FY baseline at the November review.

Break: Sell the proposed five-share tranche under §5.1 if any one of the following occurs: (a) FY2026 free cash flow is below 50% of reconciled adjusted net income; (b) the asset-return measure is below 8% at both 30 September and 31 December 2026; or (c) filed GAAP operating margin is below 18% in both post-entry quarters. Assess September at FY results and December at Q1 FY2027, no later than 28 February 2027. None of these requires volumes also to fall: pricing cannot keep a failing capital/cash test green. The 10%/8% thresholds deliberately separate warning from break; they are analyst choices, not historical local ROIC comparisons. Missing accounts prompt an urgent re-read, not a fabricated ratio.

4. Review date

10 November 2026, regardless of price. The local 5 November results date is an estimate. Final two-quarter assessment by 28 February 2027, a review deadline rather than an announced result date.

5. Numbers as of today

The price snapshot was fetched 11 September, 12:45:43 UTC and uses the prior US regular close. Figures are not intraday execution quotes.

Local check: disagreement. The local annual operating-income series is $137.6m / $213.8m / $269.4m, and local Q3 is $91.8m. Those overstate filed operating income by omitting charges. Use the filing's lower figures above. Revenue, net income and annual EPS reconcile; refreshed market EPS does not repair the operating-income classification. The current $1.40 EPS also differs from the $1.42 snapshot quoted in the prior Review; today's calculation uses $1.40.

Adjustments: The Q3 release identifies a one-time tax benefit of $0.06 per adjusted diluted share, belonging to FY ending 2026-09-30, which is not yet an annual row in earnings.json. Tariff refunds are mentioned but not separately quantified there. No clean full adjustment can be written against the current annual store, and zero MWA years carry cited adjustments. A tax-only sensitivity is $23.69 / ($1.40 − $0.06) = 17.68×; it remains incomplete and does not certify a percentile. The half allocation prices that uncertainty. The run report preserves the finding without breaching the proposals-only write boundary.

6. The case against

Theses: none.

Dominant risk (financial): Expanded factories absorb capital while pricing and exceptional benefits make the income statement look stronger than the underlying cash return.

Earliest observable: FY2026 cash conversion and assets in the November annual release, followed by December-quarter accounts by February 2027. These are within two quarters; Rule 4 adds no separate reduction. P3 can break on poor cash conversion or declining asset returns while sales and margins still look healthy.

The latest issuer release attributes part of the improvement to prices and refunds while consolidated volumes were lower. There is no assurance that utility spending fills the capacity economically, and today’s local ROIC cannot be treated as a clean filed return. Adding to a recently bought holding increases the consequence of being wrong before any post-entry results exist; the limited top-up is a choice, not a reward for a one-day price move.

Combined exposure: The only three MWA shares in holdings are tagged to this pot. At the local price and FX, they are roughly 0.041% of the £127,791 aggregate book in signals; untagged human-book MWA exposure is 0%. The top-up adds to that small combined position, not a large existing company exposure, while increasing US exposure to a book already 66.69% US. The aggregate book includes the tagged shares, so do not add the original three twice.

TW — Tradeweb Markets

What it does: Tradeweb operates electronic markets where banks, asset managers and other institutions trade bonds, derivatives and other financial instruments. It earns transaction fees, subscription fees and revenue from market data. Business description.

Run report and full ranking. Prepared 11 September 2026; local snapshot 05:39:51 UTC.

1. Order

BUY 1 share of TW on NASDAQ through Trading 212, limit $102.47, regular session only, day order for 11 September 2026. Currency USD. At local FX of $1.3513 per £1, deploy £75.83 of a £125 allocation; £49.17 of that allocation remains before fees. Do not chase an unfilled order.

The normal maximum allocation is £250, half of £500 contributed. Halve it to £125 under §7.2a: the quoted historical distributions have not been cleansed of Canton Coin gains. This is a purchase despite disclosed uncertainty, not a claim that the vendor's “recurring” earnings are certified. One share fits that reduced allocation normally; no one-share exception is used. Two shares would cost £151.66 before fees and exceed it. The resulting position is 15.17% of contributed capital.

Trading 212 lists TW. Expected costs under its Invest/ISA schedule: £0 commission, £0 custody, £0.11 FX at 0.15%, no ADR custody. Purchase transaction tax: £0 on this US common share. Allow £0.01 for dividend conversion if applicable: approximately £0.12 first-year costs, 0.16% of the ticket before any future sale. Entry broker fees are 0.15%, below §4.1a's 0.5%; first-year costs clear §4.1's 2%. Market spread is not known before placement; the limit caps the purchase price. More shares would not reduce the percentage fee.

Cash after this order alone, including entry FX: £371.30. With the companion five-share MWA order, cash remains £283.51, at these limits and FX. This fresh position receives the first allocation under §4.5a; MWA is considered afterwards. Sources: positions, prices, companion order.

2. Thesis

Tradeweb earns from transactions moving into electronic execution, with established connections between institutional customers and dealers giving it a route to more activity without building an equivalent physical asset base. Revenue grew 18.9% in FY2025, while filed operating margin rose from 39.28% to 40.70%; Q2 2026 revenue still grew 9.0% and filed operating margin reached 43.88% (annual release, Q2 release). The reported multiple is 55.7% below its stored historical median (P5), a discount that could price both unreliable crypto earnings and T1/T2-driven fee compression; my provisional reason to disagree with permanent deterioration is that Q2 credit revenue still grew 3.3% and August fully electronic high-grade share remained 19.0%, evidence for a small operating-growth position whose persistence P3 must test, not proof that the risk has disappeared (August activity).

3. Falsifier

These are decision thresholds, not management guidance. They test customer capture and monetisation directly; strong group revenue cannot overrule a break.

Warning: Review September's activity release by 9 October 2026. A fully electronic US high-grade TRACE share below 18.0%, against August's 19.0%, triggers a re-read. Also trigger a warning at Q3 results, locally dated 29 October, if cash-credit fees per million fall more than 15% year over year, or quarterly total credit revenue falls year over year. The current Q2 fee decline is already 11.4%; the warning asks whether that deterioration worsens. August baseline, fee definitions and Q2 baseline.

Break: By the 28 February 2027 review, either (a) fully electronic high-grade share below 17.0% in three consecutive post-entry monthly releases, or (b) total credit revenue declining year over year in both Q3 and Q4 2026 while total credit ADV is flat or growing in each, calls for an exit under §5.1. Route (a) catches lost customers; route (b) catches structurally weaker monetisation even when more notional is traded. For (a), do not substitute total TRACE share; for (b), use the matching total-credit revenue and ADV definitions, including derivatives. If definitions change, require a comparable restatement; missing publication triggers review rather than a fabricated pass.

External cross-check: MarketAxess's Q2 release reports portfolio-trading ADV up 33% to $2.0bn, even though its overall high-grade ADV fell 4%. Track its same-protocol ADV in quarterly results against Tradeweb's corresponding growth, without treating differently defined market shares as additive. MarketAxess has suspended monthly volume releases following the announced ICE transaction, so monthly competitor reporting is not a promised observable. Check its next quarterly filing by 15 November 2026, a review deadline rather than a confirmed release date. This comparison tests whether the low-fee protocol shift is market-wide or Tradeweb is also losing customer flow.

4. Review date

9 October 2026, regardless of price, then 30 October 2026 after expected Q3 results. Revisit the business and earnings basis; do not renew this order automatically.

5. Numbers as of today

Local check: agree on Q2 revenue, operating income, attributable net income and EPS; disagree on historical operating classification and recurring earnings. Local FY2025 opinc is $845.124m; the issuer's operating line is $835.338m. The $9.786m difference is tax-receivable-agreement income below operations. FY2024 has the same issue: $685.758m locally versus $678.028m filed. Use the filed values for the historical margin argument. Local FY2025 net income of $812.792m is attributable income, correctly different from $921.5m consolidated income before non-controlling interests.

The issuer reports FY2025 Canton Coin gains of $270.9m, including $205.4m in Q4, whereas local FY2025 norm equals ni. The Scan has no oneOff flag on TW today; that does not establish clean earnings. Issuer-adjusted EPS removes investment gains but also adds back expenses and assumes exchange of LLC interests; 27.04× is a disclosed alternative basis, not clean GAAP EPS and not a recalculated percentile. The historical gate is provisionally met on the two stored bases; §7.2a halves the size because those bases do not settle it.

Adjustments: No net-income adjustment appended. The gains above are consolidated pre-tax amounts; an attributable after-tax Canton amount or standalone per-share impact was not established. Subtracting $270.9m directly from attributable net income, or recording the entire GAAP-to-adjusted EPS difference as Canton income, would mix bases. Zero TW fiscal years carry cited own-basis adjustments in the store. This uncertainty is material and determines P1's half allocation. The brief's final write boundary restricts this run to proposals; the reconciliation and missing fields are retained here for the pipeline owner.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: electronic trading growth is the lead, but the order rests on filed operating margins after removing the tax classification error. Low-fee volume growth and competitive share losses have explicit tests, while absent capital-return measures remain absent. A currency conversion for sizing does not convert company earnings or certify their quality.

6. The case against

Theses: T2 bears on institutional trading workflows as a potential change in how clients execute; Tradeweb primarily charges for transactions rather than user seats. T1 bears indirectly through cheaper automation for customers and rivals. Neither establishes that Tradeweb keeps the resulting economics.

Dominant risk (competitive): competing execution channels and lower-fee protocols capture the economics of growing electronic volumes, leaving Tradeweb with weaker customer share or lower revenue per trade.

Earliest observable: September's monthly high-grade share and Q3 total-credit revenue/ADV plus the cash-credit fee table, reviewed on 9 and 30 October; the source and thresholds are in P3. MarketAxess's quarterly protocol data supplies the outside comparison. These are within two quarters, so Rule 4 does not independently require another reduction.

A high margin can attract cheaper substitutes; existing connections are a reason to investigate persistence, not proof of it. MarketAxess's portfolio-trading growth and the announced ICE deal strengthen that objection. T1/T2 could enlarge volumes while reducing what each venue collects, exactly the combination P3(b) tests. The current data do not show that every protocol shares one economic model.

Secondary risks are non-operating crypto volatility, the related-party data relationship with LSEG, acquisition accounting and USD/GBP movement. A low relative multiple may partly price a different earnings mix rather than undervalued execution profits.

Combined exposure: no TW holding appears in holdings, so existing direct human-book weight is 0%. This adds US-listed equity to the dashboard book already 66.76% US in signals, although its revenue driver differs from the large technology holdings. That geography measure includes the tagged MWA pot trade; it is not a separately recomputed human-only weight. Overlap is disclosed, not used to downgrade the rank.

Use the unrounded arithmetic for the aggregate: £447.24 − ($102.47 + 5 × $23.69) / 1.3513 × 1.0015 = £283.5078. Display rounding can differ by a penny. The two tickets deploy £163.49 before fees. TW ends at 15.17% of contributed capital; all eight MWA shares at 28.05%. No borrowing, one-share cap exception or fee-driven cap exception is used. Dates, session restrictions, per-order cash and first-year costs are in P1 of each proposal.

The remaining cash was considered. A second TW share exceeds its £125 reduced allocation; a sixth additional MWA share exceeds its £98.70 reduced allocation. Cheap percentage fees do not permit enlarging either allocation. The next candidates require a business outcome: NVO must show that volume survives price pressure in profits, R&S must deliver the second-half recovery, and Netflix must support monetisation with observable engagement. INTU/RELX/Wiley discounts could be the standing AI theses being priced, while LULU's operating direction is worsening. This is why a third proposal is not forced. It is not because older drafts exist, or because an imperfect earnings history automatically prohibits buying.

Reconciliations that change how to read the screen

  • TW: the Scan has no oneOff annotation, but FY2025 vendor norm equals filed attributable income despite issuer-disclosed Canton gains. The filing puts FY2025 operating income at $835.338m rather than local $845.124m, a $9.786m tax-agreement reclassification. Filed FY2024/FY2025 operating margins are 39.28%/40.70%, versus the higher stored series. The proposal uses filed margins and a 27.04× issuer-adjusted trailing sensitivity alongside the 24.57× quote multiple; this does not reconstruct a clean historical percentile. Zero years have own adjustments. Reconciliation.
  • MWA: the Review's corrections are independently supported by the annual and quarterly filings. Filed operating margin improved to 18.23% in FY2025, not the local 18.84%. The quarter's reported operating income is $80.6m, not $91.8m. The $0.06 tax benefit belongs to FY2026, whose annual end has not yet landed in the local earnings series; no adjustment is attached to FY2025. Cash and gross-profit/assets now have independent break tests, so healthy sales or price increases cannot keep them green. Reconciliation.
  • LULU: the existing own-basis entry attaches $134.5m to 2026-01-31, but the September Q2 release puts the refund in the quarter ended 2 August 2026, after that annual end. It also distinguishes $134.5m refunds, $4.1m associated interest and $0.86 per share net-of-tax impact. The stored item is therefore not evidence that the January annual net income contained that gain. Do not trust its own-basis zero percentile as a certified correction. The operating deterioration still independently supports EXCLUDE. No existing adjustment was edited or deleted.
  • INTU: local annual history ends July 2025, while the August issuer release reports FY2026 revenue $21.4bn, GAAP operating income $5.9bn and EPS $16.46. The quote has EPS $16.39, giving 19.08× versus 19.00× using the filed annual EPS. That small discrepancy does not cause rejection; declining TurboTax units and the unrebutted T2 discount do. Local capital measures are explicitly FY2025. The release identifies $143m prior-year excess stock-compensation tax benefits: not inserted into an adjusted history in this run.
  • NVO: the primary release's adjusted H1 sales are DKK148.551bn versus reported DKK175.311bn, reflecting the 340B provision reversal; Q2 adjusted operating profit also excludes impairments. Stored vendor P/E is not proof all those effects are removed. Half sizing would be available under §7.2a; the current WAIT is about volume-to-profit economics, not an invented all-years-certification gate.
  • Short windows: R&S has 144 weeks from 2023-12-15, after the operating company's listing date stated by the issuer. AMSC, GME, PLTR and XIACY also have short usable windows; none is described as five full years of operating valuation evidence. No newly proven pre-business-price contamination was found in the shortlisted names.

Execution and data gaps retained in this report

The brief both asks for adjustment/wishlist updates and ends with "Write only pot/proposals/… Touch nothing else." This run follows that final boundary. Reconciliations and gaps are recorded here and in P5; no claim is made that the adjustment store or wishlist was updated. There is no implementation or policy change requiring a design-log amendment.

Hermès is the concrete alternate-listing check. The local RMS.PA share costs £1211.30, above £447.24 cash. No quote has RMS.PA as its primary. Nevertheless, T212's HESAY instrument page establishes an OTC alternative. Its price was not adopted from the broker: HESAY has no local price, EPS or bands. A future coverage addition must verify receipt ratio, ADR custody/distribution fees and liquidity, then cost both venues; no invented £0 ADR custody and no claim that Hermès is inherently unbuyable. Paris tax/commission and the OTC first-year total were not established, so this is an uncosted alternative, not a third ticket.

No other name was rejected on an assumed board lot or an assumed IBKR minimum. R&S and Asian candidates received business decisions first; if advanced, source their actual lot and venue fee schedules, check other listings, and cost the ticket before changing WAIT to PROPOSE. Lot sizes are absent locally and have not been inferred as one share. HESAY coverage, TW attributable after-tax investment gains, the future MWA annual adjustment, and the misdated LULU entry are the concrete follow-up items.

Verification

The proposals name P1×P6, whole shares, source-backed broker availability/costs, dated two-tier falsifiers, the applicable standing theses, and combined-book exposure. The count check covers all 79 watchlist entries exactly once across the two watchlist tiers. All 26 Scan valuation tickers are covered by the 17 detailed watchlist rows or 11 additional rows (the two extra watchlist rows are recurring-only Xiaomi and negative-EPS Link). Local prices and the cash calculation use one snapshot. Source disagreements are stated; no external quote replaced a local price. Only this ranking and its two linked proposals were written.

MWA — Mueller Water Products

What it does: Mueller manufactures valves, hydrants, meters and equipment used to move and measure water. Utilities, municipalities and other customers buy its products for water networks and construction projects. Company description.

Run report and full ranking. Prepared 11 September 2026; local snapshot 05:39:51 UTC. This is a new top-up proposal; it does not retroactively change the accepted three-share thesis.

1. Order

BUY 5 additional shares of MWA on NYSE through Trading 212, limit $23.69, regular session only, day order for 11 September 2026. Currency USD. At $1.3513 per £1, deploy £87.66 of a £98.70 allocation, leaving £11.05 of that allocation idle before fees. Do not chase an unfilled order.

Positions records three shares and £500 contributed. Their current mark is £52.59, leaving £197.41 below the £250 maximum. Halve that incremental allocation to £98.70 under §7.2a, because the tariff refund is not fully isolated and the historical operating-profit field overstates filed operating income. Five shares fit normally. Six would cost £105.19 and exceed this reduced allocation. Eight shares after execution would be worth £140.25, or 28.05% of contributions; no cap exception applies.

Trading 212 lists MWA, and the original purchase is recorded as T212 in holdings. Its fee schedule gives £0 commission, £0 custody and £0.13 entry FX, 0.15%. No ADR fee. Purchase transaction tax: £0 for this US common share. Allow £0.01 for dividend conversion if applicable: approximately £0.14 first-year costs, 0.16% of the ticket before any future sale. This clears both cost gates. Market spread is unknown before placement; the limit controls price. There is no flat commission to dilute with more shares.

The fresh TW name receives the first allocation. MWA then earns a smaller top-up: its equipment business has a clearer operating improvement than the unit-sensitive software discounts or the consumer turnarounds below it. NVO's forward earnings decline, R&S's delivery-dependent second half, and NFLX's weaker visibility into engagement are reasons to keep residual cash, not reasons to fill MWA to the maximum. See the linked ranking for every alternative. Cash after MWA alone including entry FX: £359.45; after both proposed orders: £283.51.

2. Thesis

Mueller sells physical equipment needed to operate and renew water networks, with an opportunity to earn more from its installed manufacturing capacity and product mix. Filed operating margin improved from 9.99% in FY2023 to 13.82% in FY2024 and 18.23% in FY2025, on revenue of $1.276bn, $1.315bn and $1.430bn (annual filing). My inference is that some of this improvement can persist beyond a construction slowdown, making a limited addition worthwhile, but the order does not assume that price increases prove demand or that booked profit proves a satisfactory return on the factories.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At FY2026 results, locally estimated for 5 November 2026, trigger a re-read if consolidated physical volume declines again, if full-year free cash flow / company-reconciled adjusted net income is 70% or less, or if gross profit / year-end total assets falls below 26%. Management's cash-conversion commitment is above 70%; the asset-productivity threshold is my early-warning level against the local FY2025 baseline of 28.10%. Volumes can be checked from the explicit direction in the issuer's sales bridge; absent disclosure is not a pass. Q3 release and reconciliation, capital baseline.

Break: Assess FY2026 and then the trailing year ending December 2026, by 28 February 2027. Any one of these is enough to call for exit of this proposed tranche under §5.1:

  • FCF / company-reconciled adjusted net income is below 60% at both reporting dates. FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditures; construct the December trailing year as FY2026 plus the new December quarter less its year-ago quarter. Require positive adjusted net income; non-positive trailing adjusted income with non-positive FCF is itself a break.
  • Gross profit / closing total assets is below 24% at both reporting dates, using the same trailing-year flow and period-end asset convention as the baseline. Do not substitute operating margin or annualise one quarter.
  • GAAP operating margin is below 18% in each of the September and December post-entry quarters, independently of whether volumes decline.

The 60%, 24% and 18% thresholds are my judgement, not company guidance. These independent routes address the Review's objection: price can hide lost volumes and accounting margin can hide capital tied up in inventory. A missing reconciliation triggers review, not a zero or an assumed pass. Newly disclosed refunds must be identified beside both cash and income; if their after-tax treatment cannot be reconciled, an apparent ratio pass remains uncertified and further additions stop pending review.

4. Review date

10 November 2026, regardless of price. Then 28 February 2027 for the two-report break tests. November's results date is a local estimate, and February is a review deadline, not an announced release date. The two-day Review lane can investigate intervening evidence sooner.

The first observation is within two quarters, so Rule 4 adds no separate reduction.

The latest volume direction is already negative; infrastructure need is not an order book. Cash conversion through nine months is below the annual commitment, and inventory absorbs money before a sale. Customers can delay work and higher prices can invite substitution. These facts argue against extrapolating the peak margin or assuming new factories automatically earn the old return. A half allocation also limits the cost of discovering the tariff benefit was more material than the release made separable.

Combined exposure: holdings.json contains only the three MWA shares tagged to the pot, and positions.json accounts for all three. Eight pot shares would be about £140.25; this adds to a US allocation already 66.76% in the Scan's book. TW — Tradeweb Markets

What it does: Tradeweb operates electronic markets where banks, investment managers and other institutions trade bonds and other financial instruments. It earns transaction fees and sells market data and related services. Business description.

Research dated 10 September 2026. Run report and complete ranking.

1. Order

BUY 1 share of TW on Nasdaq, limit $102.47, regular session only. Use Trading 212 Invest or Stocks ISA, where the cash equity is listed. Day order for 11 September 2026; an unfilled order expires, without chasing.

Currency USD. At local GBP/USD 1.3509, deploy £75.85 of a £125 allocation. The normal £250 ceiling is halved under §7.2a because the historical earnings base is not certified against the Canton gains. This is not the one-share exception: one share fits the reduced allocation. It uses 60.68% of that allocation and leaves £49.15 before fees, £49.03 after fees.

Broker schedule. Both the under-0.5% broker gate and 2% first-year gate pass. These are entry/holding charges, not an assumed sale within the year or a dividend-tax estimate. A limit controls the purchase price; the bid/ask spread is not separately measured. Recalculate GBP costs if FX changes.

Two shares would cost £151.71 before fees and exceed the reduced allocation; commission is zero, so buying more would not improve percentage fee drag. Exposure is 15.17% of £500 contributed, with no cap breach. Starting cash is £447.24; this order alone leaves £371.27, or £283.46 if the companion five-share MWA top-up also fills at its limit. Sources: prices, positions, arithmetic at the stated limits.

2. Thesis

Tradeweb monetises institutions moving trading and execution onto electronic networks, with distribution and transaction activity supporting a business beyond the sale of software seats. Revenue grew 18.9% in FY2025 and 9.0% in Q2 2026, while filed operating margins improved, so the case rests on profitable execution activity rather than a Canton Coin revaluation. My inference is that the market is discounting a lasting slowdown in monetisation, whereas continuing client activity offers an opportunity to grow transaction earnings; the durability of that opportunity against a stronger competitor remains the test below. Annual report, Q2 release.

3. Falsifier

Warning: Re-read at the first monthly report after entry if fully electronic US high-grade TRACE share falls below 18.0%, versus 19.0% in August, or at Q3 results if credit revenue declines year on year despite positive credit cash ADV growth. The first tests lost execution activity; the second tests monetisation that total notional volume can conceal. September's monthly release is expected in early October from the observed monthly cadence; check by 9 October 2026, then on 29 October. Thresholds are my decision rules, not management guidance. August baseline, confirmed Q3 date.

Break: Exit under §5.1 if the same fully electronic high-grade share is below 17.0% in three consecutive post-entry monthly observations, or credit revenue falls year on year in both Q3 and Q4 2026 while credit cash ADV grows in both quarters. The share test can break by the November activity report, checked by 10 December 2026; assess the revenue test by 28 February 2027, a review deadline rather than an announced Q4 date. These are independent break paths: strong group earnings do not excuse losing share or giving away credit execution.

Cross-check the competitive explanation against MarketAxess's quarterly credit fee per million and portfolio-trading ADV: Q2 baselines were $129 and $2.0bn, respectively. Its next quarterly release is expected in the autumn, checked by 15 November. The competitor's own disclosure is the external source; its adoption alone does not trigger a sale. Definitions and mix matter, and share denominators must remain comparable. If releases disappear or TRACE methodology changes, record unavailable evidence and re-review rather than treating missing observations as a pass. MarketAxess Q2.

4. Review date

9 October 2026, regardless of price, then 30 October 2026 after confirmed Q3 results. Rule 4's timing does not independently require a smaller order: the share observable is monthly. §7.2a already halves the allocation.

5. Numbers as of today

Local snapshot: 20:35:57 UTC, 10 September; TW regular price struck 20:00:00 UTC. Extended-hours data is excluded.
